verses.sanskrit: ॐ ऐं मार्कण्डेय उवाच
verses.transliteration: OM aiM mArkaNDeya uvAcha
verses.translation: Om! Reverence to Chandika. Markandeya spoke:
verses.wordMeaning: Om! Reverence to Chandika. Markandeya spoke:

verses.sanskrit: सावर्णिः सूर्यतनयो यो मनुः कथ्यतेऽष्टमः । निशामय तदुत्पत्तिं विस्तराद्गदतो मम
verses.transliteration: sAvarNiH sUryatanayo yo manuH kathyate.aShTamaH | nishAmaya tadutpattiM vistarAdgadato mama
verses.translation: Surya's son Savarni is he who is called the eighth Manu. Hear about his birth, as I tell it at full length,
verses.wordMeaning: Surya's son Savarni is he who is called the eighth Manu. Hear about his birth, as I tell it at full length,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Surya's son Savarni is he who is called the eighth Manu. Hear about his birth, as I tell it at full length,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Surya's son Savarni is he who is called the eighth Manu. Hear about his birth, as I tell it at full length,

verses.sanskrit: महामायानुभावेन यथा मन्वन्तराधिपः । स बभूव महाभागः सावर्णिस्तनयो रवेः
verses.transliteration: mahAmAyAnubhAvena yathA manvantarAdhipaH | sa babhUva mahAbhAgaH sAvarNistanayo raveH
verses.translation: how by reason of the authority of the Great Illusion that illustrious son of the Sun, Savarni, became the king of the eighth manvantara.
verses.wordMeaning: how by reason of the authority of the Great Illusion that illustrious son of the Sun, Savarni, became the king of the eighth manvantara.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): how by reason of the authority of the Great Illusion that illustrious son of the Sun, Savarni, became the king of the eighth manvantara.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): how by reason of the authority of the Great Illusion that illustrious son of the Sun, Savarni, became the king of the eighth manvantara.

verses.sanskrit: स्वारोचिषेऽन्तरे पूर्वं चैत्रवंशसमुद्भवः । सुरथो नाम राजाभूत्समस्ते क्षितिमण्डले
verses.transliteration: svArochiShe.antare pUrvaM chaitravaMshasamudbhavaH | suratho nAma rAjAbhUtsamaste kShitimaNDale
verses.translation: In times ago in the Svarochisha period, a king named Suratha, sprung of the race of Chaitra, reigned over the whole earth.
verses.wordMeaning: In times ago in the Svarochisha period, a king named Suratha, sprung of the race of Chaitra, reigned over the whole earth.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): In times ago in the Svarochisha period, a king named Suratha, sprung of the race of Chaitra, reigned over the whole earth.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): In times ago in the Svarochisha period, a king named Suratha, sprung of the race of Chaitra, reigned over the whole earth.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य पालयतः सम्यक् प्रजाः पुत्रानिवौरसान् । बभूवुः शत्रवो भूपाः कोलाविध्वंसिनस्तदा
verses.transliteration: tasya pAlayataH samyak prajAH putrAnivaurasAn | babhUvuH shatravo bhUpAH kolAvidhvaMsinastadA
verses.translation: And while he guarded his subjects duly as if they were his own children, there arose hostile kings, who did not destroy the Kolas.
verses.wordMeaning: And while he guarded his subjects duly as if they were his own children, there arose hostile kings, who did not destroy the Kolas.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And while he guarded his subjects duly as if they were his own children, there arose hostile kings, who did not destroy the Kolas.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And while he guarded his subjects duly as if they were his own children, there arose hostile kings, who did not destroy the Kolas.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य तैरभवद् युद्धमतिप्रबलदण्डिनः । न्यूनैरपि स तैर्युद्धे कोलाविध्वंसिभिर्जितः
verses.transliteration: tasya tairabhavad yuddhamatiprabaladaNDinaH | nyUnairapi sa tairyuddhe kolAvidhvaMsibhirjitaH
verses.translation: He, the bearer of a very powerful sceptre, had war with them, and was defeated in war by them, inferior though they were, those non-destroyers of the Kolas.
verses.wordMeaning: He, the bearer of a very powerful sceptre, had war with them, and was defeated in war by them, inferior though they were, those non-destroyers of the Kolas.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): He, the bearer of a very powerful sceptre, had war with them, and was defeated in war by them, inferior though they were, those non-destroyers of the Kolas.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): He, the bearer of a very powerful sceptre, had war with them, and was defeated in war by them, inferior though they were, those non-destroyers of the Kolas.

verses.sanskrit: ततः स्वपुरमायातो निजदेशाधिपोऽभवत् । आक्रान्तः स महाभागस्तैस्तदा प्रबलारिभिः
verses.transliteration: tataH svapuramAyAto nijadeshAdhipo.abhavat | AkrAntaH sa mahAbhAgastaistadA prabalAribhiH
verses.translation: Then coming to his own city he reigned as king over his own country. That illustrious king was attacked then by those powerful enemies.
verses.wordMeaning: Then coming to his own city he reigned as king over his own country. That illustrious king was attacked then by those powerful enemies.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then coming to his own city he reigned as king over his own country. That illustrious king was attacked then by those powerful enemies.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then coming to his own city he reigned as king over his own country. That illustrious king was attacked then by those powerful enemies.

verses.sanskrit: अमात्यैर्बलिभिर्दुष्टैर्दुर्बलस्य दुरात्मभिः । कोशो बलं चापहृतं तत्रापि स्वपुरे ततः
verses.transliteration: amAtyairbalibhirduShTairdurbalasya durAtmabhiH | kosho balaM chApahR^itaM tatrApi svapure tataH
verses.translation: His powerful and corrupt ministers, who were evil-disposed to a weak person, thereupon robbed him of treasury and army even there in his own city.
verses.wordMeaning: His powerful and corrupt ministers, who were evil-disposed to a weak person, thereupon robbed him of treasury and army even there in his own city.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): His powerful and corrupt ministers, who were evil-disposed to a weak person, thereupon robbed him of treasury and army even there in his own city.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): His powerful and corrupt ministers, who were evil-disposed to a weak person, thereupon robbed him of treasury and army even there in his own city.

verses.sanskrit: ततो मृगयाव्याजेन हृतस्वाम्यः स भूपतिः । एकाकी हयमारुह्य जगाम गहनं वनम्
verses.transliteration: tato mR^igayAvyAjena hR^itasvAmyaH sa bhUpatiH | ekAkI hayamAruhya jagAma gahanaM vanam
verses.translation: Hence the king, deprived of his sovereignty, departed alone on horseback to a dense forest under the pretence of hunting.
verses.wordMeaning: Hence the king, deprived of his sovereignty, departed alone on horseback to a dense forest under the pretence of hunting.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Hence the king, deprived of his sovereignty, departed alone on horseback to a dense forest under the pretence of hunting.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Hence the king, deprived of his sovereignty, departed alone on horseback to a dense forest under the pretence of hunting.

verses.sanskrit: स तत्राश्रममद्राक्षीद्द्विजवर्यस्य मेधसः । प्रशान्तश्वापदाकीर्णं मुनिशिष्योपशोभितम्
verses.transliteration: sa tatrAshramamadrAkShIddvijavaryasya medhasaH | prashAntashvApadAkIrNaM munishiShyopashobhitam
verses.translation: There he saw the hermitage of the noble twice-born Medhas, inhabited by wild animals which were peaceful, graced by the muni's disciples.
verses.wordMeaning: There he saw the hermitage of the noble twice-born Medhas, inhabited by wild animals which were peaceful, graced by the muni's disciples.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): There he saw the hermitage of the noble twice-born Medhas, inhabited by wild animals which were peaceful, graced by the muni's disciples.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): There he saw the hermitage of the noble twice-born Medhas, inhabited by wild animals which were peaceful, graced by the muni's disciples.

verses.sanskrit: तस्थौ कञ्चित्स कालं च मुनिना तेन सत्कृतः । इतश्चेतश्च विचरंस्तस्मिन् मुनिवराश्रमे
verses.transliteration: tasthau ka~nchitsa kAlaM cha muninA tena satkR^itaH | itashchetashcha vicharaMstasmin munivarAshrame
verses.translation: And he dwelt there some time, honoured by the muni, roaming hither and thither in that fine hermitage of the muni.
verses.wordMeaning: And he dwelt there some time, honoured by the muni, roaming hither and thither in that fine hermitage of the muni.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And he dwelt there some time, honoured by the muni, roaming hither and thither in that fine hermitage of the muni.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And he dwelt there some time, honoured by the muni, roaming hither and thither in that fine hermitage of the muni.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽचिन्तयत्तदा तत्र ममत्वाकृष्टमानसः । मत्पूर्वैः पालितं पूर्वं मया हीनं पुरं हि तत्
verses.transliteration: so.achintayattadA tatra mamatvAkR^iShTamAnasaH | matpUrvaiH pAlitaM pUrvaM mayA hInaM puraM hi tat
verses.translation: He fell into thought there then, his mind being distraught by selfishness, egotistical: 'Lost indeed is the city which I guarded formerly, and which was guarded by my forefathers.'
verses.wordMeaning: He fell into thought there then, his mind being distraught by selfishness, egotistical: 'Lost indeed is the city which I guarded formerly, and which was guarded by my forefathers.'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): He fell into thought there then, his mind being distraught by selfishness, egotistical: 'Lost indeed is the city which I guarded formerly, and which was guarded by my forefathers.'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): He fell into thought there then, his mind being distraught by selfishness, egotistical: 'Lost indeed is the city which I guarded formerly, and which was guarded by my forefathers.'

verses.sanskrit: मद्भृत्यैस्तैरसद्वृत्तैर्धर्मतः पाल्यते न वा । न जाने स प्रधानो मे शूरो हस्ती सदामदः
verses.transliteration: madbhR^ityaistairasadvR^ittairdharmataH pAlyate na vA | na jAne sa pradhAno me shUro hastI sadAmadaH
verses.translation: 'Whether it is guarded righteously or not by those my servants of wicked conduct, I know not. My chief war-elephant, always ardent,'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Whether it is guarded righteously or not by those my servants of wicked conduct, I know not. My chief war-elephant, always ardent,'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'Whether it is guarded righteously or not by those my servants of wicked conduct, I know not. My chief war-elephant, always ardent,'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'Whether it is guarded righteously or not by those my servants of wicked conduct, I know not. My chief war-elephant, always ardent,'

verses.sanskrit: मम वैरिवशं यातः कान् भोगानुपलप्स्यते । ये ममानुगता नित्यं प्रसादधनभोजनैः
verses.transliteration: mama vairivashaM yAtaH kAn bhogAnupalapsyate | ye mamAnugatA nityaM prasAdadhanabhojanaiH
verses.translation: 'has passed into the power of my foes; what pleasures will he obtain? They who were my constant followers, favoured with grace, riches and food,'
verses.wordMeaning: 'has passed into the power of my foes; what pleasures will he obtain? They who were my constant followers, favoured with grace, riches and food,'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'has passed into the power of my foes; what pleasures will he obtain? They who were my constant followers, favoured with grace, riches and food,'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'has passed into the power of my foes; what pleasures will he obtain? They who were my constant followers, favoured with grace, riches and food,'

verses.sanskrit: अनुवृत्तिं ध्रुवं तेऽद्य कुर्वन्त्यन्यमहीभृताम् । असम्यग्व्ययशीलैस्तैः कुर्वद्भिः सततं व्ययम्
verses.transliteration: anuvR^ittiM dhruvaM te.adya kurvantyanyamahIbhR^itAm | asamyagvyayashIlaistaiH kurvadbhiH satataM vyayam
verses.translation: 'now assuredly pay court to other kings. The treasure which I amassed with great difficulty, squandered continually by those men addicted to unbecoming expenditure,'
verses.wordMeaning: 'now assuredly pay court to other kings. The treasure which I amassed with great difficulty, squandered continually by those men addicted to unbecoming expenditure,'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'now assuredly pay court to other kings. The treasure which I amassed with great difficulty, squandered continually by those men addicted to unbecoming expenditure,'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'now assuredly pay court to other kings. The treasure which I amassed with great difficulty, squandered continually by those men addicted to unbecoming expenditure,'

verses.sanskrit: सञ्चितः सोऽतिदुःखेन क्षयं कोशो गमिष्यति । एतच्चान्यच्च सततं चिन्तयामास पार्थिवः
verses.transliteration: sa~nchitaH so.atiduHkhena kShayaM kosho gamiShyati | etachchAnyachcha satataM chintayAmAsa pArthivaH
verses.translation: 'will go to waste.' These and other matters the king thought of continually.
verses.wordMeaning: 'will go to waste.' These and other matters the king thought of continually.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'will go to waste.' These and other matters the king thought of continually.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'will go to waste.' These and other matters the king thought of continually.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र विप्राश्रमाभ्याशे वैश्यमेकं ददर्श सः । स पृष्टस्तेन कस्त्वं भो हेतुश्चागमनेऽत्र कः
verses.transliteration: tatra viprAshramAbhyAshe vaishyamekaM dadarsha saH | sa pR^iShTastena kastvaM bho hetushchAgamane.atra kaH
verses.translation: Near the brahman's hermitage there he saw a solitary vaishya, and asked him, 'Ho! who art thou? and what is the reason of thy coming here?'
verses.wordMeaning: Near the brahman's hermitage there he saw a solitary vaishya, and asked him, 'Ho! who art thou? and what is the reason of thy coming here?'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Near the brahman's hermitage there he saw a solitary vaishya, and asked him, 'Ho! who art thou? and what is the reason of thy coming here?'

verses.sanskrit: सशोक इव कस्मात्त्वं दुर्मना इव लक्ष्यसे । इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तस्य भूपतेः प्रणयोदितम्
verses.transliteration: sashoka iva kasmAttvaM durmanA iva lakShyase | ityAkarNya vachastasya bhUpateH praNayoditam
verses.translation: 'Why appearest thou as if full of sorrow, as if afflicted in mind?' Hearing this speech of the king, which was uttered in friendly mood,
verses.wordMeaning: 'Why appearest thou as if full of sorrow, as if afflicted in mind?' Hearing this speech of the king, which was uttered in friendly mood,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'Why appearest thou as if full of sorrow, as if afflicted in mind?' Hearing this speech of the king, which was uttered in friendly mood,

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्युवाच स तं वैश्यः प्रश्रयावनतो नृपम्
verses.transliteration: pratyuvAcha sa taM vaishyaH prashrayAvanato nR^ipam
verses.translation: the vaishya, bowing respectfully, replied to the king.
verses.wordMeaning: the vaishya, bowing respectfully, replied to the king.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): the vaishya, bowing respectfully, replied to the king.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): the vaishya, bowing respectfully, replied to the king.

verses.sanskrit: वैश्य उवाच
verses.transliteration: vaishya uvAcha
verses.translation: The vaishya spoke:
verses.wordMeaning: The vaishya spoke:
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The vaishya spoke:
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The vaishya spoke:

verses.sanskrit: समाधिर्नाम वैश्योऽहमुत्पन्नो धनिनां कुले
verses.transliteration: samAdhirnAma vaishyo.ahamutpanno dhaninAM kule
verses.translation: I am a vaishya, Samadhi by name, born in a family of wealthy folk.
verses.wordMeaning: I am a vaishya, Samadhi by name, born in a family of wealthy folk.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): I am a vaishya, Samadhi by name, born in a family of wealthy folk.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): I am a vaishya, Samadhi by name, born in a family of wealthy folk.

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रदारैर्निरस्तश्च धनलोभादसाधुभिः । विहीनश्च धनैर्दारैः पुत्रैरादाय मे धनम्
verses.transliteration: putradArairnirastashcha dhanalobhAdasAdhubhiH | vihInashcha dhanairdAraiH putrairAdAya me dhanam
verses.translation: I have been cast out by my sons and wife, who are wicked through greed for wealth; and bereft of riches, wife and sons, my wealth taken by them,
verses.wordMeaning: I have been cast out by my sons and wife, who are wicked through greed for wealth; and bereft of riches, wife and sons, my wealth taken by them,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): I have been cast out by my sons and wife, who are wicked through greed for wealth; and bereft of riches, wife and sons, my wealth taken by them,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): I have been cast out by my sons and wife, who are wicked through greed for wealth; and bereft of riches, wife and sons, my wealth taken by them,

verses.sanskrit: वनमभ्यागतो दुःखी निरस्तश्चाप्तबन्धुभिः । सोऽहं न वेद्मि पुत्राणां कुशलाकुशलात्मिकाम्
verses.transliteration: vanamabhyAgato duHkhI nirastashchAptabandhubhiH | so.ahaM na vedmi putrANAM kushalAkushalAtmikAm
verses.translation: I have come to the forest, unhappy and cast out by my trusted kinsmen. In this state I know not the welfare or misfortune of my sons,
verses.wordMeaning: I have come to the forest, unhappy and cast out by my trusted kinsmen. In this state I know not the welfare or misfortune of my sons,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): I have come to the forest, unhappy and cast out by my trusted kinsmen. In this state I know not the welfare or misfortune of my sons,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): I have come to the forest, unhappy and cast out by my trusted kinsmen. In this state I know not the welfare or misfortune of my sons,

verses.sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं स्वजनानां च दाराणां चात्र संस्थितः । किं नु तेषां गृहे क्षेममक्षेमं किं नु साम्प्रतम्
verses.transliteration: pravR^ittiM svajanAnAM cha dArANAM chAtra saMsthitaH | kiM nu teShAM gR^ihe kShemamakShemaM kiM nu sAmpratam
verses.translation: nor the tidings of my family nor of my wife, and here I dwell. Is welfare theirs at home now, or ill-luck?
verses.wordMeaning: nor the tidings of my family nor of my wife, and here I dwell. Is welfare theirs at home now, or ill-luck?
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): nor the tidings of my family nor of my wife, and here I dwell. Is welfare theirs at home now, or ill-luck?
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): nor the tidings of my family nor of my wife, and here I dwell. Is welfare theirs at home now, or ill-luck?

verses.sanskrit: कथं ते किं नु सद्वृत्ता दुर्वृत्ताः किं नु मे सुताः
verses.transliteration: kathaM te kiM nu sadvR^ittA durvR^ittAH kiM nu me sutAH
verses.translation: How are they? Are my sons living good or evil lives?
verses.wordMeaning: How are they? Are my sons living good or evil lives?

verses.transliteration: dR^iShTadoShe.api viShaye mamatvAkR^iShTamAnasau | tatkimetanmahAbhAga yanmoho j~nAninorapi

verses.transliteration: j~nAnamasti samastasya jantorviShayagochare

verses.translation: Thou art Svaha, thou art Svadha; thou indeed art Vashatkara, thou hast sound for thy soul;
verses.hindi: तुम श्री हो, ईश्वरी हो, ह्री (लज्जा) हो, बोधस्वरूपा बुद्धि हो। तुम लज्जा हो, पुष्टि हो, तुष्टि हो, शांति हो, और क्षांति (सहनशीलता) हो।
verses.wordMeaning: This verse from the Devi Stuti (praise of the Goddess) identifies the Divine Mother with every positive quality within human experience. She is not a distant deity but the very fabric of all that is nurturing, wise, peaceful, and dignified in human life. The Shakta tradition sees the divine feminine not as a goddess among gods but as the ultimate power (shakti) underlying all existence.
verses.explanation: This verse from the Devi Stuti (praise of the Goddess) identifies the Divine Mother with every positive quality within human experience. She is not a distant deity but the very fabric of all that is nurturing, wise, peaceful, and dignified in human life. The Shakta tradition sees the divine feminine not as a goddess among gods but as the ultimate power (shakti) underlying all existence.
verses.science: The human qualities listed here — intelligence (buddhi), nourishment (pushti), satisfaction (tushti), peace (shanti), patience (kshanti) — correspond precisely to what positive psychology identifies as the components of eudaimonic wellbeing. These qualities are not merely moral virtues; neuroscience shows they are neurologically distinct states associated with oxytocin, serotonin, and parasympathetic activation. Worshipping these qualities as divine is recognising them as the most real forces in existence.
verses.lifeLesson: The Divine Mother is not outside you — she is the intelligence that understands, the patience that forgives, the nourishment that sustains, the peace that underlies all conflict. When you cultivate any of these qualities consciously, you are doing Devi puja (worship of the Goddess). Today: practice kshanti (patience) in one difficult moment. That is Shakti worship.
verses.commentary: This verse from the Devi Stuti (praise of the Goddess) identifies the Divine Mother with every positive quality within human experience. She is not a distant deity but the very fabric of all that is nurturing, wise, peaceful, and dignified in human life. The Shakta tradition sees the divine feminine not as a goddess among gods but as the ultimate power (shakti) underlying all existence.

verses.translation: and the Great Delusion, the Lady, the Great Goddess, the Great Demon-queen. And thou art the original source of the universe, the exciting cause of the three qualities;

verses.transliteration: parAparANAM paramA tvameva parameshvarI | yachcha ki~nchitkvachidvastu sadasadvAkhilAtmike

verses.sanskrit: एवमेषा समुत्पन्ना ब्रह्मणा संस्तुता स्वयम् । प्रभावमस्या देव्यास्तु भूयः शृणु वदामि ते
verses.transliteration: evameShA samutpannA brahmaNA saMstutA svayam | prabhAvamasyA devyAstu bhUyaH shR^iNu vadAmi te
verses.translation: Thus was she born, when praised by Brahma himself. Now listen again; I tell thee of this goddess' majesty.
verses.wordMeaning: Thus was she born, when praised by Brahma himself. Now listen again; I tell thee of this goddess' majesty.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ ह्रीं ऋषिरुवाच
verses.transliteration: OM hrIM R^iShiruvAcha
verses.translation: Om Hrim. The rishi spoke:
verses.hindi: जिसकी शक्ति से यह जगत व्याप्त है — जो समस्त देव-शक्तियों का समूहरूप है — उस सम्पूर्ण देव-महर्षि-पूजित अम्बिका को हम भक्ति से प्रणाम करते हैं। वह हमें शुभ प्रदान करें।
verses.wordMeaning: The second chapter's great declaration: the Devi is not one power among many — she is the totality of all divine energies combined. Mahalakshmi emerges when the individual powers of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva are each insufficient against Mahishasura. The teaching: some challenges are too large for any single strength. They require the integration of all capacities. The Divine Mother is that integration.
verses.explanation: The second chapter's great declaration: the Devi is not one power among many — she is the totality of all divine energies combined. Mahalakshmi emerges when the individual powers of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva are each insufficient against Mahishasura. The teaching: some challenges are too large for any single strength. They require the integration of all capacities. The Divine Mother is that integration.
verses.science: Research on cognitive integration (Epstein's CEST theory): the most effective human response to complex threats combines analytical intelligence, emotional intelligence, experiential wisdom, and embodied instinct — none alone is sufficient. The Mahalakshmi episode models this integration: each god contributes his energy, and together they produce a force greater than any individual capacity.
verses.lifeLesson: When a challenge feels too large for any single approach — when willpower alone fails, planning alone fails, prayer alone fails — recognise the Mahalakshmi moment: the time to integrate everything you have. Bring your intellect, emotions, relationships, and spiritual practice to bear simultaneously. That wholeness is the Goddess.
verses.commentary: The second chapter's great declaration: the Devi is not one power among many — she is the totality of all divine energies combined. verses.sanskrit: देवासुरमभूद्युद्धं पूर्णमब्दशतं पुरा । महिषेऽसुराणामधिपे देवानां च पुरन्दरे
verses.transliteration: devAsuramabhUdyuddhaM pUrNamabdashataM purA | mahiShe.asurANAmadhipe devAnAM cha purandare
verses.translation: Of yore there was a fight for a full hundred years between the gods and Asuras, when Mahisha was lord of the Asuras and Indra lord of the gods;
verses.wordMeaning: Of yore there was a fight for a full hundred years between the gods and Asuras, when Mahisha was lord of the Asuras and Indra lord of the gods;

verses.sanskrit: तत्रासुरैर्महावीर्यैर्देवसैन्यं पराजितम् । जित्वा च सकलान् देवानिन्द्रोऽभून्महिषासुरः
verses.transliteration: tatrAsurairmahAvIryairdevasainyaM parAjitam | jitvA cha sakalAn devAnindro.abhUnmahiShAsuraH
verses.translation: in it the army of the gods was vanquished by the Asuras who excelled in valour, and the Asura Mahisha, after conquering all the gods, became the Indra.
verses.wordMeaning: in it the army of the gods was vanquished by the Asuras who excelled in valour, and the Asura Mahisha, after conquering all the gods, became the Indra.

verses.sanskrit: ततः पराजिता देवाः पद्मयोनिं प्रजापतिम् । पुरस्कृत्य गतास्तत्र यत्रेशगरुडध्वजौ
verses.transliteration: tataH parAjitA devAH padmayoniM prajApatim | puraskR^itya gatAstatra yatreshagaruDadhvajau
verses.translation: Then the vanquished gods, placing the lotus-born Prajapati Brahma at their head, went where abode Shiva and Vishnu.

verses.transliteration: yathAvR^ittaM tayostadvanmahiShAsuracheShTitam | tridashAH kathayAmAsurdevAbhibhavavistaram
verses.translation: The thirty gods described to them accurately what had happened, the full story of the gods' discomfiture which had been wrought by the Asura Mahisha:

verses.sanskrit: सूर्येन्द्राग्न्यनिलेन्दूनां यमस्य वरुणस्य च । अन्येषां चाधिकारान्स स्वयमेवाधितिष्ठति
verses.transliteration: sUryendrAgnyanilendUnAM yamasya varuNasya cha | anyeShAM chAdhikArAnsa svayamevAdhitiShThati
verses.translation: 'He, Mahisha, in his own person domineers over the jurisdictions of the Sun, Indra, Agni, Vayu and the Moon, of Yama and Varuna and of the other gods.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'He, Mahisha, in his own person domineers over the jurisdictions of the Sun, Indra, Agni, Vayu and the Moon, of Yama and Varuna and of the other gods.'

verses.sanskrit: स्वर्गान्निराकृताः सर्वे तेन देवगणा भुवि । विचरन्ति यथा मर्त्या महिषेण दुरात्मना
verses.transliteration: svargAnnirAkR^itAH sarve tena devagaNA bhuvi | vicharanti yathA martyA mahiSheNa durAtmanA
verses.translation: 'Cast out by that evil-souled Mahisha from Svarga, all the hosts of the gods wander on the earth like mortals.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Cast out by that evil-souled Mahisha from Svarga, all the hosts of the gods wander on the earth like mortals.'

verses.sanskrit: एतद्वः कथितं सर्वममरारिविचेष्टितम् । शरणं वः प्रपन्नाः स्मो वधस्तस्य विचिन्त्यताम्
verses.transliteration: etadvaH kathitaM sarvamamarArivicheShTitam | sharaNaM vaH prapannAH smo vadhastasya vichintyatAm
verses.translation: 'It has now been related to you both, all that has been wrought by the foe of the Immortals, and we have sought you both as a refuge; let his destruction be devised!'
verses.wordMeaning: 'It has now been related to you both, all that has been wrought by the foe of the Immortals, and we have sought you both as a refuge; let his destruction be devised!'

verses.sanskrit: इत्थं निशम्य देवानां वचांसि मधुसूदनः । चकार कोपं शम्भुश्च भ्रुकुटीकुटिलाननौ
verses.transliteration: itthaM nishamya devAnAM vachAMsi madhusUdanaH | chakAra kopaM shambhushcha bhrukuTIkuTilAnanau
verses.translation: Having thus heard the words of the gods, Vishnu was wroth and Shiva also; both their faces became furrowed with frowns.
verses.wordMeaning: Having thus heard the words of the gods, Vishnu was wroth and Shiva also; both their faces became furrowed with frowns.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽतिकोपपूर्णस्य चक्रिणो वदनात्ततः । निश्चक्राम महत्तेजो ब्रह्मणः शङ्करस्य च
verses.transliteration: tato.atikopapUrNasya chakriNo vadanAttataH | nishchakrAma mahattejo brahmaNaH sha~Nkarasya cha
verses.translation: Then issued forth great energy from the mouth of the discus-bearer Vishnu, who was full of intense anger, and from the mouths of Brahma and Shiva;
verses.hindi: हे दैत्यविनाशिनी! यह जानकर तुम्हारा भय निश्चय ही छूट गया है। दैत्यों का विनाश करने के समय तुमने अपनी आत्मशक्ति से सदा रक्षण किया है, और वही तुम्हारा स्वभाव है, हे महावैरिणी!
verses.wordMeaning: This verse reveals the Devi's fundamental nature as the protector of the universe. She does not merely fight demons as an external enemy; she protects creation by her own inherent power (ātmaśakti). The teaching: the divine feminine is not a warrior who fights when called; she is the active principle of protection that is always engaged. The destruction of evil is not a separate activity from the protection of good — they are one and the same dynamic.

verses.sanskrit: अन्येषां चैव देवानां शक्रादीनां शरीरतः । निर्गतं सुमहत्तेजस्तच्चैक्यं समगच्छत
verses.transliteration: anyeShAM chaiva devAnAM shakrAdInAM sharIrataH | nirgataM sumahattejastachchaikyaM samagachChata
verses.translation: and from the bodies of Indra and the other gods went forth a very great energy; and it all amalgamated.
verses.hindi: जैसे तुम हृदय में प्रविष्ट होकर स्मरण की जाती हो, हे देवि! तुम्हें प्रथम देखकर, वैसे ही जब तुम्हारा स्मरण मिट जाता है, तब भी हे देवि! तुम्हें प्रथम देखकर स्मरण करते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: The paradox of divine memory: we remember the Devi both when we feel her presence (when she has "entered the heart") and when we feel her absence (when she seems "lost"). In both states, we "see her first" — meaning she is the primary reality, the ground of all experience. Whether we feel connected or disconnected, the Devi remains the first and last reality. This verse teaches that devotion is not dependent on feeling; it persists through all states of consciousness.

verses.transliteration: atIva tejasaH kUTaM jvalantamiva parvatam | dadR^ishuste surAstatra jvAlAvyAptadigantaram
verses.translation: The gods beheld the mass of intense energy there like a burning mountain, pervading the other regions of the sky with its blaze;
verses.wordMeaning: The gods beheld the mass of intense energy there like a burning mountain, pervading the other regions of the sky with its blaze;

verses.sanskrit: अतुलं तत्र तत्तेजः सर्वदेवशरीरजम् । एकस्थं तदभून्नारी व्याप्तलोकत्रयं त्विषा
verses.transliteration: atulaM tatra tattejaH sarvadevasharIrajam | ekasthaM tadabhUnnArI vyAptalokatrayaM tviShA
verses.translation: and that unparalleled energy, born of the bodies of all the gods, which pervaded the three worlds with its light, gathering into one became a female.

verses.sanskrit: यदभूच्छाम्भवं तेजस्तेनाजायत तन्मुखम् । याम्येन चाभवन् केशा बाहवो विष्णुतेजसा
verses.transliteration: yadabhUchChAmbhavaM tejastenAjAyata tanmukham | yAmyena chAbhavan keshA bAhavo viShNutejasA
verses.translation: By what was Shiva's energy her face was developed, and by Yama's energy grew her hair, and her arms by Vishnu's energy,
verses.wordMeaning: By what was Shiva's energy her face was developed, and by Yama's energy grew her hair, and her arms by Vishnu's energy,

verses.sanskrit: सौम्येन स्तनयोर्युग्मं मध्यं चैन्द्रेण चाभवत् । वारुणेन च जङ्घोरू नितम्बस्तेजसा भुवः
verses.transliteration: saumyena stanayoryugmaM madhyaM chaindreNa chAbhavat | vAruNena cha ja~NghorU nitambastejasA bhuvaH
verses.translation: by the Moon's her twin breasts; and her waist came into being by Indra's energy, and by Varuna's her legs and thighs, by the Earth's energy her hips,

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मणस्तेजसा पादौ तदङ्गुल्योऽर्कतेजसा । वसूनां च कराङ्गुल्यः कौबेरेण च नासिका
verses.transliteration: brahmaNastejasA pAdau tada~Ngulyo.arkatejasA | vasUnAM cha karA~NgulyaH kaubereNa cha nAsikA
verses.translation: by Brahma's energy her feet, her toes by the Sun's energy, and by the Vasus' energy her hands and fingers, and by Kuvera's her nose;

verses.sanskrit: तस्यास्तु दन्ताः सम्भूताः प्राजापत्येन तेजसा । नयनत्रितयं जज्ञे तथा पावकतेजसा
verses.transliteration: tasyAstu dantAH sambhUtAH prAjApatyena tejasA | nayanatritayaM jaj~ne tathA pAvakatejasA
verses.translation: and her teeth grew by the Prajapati's energy, and three eyes were developed by Agni's energy;

verses.sanskrit: भ्रुवौ च सन्ध्ययोस्तेजः श्रवणावनिलस्य च । अन्येषां चैव देवानां सम्भवस्तेजसां शिवा
verses.transliteration: bhruvau cha sandhyayostejaH shravaNAvanilasya cha | anyeShAM chaiva devAnAM sambhavastejasAM shivA
verses.translation: and her eyebrows were the energy of the two twilights, and her ears Vayu's energy; and the coming into being of the energies of the other gods became the auspicious goddess.

verses.sanskrit: ततः समस्तदेवानां तेजोराशिसमुद्भवाम् । तां विलोक्य मुदं प्रापुरमरा महिषार्दिताः । ततो देवा ददुस्तस्यै स्वानि स्वान्यायुधानि च
verses.transliteration: tataH samastadevAnAM tejorAshisamudbhavAm | tAM vilokya mudaM prApuramarA mahiShArditAH | tato devA dadustasyai svAni svAnyAyudhAni cha
verses.translation: Then gazing at her, who had sprung from the combined energies of all the gods, the Immortals who were afflicted by Mahisha felt a keen joy. Then the gods gave her each their own weapons.
verses.wordMeaning: Then gazing at her, who had sprung from the combined energies of all the gods, the Immortals who were afflicted by Mahisha felt a keen joy. Then the gods gave her each their own weapons.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then gazing at her, who had sprung from the combined energies of all the gods, the Immortals who were afflicted by Mahisha felt a keen joy. Then the gods gave her each their own weapons.

verses.sanskrit: शूलं शूलाद्विनिष्कृष्य ददौ तस्यै पिनाकधृक् । चक्रं च दत्तवान् कृष्णः समुत्पाट्य स्वचक्रतः
verses.transliteration: shUlaM shUlAdviniShkR^iShya dadau tasyai pinAkadhR^ik | chakraM cha dattavAn kR^iShNaH samutpATya svachakrataH
verses.translation: The bearer of the bow Pinaka, drawing a trident forth from his own trident, gave it to her; and Krishna gave a discus, pulling it out of his own discus;
verses.wordMeaning: The bearer of the bow Pinaka, drawing a trident forth from his own trident, gave it to her; and Krishna gave a discus, pulling it out of his own discus;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The bearer of the bow Pinaka, drawing a trident forth from his own trident, gave it to her; and Krishna gave a discus, pulling it out of his own discus;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The bearer of the bow Pinaka, drawing a trident forth from his own trident, gave it to her; and Krishna gave a discus, pulling it out of his own discus;

verses.sanskrit: शङ्खं च वरुणः शक्तिं ददौ तस्यै हुताशनः । मारुतो दत्तवांश्चापं बाणपूर्णे तथेषुधी
verses.transliteration: sha~NkhaM cha varuNaH shaktiM dadau tasyai hutAshanaH | mAruto dattavAMshchApaM bANapUrNe tatheShudhI
verses.translation: and Varuna gave her a conch, Agni a spear, Maruta gave a bow and a quiver filled with arrows.
verses.wordMeaning: and Varuna gave her a conch, Agni a spear, Maruta gave a bow and a quiver filled with arrows.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and Varuna gave her a conch, Agni a spear, Maruta gave a bow and a quiver filled with arrows.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and Varuna gave her a conch, Agni a spear, Maruta gave a bow and a quiver filled with arrows.

verses.sanskrit: वज्रमिन्द्रः समुत्पाट्य कुलिशादमराधिपः । ददौ तस्यै सहस्राक्षो घण्टामैरावताद्गजात्
verses.transliteration: vajramindraH samutpATya kulishAdamarAdhipaH | dadau tasyai sahasrAkSho ghaNTAmairAvatAdgajAt
verses.translation: Indra, lord of the Immortals, gave a thunderbolt, pulling it out of his own thunderbolt; the Thousand-eyed gave her a bell from his elephant Airavata.
verses.wordMeaning: Indra, lord of the Immortals, gave a thunderbolt, pulling it out of his own thunderbolt; the Thousand-eyed gave her a bell from his elephant Airavata.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Indra, lord of the Immortals, gave a thunderbolt, pulling it out of his own thunderbolt; the Thousand-eyed gave her a bell from his elephant Airavata.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Indra, lord of the Immortals, gave a thunderbolt, pulling it out of his own thunderbolt; the Thousand-eyed gave her a bell from his elephant Airavata.

verses.sanskrit: कालदण्डाद्यमो दण्डं पाशं चाम्बुपतिर्ददौ । प्रजापतिश्चाक्षमालां ददौ ब्रह्मा कमण्डलुम्
verses.transliteration: kAladaNDAdyamo daNDaM pAshaM chAmbupatirdadau | prajApatishchAkShamAlAM dadau brahmA kamaNDalum
verses.translation: Yama gave a rod from his own rod of Fate, and the lord of the waters a noose; and the Prajapati gave her a necklace of beads, Brahma an earthen water-pot;
verses.wordMeaning: Yama gave a rod from his own rod of Fate, and the lord of the waters a noose; and the Prajapati gave her a necklace of beads, Brahma an earthen water-pot;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Yama gave a rod from his own rod of Fate, and the lord of the waters a noose; and the Prajapati gave her a necklace of beads, Brahma an earthen water-pot;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Yama gave a rod from his own rod of Fate, and the lord of the waters a noose; and the Prajapati gave her a necklace of beads, Brahma an earthen water-pot;

verses.sanskrit: समस्तरोमकूपेषु निजरश्मीन् दिवाकरः । कालश्च दत्तवान् खड्गं तस्यै चर्म च निर्मलम्
verses.transliteration: samastaromakUpeShu nijarashmIn divAkaraH | kAlashcha dattavAn khaDgaM tasyai charma cha nirmalam
verses.translation: the Sun bestowed his own rays on all the pores of her skin, and Destiny gave her a sword and a spotless shield;
verses.wordMeaning: the Sun bestowed his own rays on all the pores of her skin, and Destiny gave her a sword and a spotless shield;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): the Sun bestowed his own rays on all the pores of her skin, and Destiny gave her a sword and a spotless shield;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): the Sun bestowed his own rays on all the pores of her skin, and Destiny gave her a sword and a spotless shield;

verses.sanskrit: क्षीरोदश्चामलं हारमजरे च तथाम्बरे । चूडामणिं तथा दिव्यं कुण्डले कटकानि च
verses.transliteration: kShIrodashchAmalaM hAramajare cha tathAmbare | chUDAmaNiM tathA divyaM kuNDale kaTakAni cha
verses.translation: and the Ocean of milk a spotless necklace of pearls and also a pair of undecaying garments, and a celestial crest-jewel, a pair of ear-rings, and bracelets,
verses.wordMeaning: and the Ocean of milk a spotless necklace of pearls and also a pair of undecaying garments, and a celestial crest-jewel, a pair of ear-rings, and bracelets,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and the Ocean of milk a spotless necklace of pearls and also a pair of undecaying garments, and a celestial crest-jewel, a pair of ear-rings, and bracelets,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and the Ocean of milk a spotless necklace of pearls and also a pair of undecaying garments, and a celestial crest-jewel, a pair of ear-rings, and bracelets,

verses.sanskrit: अर्धचन्द्रं तथा शुभ्रं केयूरान् सर्वबाहुषु । नूपुरौ विमलौ तद्वद् ग्रैवेयकमनुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration: ardhachandraM tathA shubhraM keyUrAn sarvabAhuShu | nUpurau vimalau tadvad graiveyakamanuttamam
verses.translation: and a brilliant half-moon ornament, and armlets over all her arms, and also a pair of bright anklets, and a necklet of the finest make,
verses.wordMeaning: and a brilliant half-moon ornament, and armlets over all her arms, and also a pair of bright anklets, and a necklet of the finest make,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and a brilliant half-moon ornament, and armlets over all her arms, and also a pair of bright anklets, and a necklet of the finest make,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and a brilliant half-moon ornament, and armlets over all her arms, and also a pair of bright anklets, and a necklet of the finest make,

verses.sanskrit: अङ्गुलीयकरत्नानि समस्तास्वङ्गुलीषु च । विश्वकर्मा ददौ तस्यै परशुं चातिनिर्मलम्
verses.transliteration: a~NgulIyakaratnAni samastAsva~NgulIShu cha | vishvakarmA dadau tasyai parashuM chAtinirmalam
verses.translation: and rings and gems on all her fingers; and Vishvakarman gave to her a brightly polished axe,
verses.wordMeaning: and rings and gems on all her fingers; and Vishvakarman gave to her a brightly polished axe,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and rings and gems on all her fingers; and Vishvakarman gave to her a brightly polished axe,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and rings and gems on all her fingers; and Vishvakarman gave to her a brightly polished axe,

verses.sanskrit: अस्त्राण्यनेकरूपाणि तथाभेद्यं च दंशनम् । अम्लानपङ्कजां मालां शिरस्युरसि चापराम्
verses.transliteration: astrANyanekarUpANi tathAbhedyaM cha daMshanam | amlAnapa~NkajAM mAlAM shirasyurasi chAparAm
verses.translation: weapons of many shapes and also armour that could not be pierced; and Ocean gave her a garland of fadeless lotus-flowers for her head and another for her breast,
verses.wordMeaning: weapons of many shapes and also armour that could not be pierced; and Ocean gave her a garland of fadeless lotus-flowers for her head and another for her breast,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): weapons of many shapes and also armour that could not be pierced; and Ocean gave her a garland of fadeless lotus-flowers for her head and another for her breast,

verses.sanskrit: अददज्जलधिस्तस्यै पङ्कजं चातिशोभनम् । हिमवान् वाहनं सिंहं रत्नानि विविधानि च
verses.transliteration: adadajjaladhistasyai pa~NkajaM chAtishobhanam | himavAn vAhanaM siMhaM ratnAni vividhAni cha
verses.translation: and a very brilliant lotus-flower besides. Himavat gave her a lion to ride on and gems of various kinds.
verses.wordMeaning: and a very brilliant lotus-flower besides. Himavat gave her a lion to ride on and gems of various kinds.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and a very brilliant lotus-flower besides. Himavat gave her a lion to ride on and gems of various kinds.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and a very brilliant lotus-flower besides. Himavat gave her a lion to ride on and gems of various kinds.

verses.sanskrit: ददावशून्यं सुरया पानपात्रं धनाधिपः । शेषश्च सर्वनागेशो महामणिविभूषितम्
verses.transliteration: dadAvashUnyaM surayA pAnapAtraM dhanAdhipaH | sheShashcha sarvanAgesho mahAmaNivibhUShitam
verses.translation: Kuvera, the lord of wealth, gave a drinking cup ever full of wine. And Shesha, the lord of all the serpents, who supports this earth,
verses.wordMeaning: Kuvera, the lord of wealth, gave a drinking cup ever full of wine. And Shesha, the lord of all the serpents, who supports this earth,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Kuvera, the lord of wealth, gave a drinking cup ever full of wine. And Shesha, the lord of all the serpents, who supports this earth,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Kuvera, the lord of wealth, gave a drinking cup ever full of wine. And Shesha, the lord of all the serpents, who supports this earth,

verses.sanskrit: नागहारं ददौ तस्यै धत्ते यः पृथिवीमिमाम् । अन्यैरपि सुरैर्देवी भूषणैरायुधैस्तथा
verses.transliteration: nAgahAraM dadau tasyai dhatte yaH pR^ithivImimAm | anyairapi surairdevI bhUShaNairAyudhaistathA
verses.translation: gave her a serpent-necklace adorned with large gems. Honoured by other gods also with gifts of ornaments and weapons,
verses.wordMeaning: gave her a serpent-necklace adorned with large gems. Honoured by other gods also with gifts of ornaments and weapons,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): gave her a serpent-necklace adorned with large gems. Honoured by other gods also with gifts of ornaments and weapons,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): gave her a serpent-necklace adorned with large gems. Honoured by other gods also with gifts of ornaments and weapons,

verses.sanskrit: सम्मानिता ननादोच्चैः साट्टहासं मुहुर्मुहुः । तस्या नादेन घोरेण कृत्स्नमापूरितं नभः
verses.transliteration: sammAnitA nanAdochchaiH sATTahAsaM muhurmuhuH | tasyA nAdena ghoreNa kR^itsnamApUritaM nabhaH
verses.translation: the goddess uttered a loud roar blended with a horse-laugh again and again. The whole welkin was filled with her terrible roar.
verses.wordMeaning: the goddess uttered a loud roar blended with a horse-laugh again and again. The whole welkin was filled with her terrible roar.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): the goddess uttered a loud roar blended with a horse-laugh again and again. The whole welkin was filled with her terrible roar.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): the goddess uttered a loud roar blended with a horse-laugh again and again. The whole welkin was filled with her terrible roar.

verses.sanskrit: अमायतातिमहता प्रतिशब्दो महानभूत् । चुक्षुभुः सकला लोकाः समुद्राश्च चकम्पिरे
verses.transliteration: amAyatAtimahatA pratishabdo mahAnabhUt | chukShubhuH sakalA lokAH samudrAshcha chakampire
verses.translation: By that penetrating and exceedingly great roar a great echo arose; all the worlds shook and the seas trembled,
verses.wordMeaning: By that penetrating and exceedingly great roar a great echo arose; all the worlds shook and the seas trembled,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): By that penetrating and exceedingly great roar a great echo arose; all the worlds shook and the seas trembled,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): By that penetrating and exceedingly great roar a great echo arose; all the worlds shook and the seas trembled,

verses.sanskrit: चचाल वसुधा चेलुः सकलाश्च महीधराः । जयेति देवाश्च मुदा तामूचुः सिंहवाहिनीम्
verses.transliteration: chachAla vasudhA cheluH sakalAshcha mahIdharAH | jayeti devAshcha mudA tAmUchuH siMhavAhinIm
verses.translation: the earth quaked and all the mountains moved. And 'Conquer thou!' exclaimed the gods with joy to her who rode on the lion,
verses.wordMeaning: the earth quaked and all the mountains moved. And 'Conquer thou!' exclaimed the gods with joy to her who rode on the lion,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): the earth quaked and all the mountains moved. And 'Conquer thou!' exclaimed the gods with joy to her who rode on the lion,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): the earth quaked and all the mountains moved. And 'Conquer thou!' exclaimed the gods with joy to her who rode on the lion,

verses.sanskrit: तुष्टुवुर्मुनयश्चैनां भक्तिनम्रात्ममूर्तयः । दृष्ट्वा समस्तं सङ्क्षुब्धं त्रैलोक्यममरारयः
verses.transliteration: tuShTuvurmunayashchainAM bhaktinamrAtmamUrtayaH | dR^iShTvA samastaM sa~NkShubdhaM trailokyamamarArayaH
verses.translation: and the munis extolled her as they bowed their bodies in faith. Seeing all the three worlds greatly agitated, the foes of the Immortals
verses.wordMeaning: and the munis extolled her as they bowed their bodies in faith. Seeing all the three worlds greatly agitated, the foes of the Immortals
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and the munis extolled her as they bowed their bodies in faith. Seeing all the three worlds greatly agitated, the foes of the Immortals
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and the munis extolled her as they bowed their bodies in faith. Seeing all the three worlds greatly agitated, the foes of the Immortals

verses.sanskrit: सन्नद्धाखिलसैन्यास्ते समुत्तस्थुरुदायुधाः । आः किमेतदिति क्रोधादाभाष्य महिषासुरः
verses.transliteration: sannaddhAkhilasainyAste samuttasthurudAyudhAH | AH kimetaditi krodhAdAbhAShya mahiShAsuraH
verses.translation: uniting all their armies rose up together with uplifted weapons. 'Ha! what is this?' exclaimed the Asura Mahisha in wrath,
verses.wordMeaning: uniting all their armies rose up together with uplifted weapons. 'Ha! what is this?' exclaimed the Asura Mahisha in wrath,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): uniting all their armies rose up together with uplifted weapons. 'Ha! what is this?' exclaimed the Asura Mahisha in wrath,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): uniting all their armies rose up together with uplifted weapons. 'Ha! what is this?' exclaimed the Asura Mahisha in wrath,

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यधावत तं शब्दमशेषैरसुरैर्वृतः । स ददर्श ततो देवीं व्याप्तलोकत्रयां त्विषा
verses.transliteration: abhyadhAvata taM shabdamasheShairasurairvR^itaH | sa dadarsha tato devIM vyAptalokatrayAM tviShA
verses.translation: and rushed, surrounded by all the Asuras, towards that roar. Then he saw the goddess, pervading the three worlds with her light,
verses.wordMeaning: and rushed, surrounded by all the Asuras, towards that roar. Then he saw the goddess, pervading the three worlds with her light,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and rushed, surrounded by all the Asuras, towards that roar. Then he saw the goddess, pervading the three worlds with her light,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and rushed, surrounded by all the Asuras, towards that roar. Then he saw the goddess, pervading the three worlds with her light,

verses.sanskrit: पादाक्रान्त्या नतभुवं किरीटोल्लिखिताम्बराम् । क्षोभिताशेषपातालां धनुर्ज्यानिःस्वनेन ताम्
verses.transliteration: pAdAkrAntyA natabhuvaM kirITollikhitAmbarAm | kShobhitAsheShapAtAlAM dhanurjyAniHsvanena tAm
verses.translation: causing the earth to bow at the touch of her feet, grazing the firmament with her crest, shaking the whole of Patala with the twang of her bow-string,
verses.wordMeaning: causing the earth to bow at the touch of her feet, grazing the firmament with her crest, shaking the whole of Patala with the twang of her bow-string,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): causing the earth to bow at the touch of her feet, grazing the firmament with her crest, shaking the whole of Patala with the twang of her bow-string,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): causing the earth to bow at the touch of her feet, grazing the firmament with her crest, shaking the whole of Patala with the twang of her bow-string,

verses.sanskrit: दिशो भुजसहस्रेण समन्ताद्व्याप्य संस्थिताम् । ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तया देव्या सुरद्विषाम्
verses.transliteration: disho bhujasahasreNa samantAdvyApya saMsthitAm | tataH pravavR^ite yuddhaM tayA devyA suradviShAm
verses.translation: standing pervading the sky all around with her thousand arms. Then began a battle between the goddess and the enemies of the gods,
verses.wordMeaning: standing pervading the sky all around with her thousand arms. Then began a battle between the goddess and the enemies of the gods,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): standing pervading the sky all around with her thousand arms. Then began a battle between the goddess and the enemies of the gods,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): standing pervading the sky all around with her thousand arms. Then began a battle between the goddess and the enemies of the gods,

verses.sanskrit: शस्त्रास्त्रैर्बहुधा मुक्तैरादीपितदिगन्तरम् । महिषासुरसेनानीश्चिक्षुराख्यो महासुरः
verses.transliteration: shastrAstrairbahudhA muktairAdIpitadigantaram | mahiShAsurasenAnIshchikShurAkhyo mahAsuraH
verses.translation: in which every region of the sky was illumined with the weapons and arms hurled in abundance. The Asura Mahisha's general, the great Asura named Chikshura,
verses.wordMeaning: in which every region of the sky was illumined with the weapons and arms hurled in abundance. The Asura Mahisha's general, the great Asura named Chikshura,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): in which every region of the sky was illumined with the weapons and arms hurled in abundance. The Asura Mahisha's general, the great Asura named Chikshura,

verses.sanskrit: युयुधे चामरश्चान्यैश्चतुरङ्गबलान्वितः । रथानामयुतैः षड्भिरुदग्राख्यो महासुरः
verses.transliteration: yuyudhe chAmarashchAnyaishchatura~NgabalAnvitaH | rathAnAmayutaiH ShaD.hbhirudagrAkhyo mahAsuraH
verses.translation: fought with her; and the Asura Chamara, attended by fourfold forces, fought along with others. The great Asura named Udagra with six myriads of chariots fought;
verses.wordMeaning: fought with her; and the Asura Chamara, attended by fourfold forces, fought along with others. The great Asura named Udagra with six myriads of chariots fought;
