verses.sanskrit: अयुध्यतायुतानां च सहस्रेण महाहनुः । पञ्चाशद्भिश्च नियुतैरसिलोमा महासुरः
verses.transliteration: ayudhyatAyutAnAM cha sahasreNa mahAhanuH | pa~nchAshadbhishcha niyutairasilomA mahAsuraH
verses.translation: and Mahahanu with a thousand myriads gave battle; and the great Asura Asiloman with fifty millions;
verses.wordMeaning: and Mahahanu with a thousand myriads gave battle; and the great Asura Asiloman with fifty millions;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and Mahahanu with a thousand myriads gave battle; and the great Asura Asiloman with fifty millions;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and Mahahanu with a thousand myriads gave battle; and the great Asura Asiloman with fifty millions;

verses.sanskrit: अयुतानां शतैः षड्भिर्बाष्कलो युयुधे रणे । गजवाजिसहस्रौघैरनेकैः परिवारितः
verses.transliteration: ayutAnAM shataiH ShaD.hbhirbAShkalo yuyudhe raNe | gajavAjisahasraughairanekaiH parivAritaH
verses.translation: with six hundred myriads Bashkala fought in the battle; another, surrounded with many troops of thousands of elephants and horses,
verses.wordMeaning: with six hundred myriads Bashkala fought in the battle; another, surrounded with many troops of thousands of elephants and horses,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): with six hundred myriads Bashkala fought in the battle; another, surrounded with many troops of thousands of elephants and horses,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): with six hundred myriads Bashkala fought in the battle; another, surrounded with many troops of thousands of elephants and horses,

verses.sanskrit: वृतो रथानां कोट्या च युद्धे तस्मिन्नयुध्यत । बिडालाख्योऽयुतानां च पञ्चाशद्भिरथायुतैः
verses.transliteration: vR^ito rathAnAM koTyA cha yuddhe tasminnayudhyata | biDAlAkhyo.ayutAnAM cha pa~nchAshadbhirathAyutaiH
verses.translation: and with ten million chariots, fought in that battle; and the Asura named Bidala fought in the battle there, surrounded with fifty myriads of myriads of chariots.
verses.wordMeaning: and with ten million chariots, fought in that battle; and the Asura named Bidala fought in the battle there, surrounded with fifty myriads of myriads of chariots.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and with ten million chariots, fought in that battle; and the Asura named Bidala fought in the battle there, surrounded with fifty myriads of myriads of chariots.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and with ten million chariots, fought in that battle; and the Asura named Bidala fought in the battle there, surrounded with fifty myriads of myriads of chariots.

verses.sanskrit: युयुधे संयुगे तत्र रथानां परिवारितः । अन्ये च तत्रायुतशो रथनागहयैर्वृताः
verses.transliteration: yuyudhe saMyuge tatra rathAnAM parivAritaH | anye cha tatrAyutasho rathanAgahayairvR^itAH
verses.translation: And other great Asuras in myriads, surrounded with chariots, elephants and horses,
verses.wordMeaning: And other great Asuras in myriads, surrounded with chariots, elephants and horses,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And other great Asuras in myriads, surrounded with chariots, elephants and horses,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And other great Asuras in myriads, surrounded with chariots, elephants and horses,

verses.sanskrit: युयुधुः संयुगे देव्या सह तत्र महासुराः । कोटिकोटिसहस्रैस्तु रथानां दन्तिनां तथा
verses.transliteration: yuyudhuH saMyuge devyA saha tatra mahAsurAH | koTikoTisahasraistu rathAnAM dantinAM tathA
verses.translation: fought with the goddess in that battle there. Now the Asura Mahisha was surrounded with thousands of ten million times ten millions of chariots and elephants
verses.wordMeaning: fought with the goddess in that battle there. Now the Asura Mahisha was surrounded with thousands of ten million times ten millions of chariots and elephants
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): fought with the goddess in that battle there. Now the Asura Mahisha was surrounded with thousands of ten million times ten millions of chariots and elephants
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): fought with the goddess in that battle there. Now the Asura Mahisha was surrounded with thousands of ten million times ten millions of chariots and elephants

verses.sanskrit: हयानां च वृतो युद्धे तत्राभून्महिषासुरः । तोमरैर्भिन्दिपालैश्च शक्तिभिर्मुसलैस्तथा
verses.transliteration: hayAnAM cha vR^ito yuddhe tatrAbhUnmahiShAsuraH | tomarairbhindipAlaishcha shaktibhirmusalaistathA
verses.translation: and horses in the battle there. With iron maces and javelins, with spears and clubs,
verses.wordMeaning: and horses in the battle there. With iron maces and javelins, with spears and clubs,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and horses in the battle there. With iron maces and javelins, with spears and clubs,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and horses in the battle there. With iron maces and javelins, with spears and clubs,

verses.sanskrit: युयुधुः संयुगे देव्या खड्गैः परशुपट्टिशैः । केचिच्च चिक्षिपुः शक्तीः केचित् पाशांस्तथापरे
verses.transliteration: yuyudhuH saMyuge devyA khaDgaiH parashupaTTishaiH | kechichcha chikShipuH shaktIH kechit pAshAMstathApare
verses.translation: with swords, with axes and halberds they fought in the battle against the goddess. And some hurled spears, and others nooses,
verses.wordMeaning: with swords, with axes and halberds they fought in the battle against the goddess. And some hurled spears, and others nooses,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): with swords, with axes and halberds they fought in the battle against the goddess. And some hurled spears, and others nooses,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): with swords, with axes and halberds they fought in the battle against the goddess. And some hurled spears, and others nooses,

verses.sanskrit: देवीं खड्गप्रहारैस्तु ते तां हन्तुं प्रचक्रमुः । सापि देवी ततस्तानि शस्त्राण्यस्त्राणि चण्डिका
verses.transliteration: devIM khaDgaprahAraistu te tAM hantuM prachakramuH | sApi devI tatastAni shastrANyastrANi chaNDikA
verses.translation: but they assailed the goddess with blows from their swords in order to slay her. And then the goddess Chandika those weapons and arms
verses.wordMeaning: but they assailed the goddess with blows from their swords in order to slay her. And then the goddess Chandika those weapons and arms
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): but they assailed the goddess with blows from their swords in order to slay her. And then the goddess Chandika those weapons and arms
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): but they assailed the goddess with blows from their swords in order to slay her. And then the goddess Chandika those weapons and arms

verses.sanskrit: लीलयैव प्रचिच्छेद निजशस्त्रास्त्रवर्षिणी । अनायस्तानना देवी स्तूयमाना सुरर्षिभिः
verses.transliteration: lIlayaiva prachichCheda nijashastrAstravarShiNI | anAyastAnanA devI stUyamAnA surarShibhiH
verses.translation: clove, as it were in merest play, by raining forth her own weapons and arms. The goddess betrayed no exertion in her countenance, while the gods and rishis were praising her.
verses.wordMeaning: clove, as it were in merest play, by raining forth her own weapons and arms. The goddess betrayed no exertion in her countenance, while the gods and rishis were praising her.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): clove, as it were in merest play, by raining forth her own weapons and arms. The goddess betrayed no exertion in her countenance, while the gods and rishis were praising her.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): clove, as it were in merest play, by raining forth her own weapons and arms. The goddess betrayed no exertion in her countenance, while the gods and rishis were praising her.

verses.sanskrit: मुमोचासुरदेहेषु शस्त्राण्यस्त्राणि चेश्वरी । सोऽपि क्रुद्धो धुतसटो देव्या वाहनकेसरी
verses.transliteration: mumochAsuradeheShu shastrANyastrANi cheshvarI | so.api kruddho dhutasaTo devyA vAhanakesarI
verses.translation: The queenly goddess hurled her weapons and arms at the Asuras' bodies. The lion also that bore the goddess, enraged and with ruffled mane,
verses.wordMeaning: The queenly goddess hurled her weapons and arms at the Asuras' bodies. The lion also that bore the goddess, enraged and with ruffled mane,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The queenly goddess hurled her weapons and arms at the Asuras' bodies. The lion also that bore the goddess, enraged and with ruffled mane,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The queenly goddess hurled her weapons and arms at the Asuras' bodies. The lion also that bore the goddess, enraged and with ruffled mane,

verses.sanskrit: चचारासुरसैन्येषु वनेष्विव हुताशनः । निःश्वासान् मुमुचे यांश्च युध्यमाना रणेऽम्बिका
verses.transliteration: chachArAsurasainyeShu vaneShviva hutAshanaH | niHshvAsAn mumuche yAMshcha yudhyamAnA raNe.ambikA
verses.translation: stalked among the armies of Asuras, like fire through the forests. And the deep breaths, which Ambika fighting in the battle breathed forth,
verses.wordMeaning: stalked among the armies of Asuras, like fire through the forests. And the deep breaths, which Ambika fighting in the battle breathed forth,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): stalked among the armies of Asuras, like fire through the forests. And the deep breaths, which Ambika fighting in the battle breathed forth,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): stalked among the armies of Asuras, like fire through the forests. And the deep breaths, which Ambika fighting in the battle breathed forth,

verses.sanskrit: त एव सद्यः सम्भूता गणाः शतसहस्रशः । युयुधुस्ते परशुभिर्भिन्दिपालासिपट्टिशैः
verses.transliteration: ta eva sadyaH sambhUtA gaNAH shatasahasrashaH | yuyudhuste parashubhirbhindipAlAsipaTTishaiH
verses.translation: came into real being at once as troops by hundreds and thousands. These fought with axes, with javelins, and swords and halberds,
verses.wordMeaning: came into real being at once as troops by hundreds and thousands. These fought with axes, with javelins, and swords and halberds,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): came into real being at once as troops by hundreds and thousands. These fought with axes, with javelins, and swords and halberds,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): came into real being at once as troops by hundreds and thousands. These fought with axes, with javelins, and swords and halberds,

verses.sanskrit: नाशयन्तोऽसुरगणान् देवीशक्त्युपबृंहिताः । अवादयन्त पटहान् गणाः शङ्खांस्तथापरे
verses.transliteration: nAshayanto.asuragaNAn devIshaktyupabR^iMhitAH | avAdayanta paTahAn gaNAH sha~NkhAMstathApare
verses.translation: destroying the Asura bands, being invigorated by the goddess' energy. And of these bands some raised a din with large drums, and others with conchs,
verses.wordMeaning: destroying the Asura bands, being invigorated by the goddess' energy. And of these bands some raised a din with large drums, and others with conchs,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): destroying the Asura bands, being invigorated by the goddess' energy. And of these bands some raised a din with large drums, and others with conchs,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): destroying the Asura bands, being invigorated by the goddess' energy. And of these bands some raised a din with large drums, and others with conchs,

verses.sanskrit: मृदङ्गांश्च तथैवान्ये तस्मिन् युद्धमहोत्सवे । ततो देवी त्रिशूलेन गदया शक्तिवृष्टिभिः
verses.transliteration: mR^ida~NgAMshcha tathaivAnye tasmin yuddhamahotsave | tato devI trishUlena gadayA shaktivR^iShTibhiH
verses.translation: and others besides with tabors, in that great battle-festival. Then the goddess with her trident, her club, with showers of spears,
verses.wordMeaning: and others besides with tabors, in that great battle-festival. Then the goddess with her trident, her club, with showers of spears,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and others besides with tabors, in that great battle-festival. Then the goddess with her trident, her club, with showers of spears,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and others besides with tabors, in that great battle-festival. Then the goddess with her trident, her club, with showers of spears,

verses.sanskrit: खड्गादिभिश्च शतशो निजघान महासुरान् । पातयामास चैवान्यान् घण्टास्वनविमोहितान्
verses.transliteration: khaDgAdibhishcha shatasho nijaghAna mahAsurAn | pAtayAmAsa chaivAnyAn ghaNTAsvanavimohitAn
verses.translation: and with her sword and other weapons slaughtered the great Asuras in hundreds, and laid others low who were bewitched with the ringing of her bell;
verses.wordMeaning: and with her sword and other weapons slaughtered the great Asuras in hundreds, and laid others low who were bewitched with the ringing of her bell;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and with her sword and other weapons slaughtered the great Asuras in hundreds, and laid others low who were bewitched with the ringing of her bell;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and with her sword and other weapons slaughtered the great Asuras in hundreds, and laid others low who were bewitched with the ringing of her bell;

verses.sanskrit: असुरान् भुवि पाशेन बद्ध्वा चान्यानकर्षयत् । केचिद् द्विधाकृतास्तीक्ष्णैः खड्गपातैस्तथापरे
verses.transliteration: asurAn bhuvi pAshena baddhvA chAnyAnakarShayat | kechid dvidhAkR^itAstIkShNaiH khaDgapAtaistathApare
verses.translation: and binding other Asuras with her noose, she dragged them on the ground. And others again, cloven in twain by sharp slashes of her sword,
verses.wordMeaning: and binding other Asuras with her noose, she dragged them on the ground. And others again, cloven in twain by sharp slashes of her sword,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and binding other Asuras with her noose, she dragged them on the ground. And others again, cloven in twain by sharp slashes of her sword,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and binding other Asuras with her noose, she dragged them on the ground. And others again, cloven in twain by sharp slashes of her sword,

verses.sanskrit: विपोथिता निपातेन गदया भुवि शेरते । वेमुश्च केचिद्रुधिरं मुसलेन भृशं हताः
verses.transliteration: vipothitA nipAtena gadayA bhuvi sherate | vemushcha kechidrudhiraM musalena bhR^ishaM hatAH
verses.translation: and crushed by blows with her mace, lie on the ground; and some, grievously battered by her club, vomited forth blood.
verses.wordMeaning: and crushed by blows with her mace, lie on the ground; and some, grievously battered by her club, vomited forth blood.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and crushed by blows with her mace, lie on the ground; and some, grievously battered by her club, vomited forth blood.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and crushed by blows with her mace, lie on the ground; and some, grievously battered by her club, vomited forth blood.

verses.sanskrit: केचिन्निपतिता भूमौ भिन्नाः शूलेन वक्षसि । निरन्तराः शरौघेण कृताः केचिद्रणाजिरे
verses.transliteration: kechinnipatitA bhUmau bhinnAH shUlena vakShasi | nirantarAH sharaugheNa kR^itAH kechidraNAjire
verses.translation: Some were felled to the ground, pierced in the breast by her trident. Some, being closely massed together, were cut in pieces by the torrent of her arrows in the battle-field.
verses.wordMeaning: Some were felled to the ground, pierced in the breast by her trident. Some, being closely massed together, were cut in pieces by the torrent of her arrows in the battle-field.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Some were felled to the ground, pierced in the breast by her trident. Some, being closely massed together, were cut in pieces by the torrent of her arrows in the battle-field.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Some were felled to the ground, pierced in the breast by her trident. Some, being closely massed together, were cut in pieces by the torrent of her arrows in the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit: श्येनानुकारिणः प्राणान् मुमुचुस्त्रिदशार्दनाः । केषाञ्चिद् बाहवश्छिन्नाश्छिन्नग्रीवास्तथापरे
verses.transliteration: shyenAnukAriNaH prANAn mumuchustridashArdanAH | keShA~nchid bAhavashChinnAshChinnagrIvAstathApare
verses.translation: Following the manner of an army, the afflicters of the thirty gods gave up the ghost; some with their arms cut off, and others with severed necks;
verses.wordMeaning: Following the manner of an army, the afflicters of the thirty gods gave up the ghost; some with their arms cut off, and others with severed necks;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Following the manner of an army, the afflicters of the thirty gods gave up the ghost; some with their arms cut off, and others with severed necks;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Following the manner of an army, the afflicters of the thirty gods gave up the ghost; some with their arms cut off, and others with severed necks;

verses.sanskrit: शिरांसि पेतुरन्येषामन्ये मध्ये विदारिताः । विच्छिन्नजङ्घास्त्वपरे पेतुरुर्व्यां महासुराः
verses.transliteration: shirAMsi peturanyeShAmanye madhye vidAritAH | vichChinnaja~NghAstvapare petururvyAM mahAsurAH
verses.translation: their heads fell from others, others were torn asunder in the middle; and other great Asuras fell to the earth with legs clean cut off;
verses.wordMeaning: their heads fell from others, others were torn asunder in the middle; and other great Asuras fell to the earth with legs clean cut off;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): their heads fell from others, others were torn asunder in the middle; and other great Asuras fell to the earth with legs clean cut off;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): their heads fell from others, others were torn asunder in the middle; and other great Asuras fell to the earth with legs clean cut off;

verses.sanskrit: एकबाह्वक्षिचरणाः केचिद्देव्या द्विधाकृताः । छिन्नेऽपि चान्ये शिरसि पतिताः पुनरुत्थिताः
verses.transliteration: ekabAhvakShicharaNAH kechiddevyA dvidhAkR^itAH | Chinne.api chAnye shirasi patitAH punarutthitAH
verses.translation: some were cloven by the goddess into two parts, with a single arm and eye and foot to each part; and others fell and rose again, although with head cut off.
verses.wordMeaning: some were cloven by the goddess into two parts, with a single arm and eye and foot to each part; and others fell and rose again, although with head cut off.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): some were cloven by the goddess into two parts, with a single arm and eye and foot to each part; and others fell and rose again, although with head cut off.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): some were cloven by the goddess into two parts, with a single arm and eye and foot to each part; and others fell and rose again, although with head cut off.

verses.sanskrit: कबन्धा युयुधुर्देव्या गृहीतपरमायुधाः । ननृतुश्चापरे तत्र युद्धे तूर्यलयाश्रिताः
verses.transliteration: kabandhA yuyudhurdevyA gR^ihItaparamAyudhAH | nanR^itushchApare tatra yuddhe tUryalayAshritAH
verses.translation: Headless corpses, still grasping the finest weapons, fought with the goddess; and others danced there in the battle, keeping time to the strains of the musical instruments.
verses.wordMeaning: Headless corpses, still grasping the finest weapons, fought with the goddess; and others danced there in the battle, keeping time to the strains of the musical instruments.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Headless corpses, still grasping the finest weapons, fought with the goddess; and others danced there in the battle, keeping time to the strains of the musical instruments.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Headless corpses, still grasping the finest weapons, fought with the goddess; and others danced there in the battle, keeping time to the strains of the musical instruments.

verses.sanskrit: कबन्धाश्छिन्नशिरसः खड्गशक्त्यृष्टिपाणयः । तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति भाषन्तो देवीमन्ये महासुराः
verses.transliteration: kabandhAshChinnashirasaH khaDgashaktyR^iShTipANayaH | tiShTha tiShTheti bhAShanto devImanye mahAsurAH
verses.translation: Corpses, with heads severed, still held swords and spears and lances in their hands; and other great Asuras were shouting to the goddess, 'Stand! stand!'
verses.wordMeaning: Corpses, with heads severed, still held swords and spears and lances in their hands; and other great Asuras were shouting to the goddess, 'Stand! stand!'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Corpses, with heads severed, still held swords and spears and lances in their hands; and other great Asuras were shouting to the goddess, 'Stand! stand!'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Corpses, with heads severed, still held swords and spears and lances in their hands; and other great Asuras were shouting to the goddess, 'Stand! stand!'

verses.sanskrit: पातितै रथनागाश्वैरसुरैश्च वसुन्धरा । अगम्या साभवत्तत्र यत्राभूत् स महारणः
verses.transliteration: pAtitai rathanAgAshvairasuraishcha vasundharA | agamyA sAbhavattatra yatrAbhUt sa mahAraNaH
verses.translation: With the prostrate chariots, elephants and horses and Asuras the earth became impassable where that great battle took place.
verses.wordMeaning: With the prostrate chariots, elephants and horses and Asuras the earth became impassable where that great battle took place.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): With the prostrate chariots, elephants and horses and Asuras the earth became impassable where that great battle took place.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): With the prostrate chariots, elephants and horses and Asuras the earth became impassable where that great battle took place.

verses.sanskrit: शोणितौघा महानद्यः सद्यस्तत्र प्रसुस्रुवुः । मध्ये चासुरसैन्यस्य वारणासुरवाजिनाम्
verses.transliteration: shoNitaughA mahAnadyaH sadyastatra prasusruvuH | madhye chAsurasainyasya vAraNAsuravAjinAm
verses.translation: And large rivers formed of torrents of blood straightway flowed along there amidst the armies of Asuras, and among the elephants, Asuras and horses.
verses.wordMeaning: And large rivers formed of torrents of blood straightway flowed along there amidst the armies of Asuras, and among the elephants, Asuras and horses.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And large rivers formed of torrents of blood straightway flowed along there amidst the armies of Asuras, and among the elephants, Asuras and horses.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And large rivers formed of torrents of blood straightway flowed along there amidst the armies of Asuras, and among the elephants, Asuras and horses.

verses.sanskrit: क्षणेन तन्महासैन्यमसुराणां तथाम्बिका । निन्ये क्षयं यथा वह्निस्तृणदारुमहाचयम्
verses.transliteration: kShaNena tanmahAsainyamasurANAM tathAmbikA | ninye kShayaM yathA vahnistR^iNadArumahAchayam
verses.translation: Thus Ambika brought that great army of the Asuras to utter destruction in a moment, even as fire utterly consumes a huge pile of grass and timber.
verses.wordMeaning: Thus Ambika brought that great army of the Asuras to utter destruction in a moment, even as fire utterly consumes a huge pile of grass and timber.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Thus Ambika brought that great army of the Asuras to utter destruction in a moment, even as fire utterly consumes a huge pile of grass and timber.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Thus Ambika brought that great army of the Asuras to utter destruction in a moment, even as fire utterly consumes a huge pile of grass and timber.

verses.sanskrit: स च सिंहो महानादमुत्सृजन् धुतकेसरः । शरीरेभ्योऽमरारीणामसूनिव विचिन्वति
verses.transliteration: sa cha siMho mahAnAdamutsR^ijan dhutakesaraH | sharIrebhyo.amarArINAmasUniva vichinvati
verses.translation: And the lion, with quivering mane, stalked on roaring aloud, prowling as it were for lives out of the bodies of the foes of the Immortals.
verses.wordMeaning: And the lion, with quivering mane, stalked on roaring aloud, prowling as it were for lives out of the bodies of the foes of the Immortals.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And the lion, with quivering mane, stalked on roaring aloud, prowling as it were for lives out of the bodies of the foes of the Immortals.

verses.sanskrit: देव्या गणैश्च तैस्तत्र कृतं युद्धं तथासुरैः । यथैषां तुतुषुर्देवाः पुष्पवृष्टिमुचो दिवि
verses.transliteration: devyA gaNaishcha taistatra kR^itaM yuddhaM tathAsuraiH | yathaiShAM tutuShurdevAH puShpavR^iShTimucho divi
verses.translation: The battle was fought there between those troops of the goddess and the Asuras, so that the gods in heaven, sending down showers of flowers, gratified her.
verses.wordMeaning: The battle was fought there between those troops of the goddess and the Asuras, so that the gods in heaven, sending down showers of flowers, gratified her.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The battle was fought there between those troops of the goddess and the Asuras, so that the gods in heaven, sending down showers of flowers, gratified her.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The battle was fought there between those troops of the goddess and the Asuras, so that the gods in heaven, sending down showers of flowers, gratified her.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ ऋषिरुवाच
verses.transliteration: OM R^iShiruvAcha
verses.translation: Om. The rishi spoke:
verses.wordMeaning: Om. The rishi spoke:
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Om. The rishi spoke:
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Om. The rishi spoke:

verses.sanskrit: निहन्यमानं तत्सैन्यमवलोक्य महासुरः । सेनानीश्चिक्षुरः कोपाद्ययौ योद्धुमथाम्बिकाम्
verses.transliteration: nihanyamAnaM tatsainyamavalokya mahAsuraH | senAnIshchikShuraH kopAdyayau yoddhumathAmbikAm
verses.translation: Now the great Asura, the general Chikshura, seeing that army being slaughtered, advanced in wrath to fight with Ambika.
verses.wordMeaning: Now the great Asura, the general Chikshura, seeing that army being slaughtered, advanced in wrath to fight with Ambika.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Now the great Asura, the general Chikshura, seeing that army being slaughtered, advanced in wrath to fight with Ambika.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Now the great Asura, the general Chikshura, seeing that army being slaughtered, advanced in wrath to fight with Ambika.

verses.sanskrit: स देवीं शरवर्षेण ववर्ष समरेऽसुरः । यथा मेरुगिरेः शृङ्गं तोयवर्षेण तोयदः
verses.transliteration: sa devIM sharavarSheNa vavarSha samare.asuraH | yathA merugireH shR^i~NgaM toyavarSheNa toyadaH
verses.translation: The Asura rained a shower of arrows on the goddess in the battle, as a cloud deluges mount Meru's summit with a shower of rain.
verses.wordMeaning: The Asura rained a shower of arrows on the goddess in the battle, as a cloud deluges mount Meru's summit with a shower of rain.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The Asura rained a shower of arrows on the goddess in the battle, as a cloud deluges mount Meru's summit with a shower of rain.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The Asura rained a shower of arrows on the goddess in the battle, as a cloud deluges mount Meru's summit with a shower of rain.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य छित्वा ततो देवी लीलयैव शरोत्करान् । जघान तुरगान्बाणैर्यन्तारं चैव वाजिनाम्
verses.transliteration: tasya ChitvA tato devI lIlayaiva sharotkarAn | jaghAna turagAnbANairyantAraM chaiva vAjinAm
verses.translation: The goddess, cutting asunder the masses of his arrows then as it were in play, smote his horses with her arrows and their charioteer;
verses.wordMeaning: The goddess, cutting asunder the masses of his arrows then as it were in play, smote his horses with her arrows and their charioteer;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The goddess, cutting asunder the masses of his arrows then as it were in play, smote his horses with her arrows and their charioteer;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The goddess, cutting asunder the masses of his arrows then as it were in play, smote his horses with her arrows and their charioteer;

verses.sanskrit: चिच्छेद च धनुः सद्यो ध्वजं चातिसमुच्छृतम् । विव्याध चैव गात्रेषु छिन्नधन्वानमाशुगैः
verses.transliteration: chichCheda cha dhanuH sadyo dhvajaM chAtisamuchChR^itam | vivyAdha chaiva gAtreShu ChinnadhanvAnamAshugaiH
verses.translation: and split his bow forthwith and his banner raised high aloft; and with swift missiles pierced his limbs as he stood with shattered bow.
verses.wordMeaning: and split his bow forthwith and his banner raised high aloft; and with swift missiles pierced his limbs as he stood with shattered bow.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and split his bow forthwith and his banner raised high aloft; and with swift missiles pierced his limbs as he stood with shattered bow.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and split his bow forthwith and his banner raised high aloft; and with swift missiles pierced his limbs as he stood with shattered bow.

verses.sanskrit: सच्छिन्नधन्वा विरथो हताश्वो हतसारथिः । अभ्यधावत तां देवीं खड्गचर्मधरोऽसुरः
verses.transliteration: sachChinnadhanvA viratho hatAshvo hatasArathiH | abhyadhAvata tAM devIM khaDgacharmadharo.asuraH
verses.translation: His bow shattered, his chariot useless, his horses killed, his charioteer slain, the Asura armed with sword and shield rushed at the goddess.
verses.wordMeaning: His bow shattered, his chariot useless, his horses killed, his charioteer slain, the Asura armed with sword and shield rushed at the goddess.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): His bow shattered, his chariot useless, his horses killed, his charioteer slain, the Asura armed with sword and shield rushed at the goddess.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): His bow shattered, his chariot useless, his horses killed, his charioteer slain, the Asura armed with sword and shield rushed at the goddess.

verses.sanskrit: सिंहमाहत्य खड्गेन तीक्ष्णधारेण मूर्धनि । आजघान भुजे सव्ये देवीमप्यतिवेगवान्
verses.transliteration: siMhamAhatya khaDgena tIkShNadhAreNa mUrdhani | AjaghAna bhuje savye devImapyativegavAn
verses.translation: With the utmost celerity he smote the lion on the head with his sharp-edged sword, and struck the goddess also on her left arm.
verses.wordMeaning: With the utmost celerity he smote the lion on the head with his sharp-edged sword, and struck the goddess also on her left arm.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): With the utmost celerity he smote the lion on the head with his sharp-edged sword, and struck the goddess also on her left arm.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): With the utmost celerity he smote the lion on the head with his sharp-edged sword, and struck the goddess also on her left arm.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याः खड्गो भुजं प्राप्य पफाल नृपनन्दन । ततो जग्राह शूलं स कोपादरुणलोचनः
verses.transliteration: tasyAH khaDgo bhujaM prApya paphAla nR^ipanandana | tato jagrAha shUlaM sa kopAdaruNalochanaH
verses.translation: His sword shivered to pieces as it touched her arm, O prince. Thereon, red-eyed with anger, he grasped his pike,
verses.wordMeaning: His sword shivered to pieces as it touched her arm, O prince. Thereon, red-eyed with anger, he grasped his pike,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): His sword shivered to pieces as it touched her arm, O prince. Thereon, red-eyed with anger, he grasped his pike,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): His sword shivered to pieces as it touched her arm, O prince. Thereon, red-eyed with anger, he grasped his pike,

verses.sanskrit: चिक्षेप च ततस्तत्तु भद्रकाल्यां महासुरः । जाज्वल्यमानं तेजोभी रविबिम्बमिवाम्बरात्
verses.transliteration: chikShepa cha tatastattu bhadrakAlyAM mahAsuraH | jAjvalyamAnaM tejobhI ravibimbamivAmbarAt
verses.translation: and he, the great Asura, flung it at Bhadrakali, as it were the Sun's orb blazing brightly with its splendour from out the sky.
verses.wordMeaning: and he, the great Asura, flung it at Bhadrakali, as it were the Sun's orb blazing brightly with its splendour from out the sky.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and he, the great Asura, flung it at Bhadrakali, as it were the Sun's orb blazing brightly with its splendour from out the sky.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and he, the great Asura, flung it at Bhadrakali, as it were the Sun's orb blazing brightly with its splendour from out the sky.

verses.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा तदापतच्छूलं देवी शूलममुञ्चत । तेन तच्छतधा नीतं शूलं स च महासुरः
verses.transliteration: dR^iShTvA tadApatachChUlaM devI shUlamamu~nchata | tena tachChatadhA nItaM shUlaM sa cha mahAsuraH
verses.translation: Seeing that pike falling on her, the goddess hurled her pike, and it shattered that pike into a hundred fragments and the great Asura also.
verses.wordMeaning: Seeing that pike falling on her, the goddess hurled her pike, and it shattered that pike into a hundred fragments and the great Asura also.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Seeing that pike falling on her, the goddess hurled her pike, and it shattered that pike into a hundred fragments and the great Asura also.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Seeing that pike falling on her, the goddess hurled her pike, and it shattered that pike into a hundred fragments and the great Asura also.

verses.sanskrit: हते तस्मिन्महावीर्ये महिषस्य चमूपतौ । आजगाम गजारूढश्चामरस्त्रिदशार्दनः
verses.transliteration: hate tasminmahAvIrye mahiShasya chamUpatau | AjagAma gajArUDhashchAmarastridashArdanaH
verses.translation: When he, Mahisha's very valiant general, was slain, Chamara, the afflicter of the thirty gods, advanced mounted on an elephant;
verses.wordMeaning: When he, Mahisha's very valiant general, was slain, Chamara, the afflicter of the thirty gods, advanced mounted on an elephant;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): When he, Mahisha's very valiant general, was slain, Chamara, the afflicter of the thirty gods, advanced mounted on an elephant;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): When he, Mahisha's very valiant general, was slain, Chamara, the afflicter of the thirty gods, advanced mounted on an elephant;

verses.sanskrit: सोऽपि शक्तिं मुमोचाथ देव्यास्तामम्बिका द्रुतम् । हुङ्काराभिहतां भूमौ पातयामास निष्प्रभाम्
verses.transliteration: so.api shaktiM mumochAtha devyAstAmambikA drutam | hu~NkArAbhihatAM bhUmau pAtayAmAsa niShprabhAm
verses.translation: and he also hurled his spear at the goddess. Down to the ground Ambika quickly struck it, assailed with a contemptuous hoot and rendered lustreless.
verses.wordMeaning: and he also hurled his spear at the goddess. Down to the ground Ambika quickly struck it, assailed with a contemptuous hoot and rendered lustreless.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and he also hurled his spear at the goddess. Down to the ground Ambika quickly struck it, assailed with a contemptuous hoot and rendered lustreless.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and he also hurled his spear at the goddess. Down to the ground Ambika quickly struck it, assailed with a contemptuous hoot and rendered lustreless.

verses.sanskrit: भग्नां शक्तिं निपतितां दृष्ट्वा क्रोधसमन्वितः । चिक्षेप चामरः शूलं बाणैस्तदपि साच्छिनत्
verses.transliteration: bhagnAM shaktiM nipatitAM dR^iShTvA krodhasamanvitaH | chikShepa chAmaraH shUlaM bANaistadapi sAchChinat
verses.translation: Seeing his spear broken and fallen, Chamara filled with rage flung a pike; and that she split with her arrows.
verses.wordMeaning: Seeing his spear broken and fallen, Chamara filled with rage flung a pike; and that she split with her arrows.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Seeing his spear broken and fallen, Chamara filled with rage flung a pike; and that she split with her arrows.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Seeing his spear broken and fallen, Chamara filled with rage flung a pike; and that she split with her arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सिंहः समुत्पत्य गजकुम्भान्तरे स्थितः । बाहुयुद्धेन युयुधे तेनोच्चैस्त्रिदशारिणा
verses.transliteration: tataH siMhaH samutpatya gajakumbhAntare sthitaH | bAhuyuddhena yuyudhe tenochchaistridashAriNA
verses.translation: Then the lion, leaping up, fastened on to the hollow of the elephant's forehead, and fought in close combat aloft with that foe of the thirty gods;
verses.wordMeaning: Then the lion, leaping up, fastened on to the hollow of the elephant's forehead, and fought in close combat aloft with that foe of the thirty gods;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then the lion, leaping up, fastened on to the hollow of the elephant's forehead, and fought in close combat aloft with that foe of the thirty gods;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then the lion, leaping up, fastened on to the hollow of the elephant's forehead, and fought in close combat aloft with that foe of the thirty gods;

verses.sanskrit: युध्यमानौ ततस्तौ तु तस्मान्नागान्महीं गतौ । युयुधातेऽतिसंरब्धौ प्रहारैरतिदारुणैः
verses.transliteration: yudhyamAnau tatastau tu tasmAnnAgAnmahIM gatau | yuyudhAte.atisaMrabdhau prahArairatidAruNaiH
verses.translation: but both then fell, as they were fighting, from the elephant to the ground. They fought closely locked together with most terrible blows.
verses.wordMeaning: but both then fell, as they were fighting, from the elephant to the ground. They fought closely locked together with most terrible blows.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): but both then fell, as they were fighting, from the elephant to the ground. They fought closely locked together with most terrible blows.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): but both then fell, as they were fighting, from the elephant to the ground. They fought closely locked together with most terrible blows.

verses.sanskrit: ततो वेगात् खमुत्पत्य निपत्य च मृगारिणा । करप्रहारेण शिरश्चामरस्य पृथक् कृतम्
verses.transliteration: tato vegAt khamutpatya nipatya cha mR^igAriNA | karaprahAreNa shirashchAmarasya pR^ithak kR^itam
verses.translation: Then, quickly springing up to the sky, and descending, the lion severed Chamara's head with a blow from his paw.
verses.wordMeaning: Then, quickly springing up to the sky, and descending, the lion severed Chamara's head with a blow from his paw.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then, quickly springing up to the sky, and descending, the lion severed Chamara's head with a blow from his paw.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then, quickly springing up to the sky, and descending, the lion severed Chamara's head with a blow from his paw.

verses.sanskrit: उदग्रश्च रणे देव्या शिलावृक्षादिभिर्हतः । दन्तमुष्टितलैश्चैव करालश्च निपातितः
verses.transliteration: udagrashcha raNe devyA shilAvR^ikShAdibhirhataH | dantamuShTitalaishchaiva karAlashcha nipAtitaH
verses.translation: And Udagra was slain in battle by the goddess with stones, trees and other things, and Karala also was stricken down by her teeth and fists and feet.
verses.wordMeaning: And Udagra was slain in battle by the goddess with stones, trees and other things, and Karala also was stricken down by her teeth and fists and feet.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And Udagra was slain in battle by the goddess with stones, trees and other things, and Karala also was stricken down by her teeth and fists and feet.

verses.sanskrit: देवी क्रुद्धा गदापातैश्चूर्णयामास चोद्धतम् । बाष्कलं भिन्दिपालेन बाणैस्ताम्रं तथान्धकम्
verses.transliteration: devI kruddhA gadApAtaishchUrNayAmAsa choddhatam | bAShkalaM bhindipAlena bANaistAmraM tathAndhakam
verses.translation: And the goddess, enraged, ground Uddhata to powder with blows from her club; and killed Bashkala with a dart, and Tamra and Andhaka with arrows.
verses.wordMeaning: And the goddess, enraged, ground Uddhata to powder with blows from her club; and killed Bashkala with a dart, and Tamra and Andhaka with arrows.

verses.transliteration: ugrAsyamugravIryaM cha tathaiva cha mahAhanum | trinetrA cha trishUlena jaghAna parameshvarI
verses.translation: And the supreme three-eyed goddess slew Ugrasya and Ugravirya and Mahahanu also with her trident.
verses.wordMeaning: And the supreme three-eyed goddess slew Ugrasya and Ugravirya and Mahahanu also with her trident.

verses.sanskrit: बिडालस्यासिना कायात् पातयामास वै शिरः । दुर्धरं दुर्मुखं चोभौ शरैर्निन्ये यमक्षयम्
verses.transliteration: biDAlasyAsinA kAyAt pAtayAmAsa vai shiraH | durdharaM durmukhaM chobhau sharairninye yamakShayam
verses.translation: With her sword she struck Bidala's head clean down from his body. She despatched both Durdhara and Durmukha to Yama's abode with her arrows.

verses.sanskrit: एवं सङ्क्षीयमाणे तु स्वसैन्ये महिषासुरः । माहिषेण स्वरूपेण त्रासयामास तान् गणान्
verses.transliteration: evaM sa~NkShIyamANe tu svasainye mahiShAsuraH | mAhiSheNa svarUpeNa trAsayAmAsa tAn gaNAn
verses.translation: Now, as his army was being thus destroyed utterly, the Asura Mahisha in his own buffalo-shape terrified her troops.

verses.sanskrit: कांश्चित्तुण्डप्रहारेण खुरक्षेपैस्तथापरान् । लाङ्गूलताडितांश्चान्यान् शृङ्गाभ्यां च विदारितान्
verses.transliteration: kAMshchittuNDaprahAreNa khurakShepaistathAparAn | lA~NgUlatADitAMshchAnyAn shR^i~NgAbhyAM cha vidAritAn
verses.translation: Some he laid low by a blow from his muzzle, and others by stamping with his hooves, and others because they were lashed with his tail and gashed with his horns,

verses.sanskrit: वेगेन कांश्चिदपरान्नादेन भ्रमणेन च । निःश्वासपवनेनान्यान्पातयामास भूतले
verses.transliteration: vegena kAMshchidaparAnnAdena bhramaNena cha | niHshvAsapavanenAnyAnpAtayAmAsa bhUtale
verses.translation: and others again by his impetuous rush, his bellowing and his wheeling career, and others by the blast of his breath—thus he laid them low on the face of the earth.

verses.sanskrit: निपात्य प्रमथानीकमभ्यधावत सोऽसुरः । सिंहं हन्तुं महादेव्याः कोपं चक्रे ततोऽम्बिका
verses.transliteration: nipAtya pramathAnIkamabhyadhAvata so.asuraH | siMhaM hantuM mahAdevyAH kopaM chakre tato.ambikA
verses.translation: Having laid low the van of her army, the Asura rushed to attack the great goddess' lion. Thereat Ambika displayed her wrath.
verses.wordMeaning: Having laid low the van of her army, the Asura rushed to attack the great goddess' lion. Thereat Ambika displayed her wrath.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽपि कोपान्महावीर्यः खुरक्षुण्णमहीतलः । शृङ्गाभ्यां पर्वतानुच्चांश्चिक्षेप च ननाद च
verses.transliteration: so.api kopAnmahAvIryaH khurakShuNNamahItalaH | shR^i~NgAbhyAM parvatAnuchchAMshchikShepa cha nanAda cha
verses.translation: And he, great in valour, pounding the surface of the earth with his hooves in his rage, tossed the mountains aloft with his horns and bellowed.

verses.sanskrit: वेगभ्रमणविक्षुण्णा मही तस्य व्यशीर्यत । लाङ्गूलेनाहतश्चाब्धिः प्लावयामास सर्वतः

verses.translation: Crushed by his impetuous wheelings the earth crumbled to pieces; and the sea, lashed by his tail, overflowed in every direction;

verses.sanskrit: धुतशृङ्गविभिन्नाश्च खण्डं खण्डं ययुर्घनाः । श्वासानिलास्ताः शतशो निपेतुर्नभसोऽचलाः
verses.transliteration: dhutashR^i~NgavibhinnAshcha khaNDaM khaNDaM yayurghanAH | shvAsAnilAstAH shatasho nipeturnabhaso.achalAH
verses.translation: and the clouds, pierced by his swaying horns, were rent to fragments; mountains fell in hundreds from the sky, being cast down by the blast of his breath.

verses.sanskrit: इति क्रोधसमाध्मातमापतन्तं महासुरम् । दृष्ट्वा सा चण्डिका कोपं तद्वधाय तदाकरोत्
verses.transliteration: iti krodhasamAdhmAtamApatantaM mahAsuram | dR^iShTvA sA chaNDikA kopaM tadvadhAya tadAkarot
verses.translation: Chandika looked on the great Asura, as swollen with rage he rushed on, and gave way to her wrath then in order to slay him.

verses.transliteration: tataH siMho.abhavatsadyo yAvattasyAmbikA shiraH | Chinatti tAvat puruShaH khaDgapANiradR^ishyata
verses.translation: and then became a lion suddenly. While Ambika is cutting off his head, he took the appearance of a man with scymitar in hand.

verses.transliteration: tata evAshu puruShaM devI chichCheda sAyakaiH | taM khaDgacharmaNA sArdhaM tataH so.abhUnmahAgajaH
verses.translation: Straightway the goddess with her arrows swiftly pierced the man together with his scymitar and shield. Then he became a huge elephant,

verses.transliteration: kareNa cha mahAsiMhaM taM chakarSha jagarja cha | karShatastu karaM devI khaDgena nirakR^intata
verses.translation: and tugged at her great lion with his trunk and roared, but the goddess cut off his trunk with her sword as he made his tugs.

verses.transliteration: tato mahAsuro bhUyo mAhiShaM vapurAsthitaH | tathaiva kShobhayAmAsa trailokyaM sacharAcharam
verses.translation: Next the great Asura assumed his buffalo shape again, and so shook the three worlds with all that is moveable and immoveable therein.

verses.transliteration: tataH kruddhA jaganmAtA chaNDikA pAnamuttamam | papau punaH punashchaiva jahAsAruNalochanA
verses.translation: Enraged thereat, Chandika, the mother of the world, quaffed a sublime beverage again and again, and laughed as her eyes gleamed ruddy.

verses.sanskrit: ननर्द चासुरः सोऽपि बलवीर्यमदोद्धतः । विषाणाभ्यां च चिक्षेप चण्डिकां प्रति भूधरान्
verses.transliteration: nanarda chAsuraH so.api balavIryamadoddhataH | viShANAbhyAM cha chikShepa chaNDikAM prati bhUdharAn
verses.translation: And the Asura roared out, puffed up with his strength and valour and frenzy, and hurled mountains against Chandika with his horns.

verses.transliteration: sA cha tAnprahitAMstena chUrNayantI sharotkaraiH | uvAcha taM madoddhUtamukharAgAkulAkSharam
verses.translation: And she, shivering to atoms with showers of arrows those mountains that he hurled, spoke to him in confused words, while her mouth was rendered ruddier by the mead that she had drunk.

verses.transliteration: devyuvAcha
verses.translation: The goddess spoke:

verses.sanskrit: गर्ज गर्ज क्षणं मूढ मधु यावत्पिबाम्यहम् । मया त्वयि हतेऽत्रैव गर्जिष्यन्त्याशु देवताः
verses.transliteration: garja garja kShaNaM mUDha madhu yAvatpibAmyaham | mayA tvayi hate.atraiva garjiShyantyAshu devatAH
verses.translation: Roar, roar on thy brief moment, O fool, the while I quaff this mead! The gods shall soon roar, when I shall slay thee even here.
verses.hindi: हे दुर्गे! संकट में स्मरण करने पर तुम सभी प्राणियों का भय हर लेती हो; स्वस्थ अवस्था में स्मरण करने पर उत्कृष्ट शुभ बुद्धि देती हो। हे दारिद्र्य-दुःख-भय-हारिणी! सबके उपकार के लिए सदा आर्द्र चित्त वाली तुम्हारे सिवाय और कौन है?
verses.wordMeaning: Mahishasura — the buffalo-demon — is tamas embodied: the heavy, dark, stubborn inertia that refuses to yield to light. But this verse reveals why the Devi's victory matters: she is not merely a warrior. She is "sadā ārdrа-cittā" — always soft-hearted, ever moist with compassion. The fierceness that slays Mahishasura and the tenderness that weeps for suffering are one and the same being. Durga integrates what we typically split: strength and softness, ferocity and compassion.
verses.explanation: Mahishasura — the buffalo-demon — is tamas embodied: the heavy, dark, stubborn inertia that refuses to yield to light. But this verse reveals why the Devi's victory matters: she is not merely a warrior. She is "sadā ārdrа-cittā" — always soft-hearted, ever moist with compassion. The fierceness that slays Mahishasura and the tenderness that weeps for suffering are one and the same being. Durga integrates what we typically split: strength and softness, ferocity and compassion.
verses.science: Research on "tender-minded vs. tough-minded" leadership (James MacGregor Burns): the most effective transformational leaders combine high challenge (demanding excellence, confronting hard truths) with high support (genuine care, emotional warmth). Neither alone produces transformation. The Devi's combination of fierce demon-slaying and "ārdra citta" (moist compassion) is the mythic template of this paradox.
verses.lifeLesson: Where in your life do you split strength from softness — believing you must choose between being fierce and being kind? The Devi says: the highest form of each requires the other. Your compassion without fierceness is sentimentality; your fierceness without compassion is cruelty. Cultivate both, simultaneously. That integration is Durga.
verses.commentary: Mahishasura — the buffalo-demon — is tamas embodied: the heavy, dark, stubborn inertia that refuses to yield to light. But this verse reveals why the Devi's victory matters: she is not merely a warrior. She is "sadā ārdrа-cittā" — always soft-hearted, ever moist with compassion. The fierceness that slays Mahishasura and the tenderness that weeps for suffering are one and the same being. Durga integrates what we typically split: strength and softness, ferocity and compassion.

verses.translation: Exclaiming thus she leaped upwards and sat herself on that great Asura, and kicked him on the neck with her foot and struck him with her spear.

verses.sanskrit: शक्रादयः सुरगणा निहतेऽतिवीर्ये तस्मिन्दुरात्मनि सुरारिबले च देव्या । तां तुष्टुवुः प्रणतिनम्रशिरोधरांसा वाग्भिः प्रहर्षपुलकोद्गमचारुदेहाः
verses.transliteration: shakrAdayaH suragaNA nihate.ativIrye tasmindurAtmani surAribale cha devyA | tAM tuShTuvuH praNatinamrashirodharAMsA vAgbhiH praharShapulakod.hgamachArudehAH
verses.translation: When that most valiant evil-souled army of the gods' foes was vanquished by the goddess, Shakra and the hosts of other gods poured forth their praises to her with their voices, reverently bending down their necks and shoulders, while their bodies looked handsome because their hair stood erect with exultation.

verses.sanskrit: देव्या यया ततमिदं जगदात्मशक्त्या निःशेषदेवगणशक्तिसमूहमूर्त्या । तामम्बिकामखिलदेवमहर्षिपूज्यां भक्त्या नताः स्म विदधातु शुभानि सा नः

verses.translation: The goddess, who stretched out this world by her power, whose body comprises the entire powers of all the hosts of gods—her, Ambika, worthy of worship by all gods and great rishis, we bow before in faith; may she ordain blessings for us!

verses.sanskrit: यस्याः प्रभावमतुलं भगवाननन्तो ब्रह्मा हरश्च न हि वक्तुमलं बलं च । सा चण्डिकाखिलजगत्परिपालनाय नाशाय चाशुभभयस्य मतिं करोतु
verses.transliteration: yasyAH prabhAvamatulaM bhagavAnananto brahmA harashcha na hi vaktumalaM balaM cha | sA chaNDikAkhilajagatparipAlanAya nAshAya chAshubhabhayasya matiM karotu
verses.translation: May she, whose peerless majesty and power the Adorable Ananta, Brahma and Hara cannot in sooth declare—may she, Chandika, to protect the entire world and to destroy the fear of evil turn her mind!
verses.hindi: हे सब मंगलों की मंगलरूपे! हे शिवे! हे सम्पूर्ण अर्थों की साधिके! हे शरण देने वाली! हे त्र्यम्बके! हे गौरि! हे नारायणि! तुम्हें नमस्कार है।
verses.wordMeaning: The opening verse of the Shakradi Stuti — the most beloved daily prayer of the Shakta tradition. Eight names, each revealing a different face of the same reality: Mangala (all good), Shiva (benevolent), Sarvarthasadhike (the one who accomplishes all purposes), Sharanye (the refuge), Tryambake (the three-eyed), Gauri (the luminous), Narayani (the energy of Narayana). The Devi is simultaneously gentle and all-powerful; she is the refuge and the force. This prayer teaches the paradox at the heart of Shakti: absolute power held in absolute tenderness.

The Devi is simultaneously gentle and all-powerful; she is the refuge and the force. This prayer teaches the paradox at the heart of Shakti: absolute power held in absolute tenderness.
verses.science: Research on the psychological benefits of surrender (ACT therapy, compassion-focused therapy): genuine surrender to something larger than the ego — a higher purpose, the natural order, or the divine — is associated with significant reductions in anxiety, depression, and the exhaustion of constant self-reliance. "Sharanye" (the refuge) is the psychological state research calls "safe haven." The Devi Stuti is structured access to that state.
verses.lifeLesson: Recite or slowly read this verse — not as ritual but as genuine surrender. Say: "I am not in control of everything. I take refuge in the force that sustains all good, accomplishes all purposes, and shelters all who approach." That act of genuine surrender — even once — releases a kind of tension that willpower can never release.

verses.sanskrit: या श्रीः स्वयं सुकृतिनां भवनेष्वलक्ष्मीः पापात्मनां कृतधियां हृदयेषु बुद्धिः । श्रद्धा सतां कुलजनप्रभवस्य लज्जा तां त्वां नताः स्म परिपालय देवि विश्वम्
verses.transliteration: yA shrIH svayaM sukR^itinAM bhavaneShvalakShmIH pApAtmanAM kR^itadhiyAM hR^idayeShu buddhiH | shraddhA satAM kulajanaprabhavasya lajjA tAM tvAM natAH sma paripAlaya devi vishvam
verses.translation: Her, who is Good Fortune herself in the dwellings of men of good deeds, Ill Fortune in those of men of sinful souls; who is Intelligence in the hearts of the prudent, who is Faith in those of the good, and Modesty in that of the high-born man—her, even thee, we bow before; protect the universe, O goddess!

verses.translation: Can we describe this thy thought-transcending form? Or thy abundant surpassing valour that destroyed the Asuras? Or thy surpassing feats which were displayed in battles among all the hosts of Asuras, gods and others, O goddess?

verses.sanskrit: हेतुः समस्तजगतां त्रिगुणापि दोषै- र्न ज्ञायसे हरिहरादिभिरप्यपारा । सर्वाश्रयाखिलमिदं जगदंशभूत- मव्याकृता हि परमा प्रकृतिस्त्वमाद्या
verses.transliteration: hetuH samastajagatAM triguNApi doShai\- rna j~nAyase hariharAdibhirapyapArA | sarvAshrayAkhilamidaM jagadaMshabhUta\- mavyAkR^itA hi paramA prakR^itistvamAdyA
verses.translation: Thou art the cause of all the worlds! Though characterized by the three qualities, by faults thou art not known! Even by Hari, Hara and the other gods thou art incomprehensible! Thou art the resort of all; thou art this entire world which is composed of parts! Thou verily art sublime original Nature untransformed!

verses.sanskrit: यस्याः समस्तसुरता समुदीरणेन तृप्तिं प्रयाति सकलेषु मखेषु देवि । स्वाहासि वै पितृगणस्य च तृप्तिहेतु- रुच्चार्यसे त्वमत एव जनैः स्वधा च

verses.sanskrit: या मुक्तिहेतुरविचिन्त्यमहाव्रता त्वं अभ्यस्यसे सुनियतेन्द्रियतत्त्वसारैः । मोक्षार्थिभिर्मुनिभिरस्तसमस्तदोषै- र्विद्यासि सा भगवती परमा हि देवि
verses.transliteration: yA muktiheturavichintyamahAvratA tvaM abhyasyase suniyatendriyatattvasAraiH | mokShArthibhirmunibhirastasamastadoShai\- rvidyAsi sA bhagavatI paramA hi devi
verses.translation: Thou art she who effects final emancipation, and performs great thought-transcending penances! Thou art studied by munis who seek final emancipation, who have shed all their faults, with their organs, which are the essence of strength, well-restrained! Thou art The Knowledge, adorable, sublime in sooth, O goddess!

verses.transliteration: shabdAtmikA suvimalargyajuShAM nidhAna\- mudgItharamyapadapAThavatAM cha sAmnAm | devi trayI bhagavatI bhavabhAvanAya vArtAsi sarvajagatAM paramArtihantrI
verses.translation: Sound is thy soul! Thou art the repository of the most spotless ric and yajus hymns, and of the samans, which have the charming-worded texts of the Udgitha! Thou as goddess art the triple Veda, the adorable, and for the existence and production of all the worlds art active; thou art the supreme destroyer of their pains!

verses.transliteration: medhAsi devi viditAkhilashAstrasArA durgAsi durgabhavasAgaranaurasa~NgA | shrIH kaiTabhArihR^idayaikakR^itAdhivAsA gaurI tvameva shashimaulikR^itapratiShThA
verses.translation: Thou art Mental Vigour, O goddess! Thou hast comprehended the essence of all the Scriptures! Thou art Durga, the boat to cross the difficult ocean of existence, devoid of attachments! Thou art Shri, who has planted her dominion alone in the heart of Kaitabha's foe! Thou indeed art Gauri, who has fixed her dwelling in the moon-crested god!

verses.sanskrit: ईषत्सहासममलं परिपूर्णचन्द्र- बिम्बानुकारि कनकोत्तमकान्तिकान्तम् । अत्यद्भुतं प्रहृतमात्तरुषा तथापि वक्त्रं विलोक्य सहसा महिषासुरेण
verses.transliteration: IShatsahAsamamalaM paripUrNachandra\- bimbAnukAri kanakottamakAntikAntam | atyadbhutaM prahR^itamAttaruShA tathApi vaktraM vilokya sahasA mahiShAsureNa
verses.translation: Slightly smiling, spotless, resembling the full moon's orb, beautiful as the choicest gold, and lovely was thy face! Yet it was very marvellous that, being swayed by anger, the Asura Mahisha suddenly smote thy face when he saw it.

verses.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा तु देवि कुपितं भ्रुकुटीकराल- मुद्यच्छशाङ्कसदृशच्छवि यन्न सद्यः । प्राणान् मुमोच महिषस्तदतीव चित्रं कैर्जीव्यते हि कुपितान्तकदर्शनेन
verses.transliteration: dR^iShTvA tu devi kupitaM bhrukuTIkarAla\- mudyachChashA~NkasadR^ishachChavi yanna sadyaH | prANAn mumocha mahiShastadatIva chitraM kairjIvyate hi kupitAntakadarshanena
verses.translation: But after seeing thy wrathful face, O goddess, terrible with its frowns, and sheeny in hue like the rising moon, that Mahisha did not forthwith yield up his life—it was passing wonderful! For who can live after beholding the King of Death enraged?
verses.wordMeaning: But after seeing thy wrathful face, O goddess, terrible with its frowns, and sheeny in hue like the rising moon, that Mahisha did not forthwith yield up his life—it was passing wonderful! For who can live after beholding the King of Death enraged?

verses.sanskrit: देवि प्रसीद परमा भवती भवाय सद्यो विनाशयसि कोपवती कुलानि । विज्ञातमेतदधुनैव यदस्तमेत- न्नीतं बलं सुविपुलं महिषासुरस्य
verses.transliteration: devi prasIda paramA bhavatI bhavAya sadyo vinAshayasi kopavatI kulAni | vij~nAtametadadhunaiva yadastameta\- nnItaM balaM suvipulaM mahiShAsurasya
verses.translation: Be gracious, O goddess, as supreme lady, to life! When enraged thou dost forthwith destroy whole families! Known at this very moment is this, that here is brought to its end the Asura Mahisha's most extensive might!

verses.sanskrit: ते सम्मता जनपदेषु धनानि तेषां तेषां यशांसि न च सीदति बन्धुवर्गः । धन्यास्त एव निभृतात्मजभृत्यदारा येषां सदाभ्युदयदा भवती प्रसन्ना
verses.transliteration: te sammatA janapadeShu dhanAni teShAM teShAM yashAMsi na cha sIdati bandhuvargaH | dhanyAsta eva nibhR^itAtmajabhR^ityadArA yeShAM sadAbhyudayadA bhavatI prasannA
verses.translation: Esteemed are they among the nations, theirs are riches, theirs are glories, and their sum of righteousness perishes not; happy are they indeed, and they possess devoted children, servants and wives, on whom thou, well-pleased, dost always bestow prosperity, O lady!

verses.sanskrit: धर्म्याणि देवि सकलानि सदैव कर्मा- ण्यत्यादृतः प्रतिदिनं सुकृती करोति । स्वर्गं प्रयाति च ततो भवती प्रसादा- ल्लोकत्रयेऽपि फलदा ननु देवि तेन
verses.transliteration: dharmyANi devi sakalAni sadaiva karmA\- NyatyAdR^itaH pratidinaM sukR^itI karoti | svargaM prayAti cha tato bhavatI prasAdA\- llokatraye.api phaladA nanu devi tena
verses.translation: All righteous actions ever indeed, O goddess, with utmost respect the man of good deeds daily performs, and gains heaven thereafter by thy favour, O lady. Dost thou not by him bestow rewards even on the three worlds, O goddess?

verses.sanskrit: दुर्गे स्मृता हरसि भीतिमशेषजन्तोः स्वस्थैः स्मृता मतिमतीव शुभां ददासि । दारिद्र्यदुःखभयहारिणि का त्वदन्या सर्वोपकारकरणाय सदार्द्रचित्ता
verses.transliteration: durge smR^itA harasi bhItimasheShajantoH svasthaiH smR^itA matimatIva shubhAM dadAsi | dAridryaduHkhabhayahAriNi kA tvadanyA sarvopakArakaraNAya sadArdrachittA
verses.translation: Thou, O Durga, when called to mind, dost remove terror from every creature! Thou, when called to mind by those in health, dost bestow a mind extremely bright! What goddess but thou, O dispeller of poverty, pain and fear, has ever benevolent thoughts in order to work benefits to all?

verses.sanskrit: एभिर्हतैर्जगदुपैति सुखं तथैते कुर्वन्तु नाम नरकाय चिराय पापम् । सङ्ग्राममृत्युमधिगम्य दिवं प्रयान्तु मत्वेति नूनमहितान्विनिहंसि देवि
verses.transliteration: ebhirhatairjagadupaiti sukhaM tathaite kurvantu nAma narakAya chirAya pApam | sa~NgrAmamR^ityumadhigamya divaM prayAntu matveti nUnamahitAnvinihaMsi devi
verses.translation: By these slain foes the world attains to happiness; thus let these forsooth practise sin so as to descend to hell for long! 'Meeting death in battle let them proceed to heaven'—thinking thus, thou dost assuredly destroy the enemies, O goddess!
verses.wordMeaning: By these slain foes the world attains to happiness; thus let these forsooth practise sin so as to descend to hell for long! 'Meeting death in battle let them proceed to heaven'—thinking thus, thou dost assuredly destroy the enemies, O goddess!

verses.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वैव किं न भवती प्रकरोति भस्म सर्वासुरानरिषु यत्प्रहिणोषि शस्त्रम् । लोकान्प्रयान्तु रिपवोऽपि हि शस्त्रपूता इत्थं मतिर्भवति तेष्वहितेषुसाध्वी
verses.transliteration: dR^iShTvaiva kiM na bhavatI prakaroti bhasma sarvAsurAnariShu yat.hprahiNoShi shastram | lokAnprayAntu ripavo.api hi shastrapUtA itthaM matirbhavati teShvahiteShusAdhvI
verses.translation: Having indeed seen them, why dost thou not, O lady, reduce to ashes all the Asuras, since thou directest thy weapons against the foes? 'Let even enemies, purified by dying in arms, attain in sooth to the bright worlds'—such is thy most kindly intention towards even them.

verses.sanskrit: खड्गप्रभानिकरविस्फुरणैस्तथोग्रैः शूलाग्रकान्तिनिवहेन दृशोऽसुराणाम् । यन्नागता विलयमंशुमदिन्दुखण्ड- योग्याननं तव विलोकयतां तदेतत्
verses.transliteration: khaDgaprabhAnikaravisphuraNaistathograiH shUlAgrakAntinivahena dR^isho.asurANAm | yannAgatA vilayamaMshumadindukhaNDa\- yogyAnanaM tava vilokayatAM tadetat
verses.translation: And though, neither by the sharp flashes of abundant light from thy scymitar, nor by the copious lustre of thy spear-point, the eyes of the Asuras were destroyed; yet, as they gazed upon thy countenance which bore a portion of the radiant moon, this very thing happened.
verses.wordMeaning: And though, neither by the sharp flashes of abundant light from thy scymitar, nor by the copious lustre of thy spear-point, the eyes of the Asuras were destroyed; yet, as they gazed upon thy countenance which bore a portion of the radiant moon, this very thing happened.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्वृत्तवृत्तशमनं तव देवि शीलं रूपं तथैतदविचिन्त्यमतुल्यमन्यैः । वीर्यं च हन्तृ हृतदेवपराक्रमाणां वैरिष्वपि प्रकटितैव दया त्वयेत्थम्
verses.transliteration: durvR^ittavR^ittashamanaM tava devi shIlaM rUpaM tathaitadavichintyamatulyamanyaiH | vIryaM cha hantR^i hR^itadevaparAkramANAM vairiShvapi prakaTitaiva dayA tvayettham
verses.translation: Thy disposition, O goddess, subdues the conduct of men of evil conduct; and this thy form surpasses thought and rivalry by others; and thy valour vanquishes those who have robbed the gods of their prowess; thou hast as it were manifested pity thus even on enemies!
verses.wordMeaning: Thy disposition, O goddess, subdues the conduct of men of evil conduct; and this thy form surpasses thought and rivalry by others; and thy valour vanquishes those who have robbed the gods of their prowess; thou hast as it were manifested pity thus even on enemies!

verses.sanskrit: केनोपमा भवतु तेऽस्य पराक्रमस्य रूपं च शत्रुभयकार्यतिहारि कुत्र । चित्ते कृपा समरनिष्ठुरता च दृष्टा त्वय्येव देवि वरदे भुवनत्रयेऽपि
verses.transliteration: kenopamA bhavatu te.asya parAkramasya rUpaM cha shatrubhayakAryatihAri kutra | chitte kR^ipA samaraniShThuratA cha dR^iShTA tvayyeva devi varade bhuvanatraye.api
verses.translation: To what may this thy prowess be compared? And whereto thy form most charming, which strikes fear among foes? Compassion in mind and relentlessness in battle are seen in thee, O goddess, who bestowest boons even on the three worlds!
verses.wordMeaning: To what may this thy prowess be compared? And whereto thy form most charming, which strikes fear among foes? Compassion in mind and relentlessness in battle are seen in thee, O goddess, who bestowest boons even on the three worlds!

verses.sanskrit: त्रैलोक्यमेतदखिलं रिपुनाशनेन त्रातं त्वया समरमूर्धनि तेऽपि हत्वा । नीता दिवं रिपुगणा भयमप्यपास्तम् अस्माकमुन्मदसुरारिभवं नमस्ते
verses.transliteration: trailokyametadakhilaM ripunAshanena trAtaM tvayA samaramUrdhani te.api hatvA | nItA divaM ripugaNA bhayamapyapAstam asmAkamunmadasurAribhavaM namaste
verses.translation: Through the destruction of the foes, these three worlds entire have been saved by thee. Having slain them in the battle-front, thou hast led even those hosts of foes to heaven, and dispelled the fear which beset us from the frenzied foes of the gods. Reverence to thee!

verses.sanskrit: शूलेन पाहि नो देवि पाहि खड्गेन चाम्बिके । घण्टास्वनेन नः पाहि चापज्यानिःस्वनेन च
verses.transliteration: shUlena pAhi no devi pAhi khaDgena chAmbike | ghaNTAsvanena naH pAhi chApajyAniHsvanena cha
verses.translation: With thy spear protect us, O goddess! Protect us with thy sword also, O Ambika! By the clanging of thy bell protect us, and by the twanging of the thong of thy bow!
verses.wordMeaning: With thy spear protect us, O goddess! Protect us with thy sword also, O Ambika! By the clanging of thy bell protect us, and by the twanging of the thong of thy bow!

verses.sanskrit: प्राच्यां रक्ष प्रतीच्यां च चण्डिके रक्ष दक्षिणे । भ्रामणेनात्मशूलस्य उत्तरस्यां तथेश्वरि
verses.transliteration: prAchyAM rakSha pratIchyAM cha chaNDike rakSha dakShiNe | bhrAmaNenAtmashUlasya uttarasyAM tatheshvari
verses.translation: In the east guard us, and in the west; O Chandika, guard us in the south by the brandishing of thy spear, and also in the north, O goddess!
verses.wordMeaning: In the east guard us, and in the west; O Chandika, guard us in the south by the brandishing of thy spear, and also in the north, O goddess!

verses.sanskrit: सौम्यानि यानि रूपाणि त्रैलोक्ये विचरन्ति ते । यानि चात्यन्तघोराणि तै रक्षास्मांस्तथा भुवम्
verses.transliteration: saumyAni yAni rUpANi trailokye vicharanti te | yAni chAtyantaghorANi tai rakShAsmAMstathA bhuvam
verses.translation: Whatever gentle forms of thee wander about in the three worlds, and whatever exceedingly terrible forms wander, by means of them guard us and the earth!

verses.sanskrit: ॐ क्लीं ऋषिरुवाच
verses.transliteration: OM klIM R^iShiruvAcha
verses.translation: Om Klim. The rishi spoke:
verses.hindi: तब उसके भ्रू-कुटी के मंडल से सहसा काली निकलीं — विकराल मुख वाली, खड्ग और पाश धारण करने वाली।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most powerful passages in the Devi Mahatmyam. When the Mother's gentleness is met with cruelty, she does not become weak. From her own furrowed brow — from her concentrated awareness — Kali emerges. Kali is not "another goddess" but the Mother's own fierce face. The lesson: love itself, when threatened, has a fierce mode. The compassion that allows everything is not the same as the compassion that ALLOWS injustice. Real compassion has teeth.
verses.explanation: One of the most powerful passages in the Devi Mahatmyam. When the Mother's gentleness is met with cruelty, she does not become weak. From her own furrowed brow — from her concentrated awareness — Kali emerges. Kali is not "another goddess" but the Mother's own fierce face. The lesson: love itself, when threatened, has a fierce mode. The compassion that allows everything is not the same as the compassion that ALLOWS injustice. Real compassion has teeth.
verses.science: Research on righteous anger and prosocial aggression: properly channelled anger can be a force for justice (Aaron Sell, et al.). The brain has distinct circuits for predatory aggression (cold, calculating) and protective aggression (hot, defensive of others). Healthy individuals can access protective aggression when needed without losing their ethical core. Kali is the mythic icon of this: protective fierce energy in defence of dharma.
verses.lifeLesson: Are you so committed to "being nice" that you allow injustice — to yourself or to others — to pass unchallenged? Kali whispers: kindness without fierceness is incomplete. Sometimes love requires the noose, the sword, the cutting through of comfortable illusions. The Mother is not always sweet — sometimes she is terrifying. Honour both her faces.
verses.commentary: One of the most powerful passages in the Devi Mahatmyam. When the Mother's gentleness is met with cruelty, she does not become weak. verses.transliteration: namo devyai mahAdevyai shivAyai satataM namaH | namaH prakR^ityai bhadrAyai niyatAH praNatAH sma tAm
verses.translation: Reverence to the goddess, to the great goddess! To her who is auspicious reverence perpetually! Reverence to Prakriti the good! Submissive we fall prostrate before her!

verses.sanskrit: रौद्रायै नमो नित्यायै गौर्यै धात्र्यै नमो नमः । ज्योत्स्नायै चेन्दुरूपिण्यै सुखायै सततं नमः
verses.transliteration: raudrAyai namo nityAyai gauryai dhAtryai namo namaH | jyotsnAyai chendurUpiNyai sukhAyai satataM namaH
verses.translation: Reverence to her who is terrible, to her who is constant! To Gauri, to Dhatri reverence, yea reverence! And to the Moonlight, to her who has the moon's form, to her who is happy, reverence continually!

verses.sanskrit: कल्याण्यै प्रणतां वृद्ध्यै सिद्ध्यै कुर्मो नमो नमः । नैरृत्यै भूभृतां लक्ष्म्यै शर्वाण्यै ते नमो नमः
verses.transliteration: kalyANyai praNatAM vR^iddhyai siddhyai kurmo namo namaH | nairR^ityai bhUbhR^itAM lakShmyai sharvANyai te namo namaH
verses.translation: Falling prostrate, to her who is propitious, to Prosperity, to Perfection let us pay reverence, yea reverence! To Nirriti, to the goddess of Good Fortune of kings, to thee, Sharvani, reverence, yea reverence!

verses.sanskrit: दुर्गायै दुर्गपारायै सारायै सर्वकारिण्यै । ख्यात्यै तथैव कृष्णायै धूम्रायै सततं नमः
verses.transliteration: durgAyai durgapArAyai sArAyai sarvakAriNyai | khyAtyai tathaiva kR^iShNAyai dhUmrAyai satataM namaH
verses.translation: To Durga, to her who is a further shore difficult to be reached, to her who is essential, to her who works all things, and to Fame also, to her who is blue-black, to her who is smoke-dark, reverence continually!

verses.transliteration: atisaumyAtiraudrAyai natAstasyai namo namaH | namo jagatpratiShThAyai devyai kR^ityai namo namaH
verses.translation: Before her who is at once most gentle and most harsh we fall prostrate; to her reverence, yea reverence! Reverence to her who is the foundation of the world! To the goddess who is Action reverence, yea reverence!

verses.translation: To the goddess who among all created beings is called Vishnu's illusive power—reverence to her, reverence to her, reverence to her, reverence, yea reverence! To the goddess who among all created beings bears the name Consciousness—reverence to her, reverence to her, reverence to her, reverence, yea reverence! To the goddess who among all created beings stands firm with the form of Intellect—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Sleep—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Hunger—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Shadow—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Energy—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Thirst—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Patience—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Speciality—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Modesty—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Peaceableness—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Faith—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Loveliness—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Good Fortune—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Activity—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Memory—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Mercy—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Contentment—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Mother—reverence to her, yea reverence! To the goddess who stands firm with the form of Error—reverence to her, yea reverence! To her who both governs the organs of sense of created beings, and rules among all created beings perpetually—to her, the goddess of Pervasiveness, reverence, yea reverence!

verses.sanskrit: चितिरूपेण या कृत्स्नमेतद् व्याप्य स्थिता जगत् । नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥ ५.७८-८०॥ स्तुता सुरैः पूर्वमभीष्टसंश्रया- त्तथा सुरेन्द्रेण दिनेषु सेविता । करोतु सा नः शुभहेतुरीश्वरी शुभानि भद्राण्यभिहन्तु चापदः
verses.transliteration: chitirUpeNa yA kR^itsnametad vyApya sthitA jagat | namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaH || 5\.78\-80|| stutA suraiH pUrvamabhIShTasaMshrayA\- ttathA surendreNa dineShu sevitA | karotu sA naH shubhaheturIshvarI shubhAni bhadrANyabhihantu chApadaH
verses.translation: To her who exists pervading this entire world with the form of Thinking Mind—reverence to her, reverence to her, reverence to her, reverence, yea reverence! Praised by the gods aforetime because of eagerly-desired protection, and waited upon by the lord of the gods many days, may she, the goddess, the origin of brightness, accomplish for us bright things, yea good things, and ward off calamities!

verses.sanskrit: या साम्प्रतं चोद्धतदैत्यतापितै- रस्माभिरीशा च सुरैर्नमस्यते । या च स्मृता तत्क्षणमेव हन्ति नः सर्वापदो भक्तिविनम्रमूर्तिभिः
verses.transliteration: yA sAmprataM choddhatadaityatApitai\- rasmAbhirIshA cha surairnamasyate | yA cha smR^itA tatkShaNameva hanti naH sarvApado bhaktivinamramUrtibhiH
verses.translation: And she, who is both reverenced as queen by us gods, who are tormented now by the arrogant Daityas, and whom we call to mind as we bow our bodies in faith, she this very moment destroys all our calamities!

verses.sanskrit: एवं स्तवाभियुक्तानां देवानां तत्र पार्वती । स्नातुमभ्याययौ तोये जाह्नव्या नृपनन्दन
verses.transliteration: evaM stavAbhiyuktAnAM devAnAM tatra pArvatI | snAtumabhyAyayau toye jAhnavyA nR^ipanandana
verses.translation: While the gods were thus engaged in offering hymns and other reverential acts, Parvati came there to bathe in the water of the Ganges, O prince.
verses.wordMeaning: While the gods were thus engaged in offering hymns and other reverential acts, Parvati came there to bathe in the water of the Ganges, O prince.

verses.sanskrit: साब्रवीत्तान् सुरान् सुभ्रूर्भवद्भिः स्तूयतेऽत्र का । शरीरकोशतश्चास्याः समुद्भूताब्रवीच्छिवा
verses.transliteration: sAbravIttAn surAn subhrUrbhavadbhiH stUyate.atra kA | sharIrakoshatashchAsyAH samudbhUtAbravIchChivA
verses.translation: She, the beautiful-browed, said to those gods, 'Whom do ye, lords, hymn here?' And springing forth from the treasure-house of her body, the auspicious goddess spoke:

verses.sanskrit: स्तोत्रं ममैतत्क्रियते शुम्भदैत्यनिराकृतैः । देवैः समेतैः समरे निशुम्भेन पराजितैः
verses.transliteration: stotraM mamaitatkriyate shumbhadaityanirAkR^itaiH | devaiH sametaiH samare nishumbhena parAjitaiH
verses.translation: 'For me this hymn is uttered by the assembled gods, who have been set at nought by the Daitya Shumbha and routed in battle by Nishumbha.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'For me this hymn is uttered by the assembled gods, who have been set at nought by the Daitya Shumbha and routed in battle by Nishumbha.'

verses.sanskrit: शरीरकोशाद्यत्तस्याः पार्वत्या निःसृताम्बिका । कौशिकीति समस्तेषु ततो लोकेषु गीयते
verses.transliteration: sharIrakoshAdyattasyAH pArvatyA niHsR^itAmbikA | kaushikIti samasteShu tato lokeShu gIyate
verses.translation: Because Ambika issued forth from the treasure-house of Parvati's body, she is therefore named in song as Kaushiki among all the worlds.
verses.wordMeaning: Because Ambika issued forth from the treasure-house of Parvati's body, she is therefore named in song as Kaushiki among all the worlds.
