verses.sanskrit: तस्यां विनिर्गतायां तु कृष्णाभूत्सापि पार्वती । कालिकेति समाख्याता हिमाचलकृताश्रया
verses.transliteration: tasyAM vinirgatAyAM tu kR^iShNAbhUtsApi pArvatI | kAliketi samAkhyAtA himAchalakR^itAshrayA
verses.translation: Now after she had issued forth, the other also, even Parvati, became black; she is celebrated as Kalika; she fixed her abode on Mount Himavat.
verses.wordMeaning: Now after she had issued forth, the other also, even Parvati, became black; she is celebrated as Kalika; she fixed her abode on Mount Himavat.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽम्बिकां परं रूपं बिभ्राणां सुमनोहरम् । ददर्श चण्डो मुण्डश्च भृत्यौ शुम्भनिशुम्भयोः
verses.transliteration: tato.ambikAM paraM rUpaM bibhrANAM sumanoharam | dadarsha chaNDo muNDashcha bhR^ityau shumbhanishumbhayoH
verses.translation: Thereafter Chanda and Munda, the two servants of Shumbha and Nishumbha, saw Ambika displaying her sublime and most captivating form;
verses.wordMeaning: Thereafter Chanda and Munda, the two servants of Shumbha and Nishumbha, saw Ambika displaying her sublime and most captivating form;

verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Thereafter Chanda and Munda, the two servants of Shumbha and Nishumbha, saw Ambika displaying her sublime and most captivating form;

verses.sanskrit: ताभ्यां शुम्भाय चाख्याता सातीव सुमनोहरा । काप्यास्ते स्त्री महाराज भासयन्ती हिमाचलम्
verses.transliteration: tAbhyAM shumbhAya chAkhyAtA sAtIva sumanoharA | kApyAste strI mahArAja bhAsayantI himAchalam
verses.translation: and both spake out unto Shumbha: 'What woman then, most surpassingly captivating, dwells here, illuminating Mount Himavat, O great king?'
verses.wordMeaning: and both spake out unto Shumbha: 'What woman then, most surpassingly captivating, dwells here, illuminating Mount Himavat, O great king?'

verses.sanskrit: नैव तादृक् क्वचिद्रूपं दृष्टं केनचिदुत्तमम् । ज्ञायतां काप्यसौ देवी गृह्यतां चासुरेश्वर
verses.transliteration: naiva tAdR^ik kvachidrUpaM dR^iShTaM kenachiduttamam | j~nAyatAM kApyasau devI gR^ihyatAM chAsureshvara
verses.translation: 'Such sublime beauty was never in sooth seen by anyone anywhere; let it be ascertained if she is any goddess, and let her be taken possession of, O lord of the Asuras.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Such sublime beauty was never in sooth seen by anyone anywhere; let it be ascertained if she is any goddess, and let her be taken possession of, O lord of the Asuras.'

verses.sanskrit: स्त्रीरत्नमतिचार्वङ्गी द्योतयन्ती दिशस्त्विषा । सा तु तिष्ठति दैत्येन्द्र तां भवान् द्रष्टुमर्हति
verses.transliteration: strIratnamatichArva~NgI dyotayantI dishastviShA | sA tu tiShThati daityendra tAM bhavAn draShTumarhati
verses.translation: 'A gem among women, surpassingly beautiful in body, illuminating the regions of the sky with her lustre—there she is then, O lord of the Daityas; deign, Sir, to look at her.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'A gem among women, surpassingly beautiful in body, illuminating the regions of the sky with her lustre—there she is then, O lord of the Daityas; deign, Sir, to look at her.'

verses.sanskrit: यानि रत्नानि मणयो गजाश्वादीनि वै प्रभो । त्रैलोक्ये तु समस्तानि साम्प्रतं भान्ति ते गृहे
verses.transliteration: yAni ratnAni maNayo gajAshvAdIni vai prabho | trailokye tu samastAni sAmprataM bhAnti te gR^ihe
verses.translation: 'Moreover, whatever gems, precious stones, elephants, horses and other valuable things indeed exist in the three worlds, O lord, all those display their splendour at this present time in thy house.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Moreover, whatever gems, precious stones, elephants, horses and other valuable things indeed exist in the three worlds, O lord, all those display their splendour at this present time in thy house.'

verses.sanskrit: ऐरावतः समानीतो गजरत्नं पुरन्दरात् । पारिजाततरुश्चायं तथैवोच्चैःश्रवा हयः
verses.transliteration: airAvataH samAnIto gajaratnaM purandarAt | pArijAtatarushchAyaM tathaivochchaiHshravA hayaH
verses.translation: 'Airavata, gem among elephants, has been captured from Purandara; and this Parijata tree and also the horse Uchchaihshravas.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Airavata, gem among elephants, has been captured from Purandara; and this Parijata tree and also the horse Uchchaihshravas.'

verses.sanskrit: विमानं हंससंयुक्तमेतत्तिष्ठति तेऽङ्गणे । रत्नभूतमिहानीतं यदासीद्वेधसोऽद्भुतम्
verses.transliteration: vimAnaM haMsasaMyuktametattiShThati te.a~NgaNe | ratnabhUtamihAnItaM yadAsIdvedhaso.adbhutam
verses.translation: 'Here stands the heavenly chariot yoked with swans in thy court-yard; it has been brought here, the wonderful chariot composed of gems, which belonged to Brahma.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Here stands the heavenly chariot yoked with swans in thy court-yard; it has been brought here, the wonderful chariot composed of gems, which belonged to Brahma.'

verses.sanskrit: निधिरेष महापद्मः समानीतो धनेश्वरात् । किञ्जल्किनीं ददौ चाब्धिर्मालामम्लानपङ्कजाम्
verses.transliteration: nidhireSha mahApadmaH samAnIto dhaneshvarAt | ki~njalkinIM dadau chAbdhirmAlAmamlAnapa~NkajAm
verses.translation: 'Here is the Nidhi Mahapadma, captured from the Lord of wealth. And the Ocean gave a garland made of filaments and of undying lotus flowers.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Here is the Nidhi Mahapadma, captured from the Lord of wealth. And the Ocean gave a garland made of filaments and of undying lotus flowers.'

verses.sanskrit: छत्रं ते वारुणं गेहे काञ्चनस्रावि तिष्ठति । तथायं स्यन्दनवरो यः पुरासीत्प्रजापतेः
verses.transliteration: ChatraM te vAruNaM gehe kA~nchanasrAvi tiShThati | tathAyaM syandanavaro yaH purAsItprajApateH
verses.translation: 'In thy house stands Varuna's umbrella, which streams with gold. And here is the choice chariot that belonged to Prajapati formerly.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'In thy house stands Varuna's umbrella, which streams with gold. And here is the choice chariot that belonged to Prajapati formerly.'

verses.sanskrit: मृत्योरुत्क्रान्तिदा नाम शक्तिरीश त्वया हृता । पाशः सलिलराजस्य भ्रातुस्तव परिग्रहे
verses.transliteration: mR^ityorutkrAntidA nAma shaktirIsha tvayA hR^itA | pAshaH salilarAjasya bhrAtustava parigrahe
verses.translation: 'Thou, O lord, hast carried off Death's power, which is named Utkranti-da. The noose of the Ocean-king is in thy brother's possession.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Thou, O lord, hast carried off Death's power, which is named Utkranti-da. The noose of the Ocean-king is in thy brother's possession.'

verses.sanskrit: निशुम्भस्याब्धिजाताश्च समस्ता रत्नजातयः । वह्निरपि ददौ तुभ्यमग्निशौचे च वाससी
verses.transliteration: nishumbhasyAbdhijAtAshcha samastA ratnajAtayaH | vahnirapi dadau tubhyamagnishauche cha vAsasI
verses.translation: 'And Nishumbha has every kind of gem which is produced in the sea. Agni also gave thee two garments which are purified by fire.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'And Nishumbha has every kind of gem which is produced in the sea. Agni also gave thee two garments which are purified by fire.'

verses.sanskrit: एवं दैत्येन्द्र रत्नानि समस्तान्याहृतानि ते । स्त्रीरत्नमेषा कल्याणी त्वया कस्मान्न गृह्यते
verses.transliteration: evaM daityendra ratnAni samastAnyAhR^itAni te | strIratnameShA kalyANI tvayA kasmAnna gR^ihyate
verses.translation: 'Thus, O lord of the Daityas, all gems have been captured by thee; why dost thou not seize this auspicious lady, this gem of womankind?'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Thus, O lord of the Daityas, all gems have been captured by thee; why dost thou not seize this auspicious lady, this gem of womankind?'

verses.sanskrit: निशम्येति वचः शुम्भः स तदा चण्डमुण्डयोः । प्रेषयामास सुग्रीवं दूतं देव्या महासुरम्
verses.transliteration: nishamyeti vachaH shumbhaH sa tadA chaNDamuNDayoH | preShayAmAsa sugrIvaM dUtaM devyA mahAsuram
verses.translation: Shumbha, on hearing this speech then from Chanda and Munda, sent the great Asura Sugriva as messenger to the goddess,

verses.sanskrit: इति चेति च वक्तव्या सा गत्वा वचनान्मम । यथा चाभ्येति सम्प्रीत्या तथा कार्यं त्वया लघु
verses.transliteration: iti cheti cha vaktavyA sA gatvA vachanAnmama | yathA chAbhyeti samprItyA tathA kAryaM tvayA laghu
verses.translation: saying, 'Go and address her thus and thus according to my words, and lightly conduct the matter so that she may come to me of her own good pleasure.'
verses.wordMeaning: saying, 'Go and address her thus and thus according to my words, and lightly conduct the matter so that she may come to me of her own good pleasure.'

verses.sanskrit: स तत्र गत्वा यत्रास्ते शैलोद्देशेऽतिशोभने । तां च देवीं ततः प्राह श्लक्ष्णं मधुरया गिरा
verses.transliteration: sa tatra gatvA yatrAste shailoddeshe.atishobhane | tAM cha devIM tataH prAha shlakShNaM madhurayA girA
verses.translation: He went to where the goddess sat on a very bright spot in the mountain, and spoke gently with mellifluous voice.
verses.wordMeaning: He went to where the goddess sat on a very bright spot in the mountain, and spoke gently with mellifluous voice.

verses.sanskrit: देवि दैत्येश्वरः शुम्भस्त्रैलोक्ये परमेश्वरः । दूतोऽहं प्रेषितस्तेन त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः
verses.transliteration: devi daityeshvaraH shumbhastrailokye parameshvaraH | dUto.ahaM preShitastena tvatsakAshamihAgataH
verses.translation: O goddess! Shumbha, lord of the Daityas, is supreme lord over the three worlds. A messenger am I, sent by him; to thy presence here I have come.
verses.wordMeaning: O goddess! Shumbha, lord of the Daityas, is supreme lord over the three worlds. A messenger am I, sent by him; to thy presence here I have come.

verses.sanskrit: अव्याहताज्ञः सर्वासु यः सदा देवयोनिषु । निर्जिताखिलदैत्यारिः स यदाह शृणुष्व तत्
verses.transliteration: avyAhatAj~naH sarvAsu yaH sadA devayoniShu | nirjitAkhiladaityAriH sa yadAha shR^iNuShva tat
verses.translation: Hearken to what he has said, whose command is never resisted among all beings of divine origin, and who has vanquished every foe of the Daityas:
verses.wordMeaning: Hearken to what he has said, whose command is never resisted among all beings of divine origin, and who has vanquished every foe of the Daityas:

verses.sanskrit: मम त्रैलोक्यमखिलं मम देवा वशानुगाः । यज्ञभागानहं सर्वानुपाश्नामि पृथक् पृथक्
verses.transliteration: mama trailokyamakhilaM mama devA vashAnugAH | yaj~nabhAgAnahaM sarvAnupAshnAmi pR^ithak pR^ithak
verses.translation: 'Mine are all the three worlds; obedient to my authority are the gods; I eat every portion of the sacrifices separately.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Mine are all the three worlds; obedient to my authority are the gods; I eat every portion of the sacrifices separately.'

verses.sanskrit: त्रैलोक्ये वररत्नानि मम वश्यान्यशेषतः । तथैव गजरत्नं च हृतं देवेन्द्रवाहनम्
verses.transliteration: trailokye vararatnAni mama vashyAnyasheShataH | tathaiva gajaratnaM cha hR^itaM devendravAhanam
verses.translation: 'The choicest gems in the three worlds are altogether under my power; and so is the finest of elephants, the chariot-beast of the lord of the gods, since I have captured it.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'The choicest gems in the three worlds are altogether under my power; and so is the finest of elephants, the chariot-beast of the lord of the gods, since I have captured it.'

verses.sanskrit: क्षीरोदमथनोद्भूतमश्वरत्नं ममामरैः । उच्चैःश्रवससंज्ञं तत्प्रणिपत्य समर्पितम्
verses.transliteration: kShIrodamathanodbhUtamashvaratnaM mamAmaraiH | uchchaiHshravasasaMj~naM tatpraNipatya samarpitam
verses.translation: 'That gem among horses, named Uchchaihshravas, which came forth at the churning of the sea of milk, was presented to me by the immortals who prostrated themselves before me.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'That gem among horses, named Uchchaihshravas, which came forth at the churning of the sea of milk, was presented to me by the immortals who prostrated themselves before me.'

verses.sanskrit: यानि चान्यानि देवेषु गन्धर्वेषूरगेषु च । रत्नभूतानि भूतानि तानि मय्येव शोभने
verses.transliteration: yAni chAnyAni deveShu gandharveShUrageShu cha | ratnabhUtAni bhUtAni tAni mayyeva shobhane
verses.translation: 'And whatever other created things in the shape of gems existed among the gods, Gandharvas and Nagas, they were presented even to me, O brilliant lady.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'And whatever other created things in the shape of gems existed among the gods, Gandharvas and Nagas, they were presented even to me, O brilliant lady.'

verses.sanskrit: स्त्रीरत्नभूतां त्वां देवि लोके मन्यामहे वयम् । सा त्वमस्मानुपागच्छ यतो रत्नभुजो वयम्
verses.transliteration: strIratnabhUtAM tvAM devi loke manyAmahe vayam | sA tvamasmAnupAgachCha yato ratnabhujo vayam
verses.translation: 'I esteem thee, O goddess, to be the gem of womankind in the world; do thou, who art such, approach unto me, since I am an enjoyer of gems.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'I esteem thee, O goddess, to be the gem of womankind in the world; do thou, who art such, approach unto me, since I am an enjoyer of gems.'

verses.sanskrit: मां वा ममानुजं वापि निशुम्भमुरुविक्रमम् । भज त्वं चञ्चलापाङ्गि रत्नभूतासि वै यतः
verses.transliteration: mAM vA mamAnujaM vApi nishumbhamuruvikramam | bhaja tvaM cha~nchalApA~Ngi ratnabhUtAsi vai yataH
verses.translation: 'Either to me, or to my younger brother Nishumbha of wide-reaching prowess, approach thou, O lady of quick side-glances, since thou art in truth a gem.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Either to me, or to my younger brother Nishumbha of wide-reaching prowess, approach thou, O lady of quick side-glances, since thou art in truth a gem.'

verses.sanskrit: परमैश्वर्यमतुलं प्राप्स्यसे मत्परिग्रहात् । एतद्बुद्ध्या समालोच्य मत्परिग्रहतां व्रज
verses.transliteration: paramaishvaryamatulaM prApsyase matparigrahAt | etadbuddhyA samAlochya matparigrahatAM vraja
verses.translation: 'Supreme dominion beyond compare thou shalt gain by wedding me. Understand and consider this, and come unto wedlock with me.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Supreme dominion beyond compare thou shalt gain by wedding me. Understand and consider this, and come unto wedlock with me.'

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्ता सा तदा देवी गम्भीरान्तःस्मिता जगौ । दुर्गा भगवती भद्रा ययेदं धार्यते जगत्
verses.transliteration: ityuktA sA tadA devI gambhIrAntaHsmitA jagau | durgA bhagavatI bhadrA yayedaM dhAryate jagat
verses.translation: Thus accosted, the goddess, smiling deeply within herself—she, Durga the adorable and good, who supports this world—sang this reply then.
verses.wordMeaning: Thus accosted, the goddess, smiling deeply within herself—she, Durga the adorable and good, who supports this world—sang this reply then.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यमुक्तं त्वया नात्र मिथ्या किञ्चित्त्वयोदितम् । त्रैलोक्याधिपतिः शुम्भो निशुम्भश्चापि तादृशः
verses.transliteration: satyamuktaM tvayA nAtra mithyA ki~nchittvayoditam | trailokyAdhipatiH shumbho nishumbhashchApi tAdR^ishaH
verses.translation: Truly hast thou spoken; nought hast thou uttered falsely herein. Sovereign of the three worlds is Shumbha, and like unto him is Nishumbha also!
verses.wordMeaning: Truly hast thou spoken; nought hast thou uttered falsely herein. Sovereign of the three worlds is Shumbha, and like unto him is Nishumbha also!

verses.sanskrit: किं त्वत्र यत्प्रतिज्ञातं मिथ्या तत्क्रियते कथम् । श्रूयतामल्पबुद्धित्वात्प्रतिज्ञा या कृता पुरा
verses.transliteration: kiM tvatra yatpratij~nAtaM mithyA tatkriyate katham | shrUyatAmalpabuddhitvAtpratij~nA yA kR^itA purA
verses.translation: But how can that which has been promised concerning this myself be fulfilled falsely? Hearken, what vow I made formerly by reason of my small understanding at that time:
verses.wordMeaning: But how can that which has been promised concerning this myself be fulfilled falsely? Hearken, what vow I made formerly by reason of my small understanding at that time:

verses.sanskrit: यो मां जयति सङ्ग्रामे यो मे दर्पं व्यपोहति । यो मे प्रतिबलो लोके स मे भर्ता भविष्यति
verses.transliteration: yo mAM jayati sa~NgrAme yo me darpaM vyapohati | yo me pratibalo loke sa me bhartA bhaviShyati
verses.translation: 'He who vanquishes me in fight, who forces my pride from me, and who is my match in strength in the world, he shall be my husband.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'He who vanquishes me in fight, who forces my pride from me, and who is my match in strength in the world, he shall be my husband.'

verses.sanskrit: तदागच्छतु शुम्भोऽत्र निशुम्भो वा महाबलः । मां जित्वा किं चिरेणात्र पाणिं गृह्णातु मे लघु
verses.transliteration: tadAgachChatu shumbho.atra nishumbho vA mahAbalaH | mAM jitvA kiM chireNAtra pANiM gR^ihNAtu me laghu
verses.translation: Let Shumbha come here then, or Nishumbha the great Asura; let him vanquish me—what need of delay here?—and let him lightly take my hand in marriage!
verses.wordMeaning: Let Shumbha come here then, or Nishumbha the great Asura; let him vanquish me—what need of delay here?—and let him lightly take my hand in marriage!

verses.sanskrit: अवलिप्तासि मैवं त्वं देवि ब्रूहि ममाग्रतः । त्रैलोक्ये कः पुमांस्तिष्ठेदग्रे शुम्भनिशुम्भयोः
verses.transliteration: avaliptAsi maivaM tvaM devi brUhi mamAgrataH | trailokye kaH pumAMstiShThedagre shumbhanishumbhayoH
verses.translation: Proud art thou! Talk not so before me, O goddess! What male in the three worlds may stand front to front with Shumbha and Nishumbha?
verses.wordMeaning: Proud art thou! Talk not so before me, O goddess! What male in the three worlds may stand front to front with Shumbha and Nishumbha?

verses.sanskrit: अन्येषामपि दैत्यानां सर्वे देवा न वै युधि । तिष्ठन्ति सम्मुखे देवि किं पुनः स्त्री त्वमेकिका
verses.transliteration: anyeShAmapi daityAnAM sarve devA na vai yudhi | tiShThanti sammukhe devi kiM punaH strI tvamekikA
verses.translation: All the gods verily stand not face to face with even the other Daityas in battle, O goddess; how much less canst thou so stand, a woman single-handed!
verses.wordMeaning: All the gods verily stand not face to face with even the other Daityas in battle, O goddess; how much less canst thou so stand, a woman single-handed!
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): All the gods verily stand not face to face with even the other Daityas in battle, O goddess; how much less canst thou so stand, a woman single-handed!

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्राद्याः सकला देवास्तस्थुर्येषां न संयुगे । शुम्भादीनां कथं तेषां स्त्री प्रयास्यसि सम्मुखम्
verses.transliteration: indrAdyAH sakalA devAstasthuryeShAM na saMyuge | shumbhAdInAM kathaM teShAM strI prayAsyasi sammukham
verses.translation: With Shumbha and those other Daityas, against whom Indra and all the other gods stood not in battle, how shalt thou, a woman, venture face to face?
verses.wordMeaning: With Shumbha and those other Daityas, against whom Indra and all the other gods stood not in battle, how shalt thou, a woman, venture face to face?
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): With Shumbha and those other Daityas, against whom Indra and all the other gods stood not in battle, how shalt thou, a woman, venture face to face?

verses.sanskrit: सा त्वं गच्छ मयैवोक्ता पार्श्वं शुम्भनिशुम्भयोः । केशाकर्षणनिर्धूतगौरवा मा गमिष्यसि
verses.transliteration: sA tvaM gachCha mayaivoktA pArshvaM shumbhanishumbhayoH | keshAkarShaNanirdhUtagauravA mA gamiShyasi
verses.translation: Do thou, being such, to whom I have in sooth delivered my message, go near unto Shumbha and Nishumbha; let it not be that thou shalt go with thy dignity shattered, in that thou wilt be dragged thither by thy hair!
verses.wordMeaning: Do thou, being such, to whom I have in sooth delivered my message, go near unto Shumbha and Nishumbha; let it not be that thou shalt go with thy dignity shattered, in that thou wilt be dragged thither by thy hair!

verses.sanskrit: एवमेतद् बली शुम्भो निशुम्भश्चापितादृशः । किं करोमि प्रतिज्ञा मे यदनालोचिता पुरा
verses.transliteration: evametad balI shumbho nishumbhashchApitAdR^ishaH | kiM karomi pratij~nA me yadanAlochitA purA
verses.translation: So strong as this is Shumbha! and so exceedingly heroic is Nishumbha! What can I do, since there stands my ill-considered promise of long ago?
verses.wordMeaning: So strong as this is Shumbha! and so exceedingly heroic is Nishumbha! What can I do, since there stands my ill-considered promise of long ago?

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं गच्छ मयोक्तं ते यदेतत्सर्वमादृतः । तदाचक्ष्वासुरेन्द्राय स च युक्तं करोतु यत्
verses.transliteration: sa tvaM gachCha mayoktaM te yadetatsarvamAdR^itaH | tadAchakShvAsurendrAya sa cha yuktaM karotu yat
verses.translation: Go thou thyself; make known respectfully to the lord of the Asuras all this that I have said to thee, and let him do whatever is fitting.

verses.sanskrit: केषाञ्चित्पाटयामास नखैः कोष्ठानि केसरी । तथा तलप्रहारेण शिरांसि कृतवान्पृथक्
verses.transliteration: keShA~nchitpATayAmAsa nakhaiH koShThAni kesarI | tathA talaprahAreNa shirAMsi kR^itavAnpR^ithak
verses.translation: The lion with his claws tore out the entrails of some, and struck their heads off with a cuff-like blow.
verses.hindi: देवी ने एक हुंकार से ही उस दैत्य को भस्म कर दिया। और सिंह ने उसके साथियों और सेना को भयभीत किया।
verses.wordMeaning: Dhumralochana — "smoke-eyed" — is the demon who cannot see clearly; the principle of vision obscured by the smoke of passion, pride, and desire. One "humkara" — a single vibration of concentrated divine power — destroys him entirely. The teaching: clarity of perception, powerfully directed, dissolves the demons of confusion. You do not argue with obscured vision; you dispel it with a single act of radical attention.
verses.explanation: Dhumralochana — "smoke-eyed" — is the demon who cannot see clearly; the principle of vision obscured by the smoke of passion, pride, and desire. One "humkara" — a single vibration of concentrated divine power — destroys him entirely. The teaching: clarity of perception, powerfully directed, dissolves the demons of confusion. You do not argue with obscured vision; you dispel it with a single act of radical attention.
verses.science: Research on mindfulness and cognitive clarity (Kabat-Zinn; Brewer's research on addiction): present-moment awareness changes the brain's relationship to reactive patterns. The "smoke" of habitual thought (Default Mode Network over-activity) is reduced by one moment of concentrated, non-reactive attention. One focused moment of clear awareness is more powerful than hours of reactive analysis.
verses.lifeLesson: When you are confused — when smoke fills your inner vision — stop thinking more. The Devi's answer to Dhumralochana is not a clever argument; it is a single sound of power. Try this: sit still, take one deep breath, and on the exhale, sound "HUM" from your belly. Then observe what the silence reveals. Clarity is not constructed; it is uncovered.
verses.commentary: Dhumralochana — "smoke-eyed" — is the demon who cannot see clearly; the principle of vision obscured by the smoke of passion, pride, and desire. You do not argue with obscured vision; you dispel it with a single act of radical attention.

verses.translation: 'When that shrew is slain and her lion stricken down, seize her, Ambika, bind her and bring her quickly!'
verses.wordMeaning: 'When that shrew is slain and her lion stricken down, seize her, Ambika, bind her and bring her quickly!'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'When that shrew is slain and her lion stricken down, seize her, Ambika, bind her and bring her quickly!'

verses.transliteration: OM R^iShiruvAcha
verses.translation: Om. The rishi spoke:

verses.sanskrit: आज्ञप्तास्ते ततो दैत्याश्चण्डमुण्डपुरोगमाः । चतुरङ्गबलोपेता ययुरभ्युद्यतायुधाः
verses.transliteration: Aj~naptAste tato daityAshchaNDamuNDapurogamAH | chatura~NgabalopetA yayurabhyudyatAyudhAH
verses.translation: Then at his command the Daityas, led by Chanda and Munda, and arrayed in the four-fold order of an army, marched with weapons uplifted.
verses.wordMeaning: Then at his command the Daityas, led by Chanda and Munda, and arrayed in the four-fold order of an army, marched with weapons uplifted.

verses.sanskrit: ददृशुस्ते ततो देवीमीषद्धासां व्यवस्थिताम् । सिंहस्योपरि शैलेन्द्रशृङ्गे महति काञ्चने
verses.transliteration: dadR^ishuste tato devImIShaddhAsAM vyavasthitAm | siMhasyopari shailendrashR^i~Nge mahati kA~nchane
verses.translation: Soon they saw the goddess, slightly smiling, seated upon the lion, on a huge golden peak of the majestic mountain.
verses.wordMeaning: Soon they saw the goddess, slightly smiling, seated upon the lion, on a huge golden peak of the majestic mountain.

verses.sanskrit: ते दृष्ट्वा तां समादातुमुद्यमं चक्रुरुद्यताः । आकृष्टचापासिधरास्तथान्ये तत्समीपगाः
verses.transliteration: te dR^iShTvA tAM samAdAtumudyamaM chakrurudyatAH | AkR^iShTachApAsidharAstathAnye tatsamIpagAH
verses.translation: On seeing her, some of them made a strenuous effort to capture her, and others approached her holding their bows bent and their swords drawn.
verses.wordMeaning: On seeing her, some of them made a strenuous effort to capture her, and others approached her holding their bows bent and their swords drawn.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कोपं चकारोच्चैरम्बिका तानरीन्प्रति । कोपेन चास्या वदनं मषीवर्णमभूत्तदा
verses.transliteration: tataH kopaM chakArochchairambikA tAnarInprati | kopena chAsyA vadanaM maShIvarNamabhUttadA
verses.translation: Thereat Ambika uttered her wrath aloud against those foes, and her countenance then grew dark as ink in her wrath.
verses.wordMeaning: Thereat Ambika uttered her wrath aloud against those foes, and her countenance then grew dark as ink in her wrath.

verses.sanskrit: भ्रुकुटीकुटिलात्तस्या ललाटफलकाद्द्रुतम् । काली करालवदना विनिष्क्रान्तासिपाशिनी
verses.transliteration: bhrukuTIkuTilAttasyA lalATaphalakAddrutam | kAlI karAlavadanA viniShkrAntAsipAshinI
verses.translation: Out from the surface of her forehead, which was rugged with frowns, issued suddenly Kali of the terrible countenance, armed with a sword and noose,
verses.wordMeaning: Out from the surface of her forehead, which was rugged with frowns, issued suddenly Kali of the terrible countenance, armed with a sword and noose,

verses.sanskrit: विचित्रखट्वाङ्गधरा नरमालाविभूषणा । द्वीपिचर्मपरीधाना शुष्कमांसातिभैरवा
verses.transliteration: vichitrakhaTvA~NgadharA naramAlAvibhUShaNA | dvIpicharmaparIdhAnA shuShkamAMsAtibhairavA
verses.translation: bearing a many-coloured skull-topped staff, decorated with a garland of skulls, clad in a tiger's skin, very appalling because of her emaciated flesh,

verses.sanskrit: अतिविस्तारवदना जिह्वाललनभीषणा । निमग्नारक्तनयना नादापूरितदिङ्मुखा
verses.transliteration: ativistAravadanA jihvAlalanabhIShaNA | nimagnAraktanayanA nAdApUritadi~NmukhA
verses.translation: exceedingly wide of mouth, lolling out her tongue terribly, having deep-sunk reddish eyes, and filling the regions of the sky with her roars.
verses.wordMeaning: exceedingly wide of mouth, lolling out her tongue terribly, having deep-sunk reddish eyes, and filling the regions of the sky with her roars.

verses.sanskrit: सा वेगेनाभिपतिता घातयन्ती महासुरान् । सैन्ये तत्र सुरारीणामभक्षयत तद्बलम्
verses.transliteration: sA vegenAbhipatitA ghAtayantI mahAsurAn | sainye tatra surArINAmabhakShayata tadbalam
verses.translation: She fell upon the great Asuras impetuously, dealing slaughter among the host, and devoured that army of the gods' foes there.
verses.wordMeaning: She fell upon the great Asuras impetuously, dealing slaughter among the host, and devoured that army of the gods' foes there.

verses.sanskrit: पार्ष्णिग्राहाङ्कुशग्राहयोधघण्टासमन्वितान् । समादायैकहस्तेन मुखे चिक्षेप वारणान्
verses.transliteration: pArShNigrAhA~NkushagrAhayodhaghaNTAsamanvitAn | samAdAyaikahastena mukhe chikShepa vAraNAn
verses.translation: Taking up the elephants with one hand she flung them into her mouth, together with their rearmen and drivers and their warrior-riders and bells.

verses.transliteration: tathaiva yodhaM turagai rathaM sArathinA saha | nikShipya vaktre dashanaishcharvayantyatibhairavam
verses.translation: Flinging likewise warrior with his horses, and chariot with its driver into her mouth, she ground them most frightfully with her teeth.

verses.transliteration: ekaM jagrAha kesheShu grIvAyAmatha chAparam | pAdenAkramya chaivAnyamurasAnyamapothayat
verses.translation: She seized one by the hair, and another by the neck; and she kicked another with her foot, and crushed another against her breast.

verses.transliteration: tairmuktAni cha shastrANi mahAstrANi tathAsuraiH | mukhena jagrAha ruShA dashanairmathitAnyapi
verses.translation: And she seized with her mouth the weapons and the great arms which those Asuras abandoned, and crunched them up with her teeth in her fury.

verses.transliteration: balinAM tadbalaM sarvamasurANAM durAtmanAm | mamardAbhakShayachchAnyAnanyAMshchAtADayattadA
verses.translation: She crushed all that host of mighty and high-spirited Asuras; and devoured some and battered others.
verses.wordMeaning: She crushed all that host of mighty and high-spirited Asuras; and devoured some and battered others.

verses.transliteration: asinA nihatAH kechitkechitkhaTvA~NgatADitAH | jagmurvinAshamasurA dantAgrAbhihatAstathA
verses.translation: Some were slain with her sword, some were struck with her skull-topped staff, and other Asuras met their death being wounded with the edge of her teeth.

verses.transliteration: kShaNena tadbalaM sarvamasurANAM nipAtitam | dR^iShTvA chaNDo.abhidudrAva tAM kAlImatibhIShaNAm

verses.transliteration: sharavarShairmahAbhImairbhImAkShIM tAM mahAsuraH | ChAdayAmAsa chakraishcha muNDaH kShiptaiH sahasrashaH
verses.translation: Munda the great Asura covered her, the terrible-eyed goddess, with very terrible showers of arrows and with discuses hurled in thousands.

verses.transliteration: tAni chakrANyanekAni vishamAnAni tanmukham | babhuryathArkabimbAni subahUni ghanodaram
verses.translation: Those discuses seemed to be penetrating her countenance in multitudes, like as very many solar orbs might penetrate the body of a thunder-cloud.

verses.translation: Thereat Kali, who was roaring frightfully, laughed terribly with excessive fury, showing the gleam of her unsightly teeth within her dreadful mouth.

verses.translation: And the goddess, mounting upon her great lion, rushed at Chanda, and seizing him by his hair struck off his head with her sword.

verses.transliteration: atha muNDo.abhyadhAvattAM dR^iShTvA chaNDaM nipAtitam | tamapyapAtayadbhUmau sA khaDgAbhihataM ruShA
verses.translation: And Munda also rushed at her when he saw Chanda laid low; him also she felled to the ground, stricken with her scymitar in her fury.

verses.sanskrit: हतशेषं ततः सैन्यं दृष्ट्वा चण्डं निपातितम् । मुण्डं च सुमहावीर्यं दिशो भेजे भयातुरम्
verses.transliteration: hatasheShaM tataH sainyaM dR^iShTvA chaNDaM nipAtitam | muNDaM cha sumahAvIryaM disho bheje bhayAturam
verses.translation: Then the army, so much as escaped unslain, seeing Chanda laid low and most valiant Munda also, seized with panic fled in all directions.
verses.hindi: चण्ड और मुण्ड को पकड़कर, देवी चण्डिका ने तब प्रचण्ड अट्टहास के साथ अपना उत्तम माहात्म्य प्रकट किया।
verses.wordMeaning: Chanda ("passion") and Munda ("stubbornness") are the two most insidious inner enemies — not because they are powerful but because they disguise themselves as virtues: passion masquerades as enthusiasm, stubbornness as conviction. Kali's laughter as she presents them to the Mother is significant: the fierce energy laughs at what seemed so formidable. What once held you in terror becomes, to the awakened one, almost comic in its pretension.
verses.explanation: Chanda ("passion") and Munda ("stubbornness") are the two most insidious inner enemies — not because they are powerful but because they disguise themselves as virtues: passion masquerades as enthusiasm, stubbornness as conviction. Kali's laughter as she presents them to the Mother is significant: the fierce energy laughs at what seemed so formidable. What once held you in terror becomes, to the awakened one, almost comic in its pretension.
verses.science: Research on cognitive defusion (ACT, Steven Hayes): when we learn to observe our thoughts as mental events rather than facts, their power to compel action dissolves. A client who once said "I cannot resist this craving" — after defusion practice — can say "I notice I'm having the craving thought." The craving has not changed; the relationship to it has. Kali's laughter is defusion: the demon is real but its claim to sovereignty is exposed as absurd.
verses.lifeLesson: Pick the inner pattern that most "has" you — the passion or the stubbornness that most controls your choices. Now: imagine Kali picking it up by the hair, holding it at arm's length, and laughing. Not in cruelty, but in recognition: "Is this what had me? This?" That moment of lightness is the beginning of Chamunda's freedom.
verses.commentary: Chanda ("passion") and Munda ("stubbornness") are the two most insidious inner enemies — not because they are powerful but because they disguise themselves as virtues: passion masquerades as enthusiasm, stubbornness as conviction. Kali's laughter as she presents them to the Mother is significant: the fierce energy laughs at what seemed so formidable. What once held you in terror becomes, to the awakened one, almost comic in its pretension.

verses.wordMeaning: Likewise Vishnu's Energy, seated upon Garuda, advanced with conch, discus, club, bow and scymitar in hand.

verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Likewise Vishnu's Energy, seated upon Garuda, advanced with conch, discus, club, bow and scymitar in hand.

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञवाराहमतुलं रूपं या बिभ्रतो हरेः । शक्तिः साप्याययौ तत्र वाराहीं बिभ्रती तनुम्
verses.transliteration: yaj~navArAhamatulaM rUpaM yA bibhrato hareH | shaktiH sApyAyayau tatra vArAhIM bibhratI tanum
verses.translation: The Energy of Hari, who assumes the peerless form of a sacrificial boar, she also advanced there, assuming a boar-like form.
verses.wordMeaning: The Energy of Hari, who assumes the peerless form of a sacrificial boar, she also advanced there, assuming a boar-like form.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The Energy of Hari, who assumes the peerless form of a sacrificial boar, she also advanced there, assuming a boar-like form.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The Energy of Hari, who assumes the peerless form of a sacrificial boar, she also advanced there, assuming a boar-like form.

verses.sanskrit: नारसिंही नृसिंहस्य बिभ्रती सदृशं वपुः । प्राप्ता तत्र सटाक्षेपक्षिप्तनक्षत्रसंहतिः
verses.transliteration: nArasiMhI nR^isiMhasya bibhratI sadR^ishaM vapuH | prAptA tatra saTAkShepakShiptanakShatrasaMhatiH
verses.translation: Narasimha's Energy, assuming a body like Nrisimha's, arrived there, adorned with a cluster of constellations hurled down by the tossing of his mane.
verses.wordMeaning: Narasimha's Energy, assuming a body like Nrisimha's, arrived there, adorned with a cluster of constellations hurled down by the tossing of his mane.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Narasimha's Energy, assuming a body like Nrisimha's, arrived there, adorned with a cluster of constellations hurled down by the tossing of his mane.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Narasimha's Energy, assuming a body like Nrisimha's, arrived there, adorned with a cluster of constellations hurled down by the tossing of his mane.

verses.sanskrit: वज्रहस्ता तथैवैन्द्री गजराजोपरि स्थिता । प्राप्ता सहस्रनयना यथा शक्रस्तथैव सा
verses.transliteration: vajrahastA tathaivaindrI gajarAjopari sthitA | prAptA sahasranayanA yathA shakrastathaiva sA
verses.translation: Likewise Indra's Energy, with thunderbolt in hand, seated upon the lord of elephants and having a thousand eyes, arrived; as is Shakra, such indeed was she.
verses.wordMeaning: Likewise Indra's Energy, with thunderbolt in hand, seated upon the lord of elephants and having a thousand eyes, arrived; as is Shakra, such indeed was she.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Likewise Indra's Energy, with thunderbolt in hand, seated upon the lord of elephants and having a thousand eyes, arrived; as is Shakra, such indeed was she.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Likewise Indra's Energy, with thunderbolt in hand, seated upon the lord of elephants and having a thousand eyes, arrived; as is Shakra, such indeed was she.

verses.sanskrit: ततः परिवृतस्ताभिरीशानो देवशक्तिभिः । हन्यन्तामसुराः शीघ्रं मम प्रीत्याह चण्डिकाम्
verses.transliteration: tataH parivR^itastAbhirIshAno devashaktibhiH | hanyantAmasurAH shIghraM mama prItyAha chaNDikAm
verses.translation: Then Shiva, surrounded by those Energies of the gods, said to Chandika, 'Let the Asuras be slain forthwith through my good-will.'
verses.wordMeaning: Then Shiva, surrounded by those Energies of the gods, said to Chandika, 'Let the Asuras be slain forthwith through my good-will.'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then Shiva, surrounded by those Energies of the gods, said to Chandika, 'Let the Asuras be slain forthwith through my good-will.'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then Shiva, surrounded by those Energies of the gods, said to Chandika, 'Let the Asuras be slain forthwith through my good-will.'

verses.sanskrit: ततो देवीशरीरात्तु विनिष्क्रान्तातिभीषणा । चण्डिका शक्तिरत्युग्रा शिवाशतनिनादिनी
verses.transliteration: tato devIsharIrAttu viniShkrAntAtibhIShaNA | chaNDikA shaktiratyugrA shivAshataninAdinI
verses.translation: Thereupon from the goddess' body there came forth Chandika's Energy, most terrific, exceedingly fierce, howling like a hundred jackals.
verses.wordMeaning: Thereupon from the goddess' body there came forth Chandika's Energy, most terrific, exceedingly fierce, howling like a hundred jackals.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Thereupon from the goddess' body there came forth Chandika's Energy, most terrific, exceedingly fierce, howling like a hundred jackals.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Thereupon from the goddess' body there came forth Chandika's Energy, most terrific, exceedingly fierce, howling like a hundred jackals.

verses.sanskrit: सा चाह धूम्रजटिलमीशानमपराजिता । दूत त्वं गच्छ भगवन् पार्श्वं शुम्भनिशुम्भयोः
verses.transliteration: sA chAha dhUmrajaTilamIshAnamaparAjitA | dUta tvaM gachCha bhagavan pArshvaM shumbhanishumbhayoH
verses.translation: And she, the unconquered, said to Shiva, who was smoke-coloured and had matted locks, 'Be thou, my lord, a messenger to the presence of Shumbha and Nishumbha.'
verses.wordMeaning: And she, the unconquered, said to Shiva, who was smoke-coloured and had matted locks, 'Be thou, my lord, a messenger to the presence of Shumbha and Nishumbha.'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And she, the unconquered, said to Shiva, who was smoke-coloured and had matted locks, 'Be thou, my lord, a messenger to the presence of Shumbha and Nishumbha.'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And she, the unconquered, said to Shiva, who was smoke-coloured and had matted locks, 'Be thou, my lord, a messenger to the presence of Shumbha and Nishumbha.'

verses.sanskrit: ब्रूहि शुम्भं निशुम्भं च दानवावतिगर्वितौ । ये चान्ये दानवास्तत्र युद्धाय समुपस्थिताः
verses.transliteration: brUhi shumbhaM nishumbhaM cha dAnavAvatigarvitau | ye chAnye dAnavAstatra yuddhAya samupasthitAH
verses.translation: 'Say unto the two overweening Danavas, Shumbha and Nishumbha, and to whatever other Danavas are assembled there to do battle:'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Say unto the two overweening Danavas, Shumbha and Nishumbha, and to whatever other Danavas are assembled there to do battle:'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'Say unto the two overweening Danavas, Shumbha and Nishumbha, and to whatever other Danavas are assembled there to do battle:'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'Say unto the two overweening Danavas, Shumbha and Nishumbha, and to whatever other Danavas are assembled there to do battle:'

verses.sanskrit: त्रैलोक्यमिन्द्रो लभतां देवाः सन्तु हविर्भुजः । यूयं प्रयात पातालं यदि जीवितुमिच्छथ
verses.transliteration: trailokyamindro labhatAM devAH santu havirbhujaH | yUyaM prayAta pAtAlaM yadi jIvitumichChatha
verses.translation: 'Let Indra obtain the three worlds, let the gods be the enjoyers of the oblations; go ye to Patala if ye wish to live.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Let Indra obtain the three worlds, let the gods be the enjoyers of the oblations; go ye to Patala if ye wish to live.'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'Let Indra obtain the three worlds, let the gods be the enjoyers of the oblations; go ye to Patala if ye wish to live.'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'Let Indra obtain the three worlds, let the gods be the enjoyers of the oblations; go ye to Patala if ye wish to live.'

verses.sanskrit: बलावलेपादथ चेद्भवन्तो युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः । तदागच्छत तृप्यन्तु मच्छिवाः पिशितेन वः
verses.transliteration: balAvalepAdatha chedbhavanto yuddhakA~NkShiNaH | tadAgachChata tR^ipyantu machChivAH pishitena vaH
verses.translation: 'Yet if through pride in your strength ye are longing for battle, come ye on then! Let my jackals be glutted with your flesh.'
verses.wordMeaning: 'Yet if through pride in your strength ye are longing for battle, come ye on then! Let my jackals be glutted with your flesh.'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'Yet if through pride in your strength ye are longing for battle, come ye on then! Let my jackals be glutted with your flesh.'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): 'Yet if through pride in your strength ye are longing for battle, come ye on then! Let my jackals be glutted with your flesh.'

verses.sanskrit: यतो नियुक्तो दौत्येन तया देव्या शिवः स्वयम् । शिवदूतीति लोकेऽस्मिंस्ततः सा ख्यातिमागता
verses.transliteration: yato niyukto dautyena tayA devyA shivaH svayam | shivadUtIti loke.asmiMstataH sA khyAtimAgatA
verses.translation: Because the goddess appointed Shiva himself to be ambassador, she has hence attained fame as Shivaduti in this world.
verses.wordMeaning: Because the goddess appointed Shiva himself to be ambassador, she has hence attained fame as Shivaduti in this world.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Because the goddess appointed Shiva himself to be ambassador, she has hence attained fame as Shivaduti in this world.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Because the goddess appointed Shiva himself to be ambassador, she has hence attained fame as Shivaduti in this world.

verses.sanskrit: तेऽपि श्रुत्वा वचो देव्याः शर्वाख्यातं महासुराः । अमर्षापूरिता जग्मुर्यत्र कात्यायनी स्थिता
verses.transliteration: te.api shrutvA vacho devyAH sharvAkhyAtaM mahAsurAH | amarShApUritA jagmuryatra kAtyAyanI sthitA
verses.translation: Those great Asuras however, on hearing the goddess' speech fully announced, were filled with indignation and went where Katyayani stood.
verses.wordMeaning: Those great Asuras however, on hearing the goddess' speech fully announced, were filled with indignation and went where Katyayani stood.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Those great Asuras however, on hearing the goddess' speech fully announced, were filled with indignation and went where Katyayani stood.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Those great Asuras however, on hearing the goddess' speech fully announced, were filled with indignation and went where Katyayani stood.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रथममेवाग्रे शरशक्त्यृष्टिवृष्टिभिः । ववर्षुरुद्धतामर्षास्तां देवीममरारयः
verses.transliteration: tataH prathamamevAgre sharashaktyR^iShTivR^iShTibhiH | vavarShuruddhatAmarShAstAM devImamarArayaH
verses.translation: Then, at the very first, the arrogant and indignant foes of the Immortals in front poured on the goddess showers of arrows, javelins and spears.
verses.wordMeaning: Then, at the very first, the arrogant and indignant foes of the Immortals in front poured on the goddess showers of arrows, javelins and spears.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then, at the very first, the arrogant and indignant foes of the Immortals in front poured on the goddess showers of arrows, javelins and spears.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then, at the very first, the arrogant and indignant foes of the Immortals in front poured on the goddess showers of arrows, javelins and spears.

verses.sanskrit: सा च तान् प्रहितान् बाणाञ्छूलशक्तिपरश्वधान् । चिच्छेद लीलयाध्मातधनुर्मुक्तैर्महेषुभिः
verses.transliteration: sA cha tAn prahitAn bANA~nChUlashaktiparashvadhAn | chichCheda lIlayAdhmAtadhanurmuktairmaheShubhiH
verses.translation: And gracefully she clove those arrows, darts, spears and axes, which were hurled, with large arrows shot from her resounding bow.
verses.wordMeaning: And gracefully she clove those arrows, darts, spears and axes, which were hurled, with large arrows shot from her resounding bow.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And gracefully she clove those arrows, darts, spears and axes, which were hurled, with large arrows shot from her resounding bow.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And gracefully she clove those arrows, darts, spears and axes, which were hurled, with large arrows shot from her resounding bow.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याग्रतस्तथा काली शूलपातविदारितान् । खट्वाङ्गपोथितांश्चारीन्कुर्वती व्यचरत्तदा
verses.transliteration: tasyAgratastathA kAlI shUlapAtavidAritAn | khaTvA~NgapothitAMshchArInkurvatI vyacharattadA
verses.translation: And in front of her stalked Kali then, tearing the foes asunder with the onset of her darts and crushing them with her skull-topped staff.
verses.wordMeaning: And in front of her stalked Kali then, tearing the foes asunder with the onset of her darts and crushing them with her skull-topped staff.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And in front of her stalked Kali then, tearing the foes asunder with the onset of her darts and crushing them with her skull-topped staff.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And in front of her stalked Kali then, tearing the foes asunder with the onset of her darts and crushing them with her skull-topped staff.

verses.sanskrit: कमण्डलुजलाक्षेपहतवीर्यान् हतौजसः । ब्रह्माणी चाकरोच्छत्रून्येन येन स्म धावति
verses.transliteration: kamaNDalujalAkShepahatavIryAn hataujasaH | brahmANI chAkarochChatrUnyena yena sma dhAvati
verses.translation: And Brahmani caused the foes to lose their courage by casting water on them from her earthen pot, and weakened their vigour, by whatever way she ran.
verses.wordMeaning: And Brahmani caused the foes to lose their courage by casting water on them from her earthen pot, and weakened their vigour, by whatever way she ran.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And Brahmani caused the foes to lose their courage by casting water on them from her earthen pot, and weakened their vigour, by whatever way she ran.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And Brahmani caused the foes to lose their courage by casting water on them from her earthen pot, and weakened their vigour, by whatever way she ran.

verses.sanskrit: माहेश्वरी त्रिशूलेन तथा चक्रेण वैष्णवी । दैत्याञ्जघान कौमारी तथा शक्त्यातिकोपना
verses.transliteration: mAheshvarI trishUlena tathA chakreNa vaiShNavI | daityA~njaghAna kaumArI tathA shaktyAtikopanA
verses.translation: Maheshvara's Energy slew Daityas with her trident, and Vishnu's Energy with her discus, and Kumara's Energy, very wrathful, slew them with her javelin.
verses.wordMeaning: Maheshvara's Energy slew Daityas with her trident, and Vishnu's Energy with her discus, and Kumara's Energy, very wrathful, slew them with her javelin.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Maheshvara's Energy slew Daityas with her trident, and Vishnu's Energy with her discus, and Kumara's Energy, very wrathful, slew them with her javelin.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Maheshvara's Energy slew Daityas with her trident, and Vishnu's Energy with her discus, and Kumara's Energy, very wrathful, slew them with her javelin.

verses.sanskrit: ऐन्द्री कुलिशपातेन शतशो दैत्यदानवाः । पेतुर्विदारिताः पृथ्व्यां रुधिरौघप्रवर्षिणः
verses.transliteration: aindrI kulishapAtena shatasho daityadAnavAH | peturvidAritAH pR^ithvyAM rudhiraughapravarShiNaH
verses.translation: Torn to pieces by the down-rush of the thunderbolt hurled by Indra's Energy, Daityas and Danavas fell on the earth in hundreds, pouring out streams of blood.
verses.wordMeaning: Torn to pieces by the down-rush of the thunderbolt hurled by Indra's Energy, Daityas and Danavas fell on the earth in hundreds, pouring out streams of blood.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Torn to pieces by the down-rush of the thunderbolt hurled by Indra's Energy, Daityas and Danavas fell on the earth in hundreds, pouring out streams of blood.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Torn to pieces by the down-rush of the thunderbolt hurled by Indra's Energy, Daityas and Danavas fell on the earth in hundreds, pouring out streams of blood.

verses.sanskrit: तुण्डप्रहारविध्वस्ता दंष्ट्राग्रक्षतवक्षसः । वाराहमूर्त्या न्यपतंश्चक्रेण च विदारिताः
verses.transliteration: tuNDaprahAravidhvastA daMShTrAgrakShatavakShasaH | vArAhamUrtyA nyapataMshchakreNa cha vidAritAH
verses.translation: Shattered by the boar-embodied Energy with blows from her snout, wounded in their breasts by the points of her tushes, and torn by her discus, demons fell down.
verses.wordMeaning: Shattered by the boar-embodied Energy with blows from her snout, wounded in their breasts by the points of her tushes, and torn by her discus, demons fell down.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Shattered by the boar-embodied Energy with blows from her snout, wounded in their breasts by the points of her tushes, and torn by her discus, demons fell down.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Shattered by the boar-embodied Energy with blows from her snout, wounded in their breasts by the points of her tushes, and torn by her discus, demons fell down.

verses.sanskrit: नखैर्विदारितांश्चान्यान् भक्षयन्ती महासुरान् । नारसिंही चचाराजौ नादापूर्णदिगम्बरा
verses.transliteration: nakhairvidAritAMshchAnyAn bhakShayantI mahAsurAn | nArasiMhI chachArAjau nAdApUrNadigambarA
verses.translation: And Narasimha's Energy roamed about in the battle, devouring other great Asuras who were torn by her claws, as she filled the intermediate region of the sky with her roaring.
verses.wordMeaning: And Narasimha's Energy roamed about in the battle, devouring other great Asuras who were torn by her claws, as she filled the intermediate region of the sky with her roaring.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And Narasimha's Energy roamed about in the battle, devouring other great Asuras who were torn by her claws, as she filled the intermediate region of the sky with her roaring.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And Narasimha's Energy roamed about in the battle, devouring other great Asuras who were torn by her claws, as she filled the intermediate region of the sky with her roaring.

verses.sanskrit: चण्डाट्टहासैरसुराः शिवदूत्यभिदूषिताः । पेतुः पृथिव्यां पतितांस्तांश्चखादाथ सा तदा
verses.transliteration: chaNDATTahAsairasurAH shivadUtyabhidUShitAH | petuH pR^ithivyAM patitAMstAMshchakhAdAtha sA tadA
verses.translation: Asuras, demoralized by Shivaduti with her violent loud laughs, fell down on the earth; she then devoured those fallen ones.
verses.wordMeaning: Asuras, demoralized by Shivaduti with her violent loud laughs, fell down on the earth; she then devoured those fallen ones.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Asuras, demoralized by Shivaduti with her violent loud laughs, fell down on the earth; she then devoured those fallen ones.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Asuras, demoralized by Shivaduti with her violent loud laughs, fell down on the earth; she then devoured those fallen ones.

verses.sanskrit: इति मातृगणं क्रुद्धं मर्दयन्तं महासुरान् । दृष्ट्वाभ्युपायैर्विविधैर्नेशुर्देवारिसैनिकाः
verses.transliteration: iti mAtR^igaNaM kruddhaM mardayantaM mahAsurAn | dR^iShTvAbhyupAyairvividhairneshurdevArisainikAH
verses.translation: Seeing the enraged band of Mothers crushing the great Asuras thus by various means, the troops of the gods' foes perished.
verses.wordMeaning: Seeing the enraged band of Mothers crushing the great Asuras thus by various means, the troops of the gods' foes perished.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Seeing the enraged band of Mothers crushing the great Asuras thus by various means, the troops of the gods' foes perished.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Seeing the enraged band of Mothers crushing the great Asuras thus by various means, the troops of the gods' foes perished.

verses.sanskrit: पलायनपरान्दृष्ट्वा दैत्यान्मातृगणार्दितान् । योद्धुमभ्याययौ क्रुद्धो रक्तबीजो महासुरः
verses.transliteration: palAyanaparAndR^iShTvA daityAnmAtR^igaNArditAn | yoddhumabhyAyayau kruddho raktabIjo mahAsuraH
verses.translation: Raktavija, a great Asura, seeing the Daityas, who were hard-pressed by the band of Mothers, intent on fleeing, strode forward to fight in wrath.
verses.wordMeaning: Raktavija, a great Asura, seeing the Daityas, who were hard-pressed by the band of Mothers, intent on fleeing, strode forward to fight in wrath.

verses.sanskrit: रक्तबिन्दुर्यदा भूमौ पतत्यस्य शरीरतः । समुत्पतति मेदिन्यां तत्प्रमाणो महासुरः
verses.transliteration: raktabinduryadA bhUmau patatyasya sharIrataH | samutpatati medinyAM tatpramANo mahAsuraH
verses.translation: When from his body there falls to the ground a drop of blood, at that moment starts up from the earth an Asura of his stature.
verses.wordMeaning: When from his body there falls to the ground a drop of blood, at that moment starts up from the earth an Asura of his stature.

verses.sanskrit: युयुधे स गदापाणिरिन्द्रशक्त्या महासुरः । ततश्चैन्द्री स्ववज्रेण रक्तबीजमताडयत्
verses.transliteration: yuyudhe sa gadApANirindrashaktyA mahAsuraH | tatashchaindrI svavajreNa raktabIjamatADayat
verses.translation: He, a great Asura, with club in hand, fought with Indra's Energy, and Indra's Energy then struck Raktavija with her thunderbolt;

verses.sanskrit: कुलिशेनाहतस्याशु बहु सुस्राव शोणितम् । समुत्तस्थुस्ततो योधास्तद्रूपास्तत्पराक्रमाः
verses.transliteration: kulishenAhatasyAshu bahu susrAva shoNitam | samuttasthustato yodhAstadrUpAstatparAkramAH
verses.translation: blood flowed quickly from him when wounded by the thunderbolt. Thereupon stood up together fresh combatants, like him in body, like him in valour;

verses.sanskrit: यावन्तः पतितास्तस्य शरीराद्रक्तबिन्दवः । तावन्तः पुरुषा जातास्तद्वीर्यबलविक्रमाः
verses.transliteration: yAvantaH patitAstasya sharIrAdraktabindavaH | tAvantaH puruShA jAtAstadvIryabalavikramAH
verses.translation: for as many blood-drops fell from his body, so many men came into being, like him in courage, strength and valour.
verses.wordMeaning: for as many blood-drops fell from his body, so many men came into being, like him in courage, strength and valour.

verses.sanskrit: ते चापि युयुधुस्तत्र पुरुषा रक्तसम्भवाः । समं मातृभिरत्युग्रशस्त्रपातातिभीषणम्
verses.transliteration: te chApi yuyudhustatra puruShA raktasambhavAH | samaM mAtR^ibhiratyugrashastrapAtAtibhIShaNam
verses.translation: And those men also who sprang from his blood fought there with the Mothers in a combat, dreadful because of the sweep of their very sharp weapons.
verses.wordMeaning: And those men also who sprang from his blood fought there with the Mothers in a combat, dreadful because of the sweep of their very sharp weapons.

verses.transliteration: punashcha vajrapAtena kShatamasya shiro yadA | vavAha raktaM puruShAstato jAtAH sahasrashaH
verses.translation: And again when his head was wounded by the fall of her thunderbolt, his blood poured forth; therefrom were born men by thousands.
verses.wordMeaning: And again when his head was wounded by the fall of her thunderbolt, his blood poured forth; therefrom were born men by thousands.

verses.transliteration: vaiShNavI samare chainaM chakreNAbhijaghAna ha | gadayA tADayAmAsa aindrI tamasureshvaram
verses.translation: And Vishnu's Energy struck at this foe with her discus in the battle. Indra's Energy beat that lord of the Asuras with her club.

verses.transliteration: vaiShNavIchakrabhinnasya rudhirasrAvasambhavaiH | sahasrasho jagadvyAptaM tatpramANairmahAsuraiH
verses.translation: The world was filled by the thousands of great Asuras, who were his equals, and who sprang from the blood that flowed from him when cloven by the discus of Vishnu's Energy.

verses.transliteration: shaktyA jaghAna kaumArI vArAhI cha tathAsinA | mAheshvarI trishUlena raktabIjaM mahAsuram
verses.translation: Kumara's Energy struck the great Asura Raktavija with her spear, and Varaha's Energy also struck him with her sword, and Maheshvara's Energy with her trident.

verses.translation: And the Daitya Raktavija, that great Asura, filled full of wrath, struck every one of the Mothers in turn with his club.

verses.translation: By the stream of blood, which fell on the earth from him when he received many wounds from the spears, darts and other weapons, Asuras came verily into being in hundreds.

verses.translation: And those Asuras who sprang from that Asura's blood pervaded the whole world; thereat the gods fell into the utmost terror.

verses.translation: Seeing the gods dejected, Chandika spoke with haste; she said to Kali, 'O Chamunda! stretch out thy mouth wide;'

verses.translation: 'Roam about in the battle, devouring the great Asuras who sprang from him; so shall this Daitya, with his blood ebbing away, meet destruction.'

verses.translation: 'These fierce demons are being devoured by thee, and at the same time no others will be produced.' Having enjoined her thus, the goddess next smote him with her dart.

verses.sanskrit: तांश्चखादाथ चामुण्डा पपौ तस्य च शोणितम् । देवी शूलेन वज्रेण बाणैरसिभिरृष्टिभिः
verses.transliteration: tAMshchakhAdAtha chAmuNDA papau tasya cha shoNitam | devI shUlena vajreNa bANairasibhirR^iShTibhiH
verses.translation: Chamunda both devoured them and quaffed his blood. The goddess smote Raktavija with her dart, her thunderbolt, arrows, swords and spears,
verses.hindi: रक्तबीज का जितना रक्त पृथ्वी पर गिरता, उतने ही उसके समान महाबलशाली महादानव उत्पन्न हो जाते।
verses.wordMeaning: Raktabija — "blood-seed" — is the most psychologically sophisticated demon in the Saptashati. Every drop of his blood becomes a new demon equal in power to him. He cannot be killed by ordinary combat; fighting him directly multiplies him. He represents self-replicating thought patterns: the more you battle certain kinds of anxiety, craving, or obsession head-on, the more they proliferate. The solution is Kali — who opens her vast mouth and drinks the blood before it can touch the ground. The teaching: intercept the pattern at its source, before it takes root.
verses.explanation: Raktabija — "blood-seed" — is the most psychologically sophisticated demon in the Saptashati. Every drop of his blood becomes a new demon equal in power to him. He cannot be killed by ordinary combat; fighting him directly multiplies him. He represents self-replicating thought patterns: the more you battle certain kinds of anxiety, craving, or obsession head-on, the more they proliferate. The solution is Kali — who opens her vast mouth and drinks the blood before it can touch the ground. The teaching: intercept the pattern at its source, before it takes root.
verses.science: Research on the "ironic rebound" effect (Daniel Wegner): deliberate suppression of a thought ("do NOT think of a white bear") causes it to recur far more than if it were allowed freely. The more directly you fight Raktabija, the more you feed him. The clinical solution — mirroring Kali — is defusion: not drinking from the pattern's power by neither indulging nor suppressing, but simply not giving it ground to land.
verses.lifeLesson: Identify one thought pattern that multiplies the more you fight it. Today, instead of fighting it: observe it arising. Name it neutrally ("the anxiety is here again"). Do not let it land into action or rumination. Watch it appear, lose power, and dissolve — like blood drunk before it hits the ground. That is Kali's method.

He represents self-replicating thought patterns: the more you battle certain kinds of anxiety, craving, or obsession head-on, the more they proliferate. The solution is Kali — who opens her vast mouth and drinks the blood before it can touch the ground. The teaching: intercept the pattern at its source, before it takes root.

verses.sanskrit: कोपाध्मातो निशुम्भोऽथ शूलं जग्राह दानवः । आयातं मुष्टिपातेन देवी तच्चाप्यचूर्णयत्
verses.transliteration: kopAdhmAto nishumbho.atha shUlaM jagrAha dAnavaH | AyAtaM muShTipAtena devI tachchApyachUrNayat
verses.translation: Then Nishumbha, the Danava, puffed up with wrath, seized a dart; and that also, when it came, the goddess shattered with a blow of her fist.
verses.hindi: अपने प्राण-प्रिय भाई निशुम्भ को मारा हुआ देखकर, और सेना के नष्ट होते देखकर, शुम्भ क्रोध में बोला।
verses.wordMeaning: Shumbha and Nishumbha — pride and the ego's shadow — are twin demons, inseparable. When Nishumbha falls (the ego's outer defences collapse), Shumbha's fury intensifies — the last desperate assertion of the self that will not yield. This moment of escalating rage just before the final defeat is psychologically precise. In any genuine transformation, the pattern that is about to end often makes one final, most intense appearance.
verses.explanation: Shumbha and Nishumbha — pride and the ego's shadow — are twin demons, inseparable. When Nishumbha falls (the ego's outer defences collapse), Shumbha's fury intensifies — the last desperate assertion of the self that will not yield. This moment of escalating rage just before the final defeat is psychologically precise. In any genuine transformation, the pattern that is about to end often makes one final, most intense appearance.
verses.science: Extinction bursts in behavioural psychology: when a reinforced behaviour pattern stops receiving its reward, it briefly intensifies before extinguishing. Therapists and coaches know this as "the storm before the breakthrough." Patients in withdrawal, people in the final stages of ending a destructive relationship, practitioners at the edge of a breakthrough — all experience the Shumbha moment: maximum fury just before the final release.
verses.lifeLesson: If you are in a process of transformation and your old patterns suddenly seem to return with maximum ferocity — louder, more insistent, more desperate than ever — do not interpret this as failure. Recognise: Nishumbha has fallen. Shumbha is making his last stand. Hold steady. The Goddess is not retreating; she is preparing the final stroke.
verses.commentary: Shumbha and Nishumbha — pride and the ego's shadow — are twin demons, inseparable. verses.transliteration: pUrayAmAsa kakubho nijaghaNTAsvanena cha | samastadaityasainyAnAM tejovadhavidhAyinA
verses.translation: And she filled all regions with the clanging of her bell, which caused the vigour of all the Daitya hosts to die away.
verses.wordMeaning: And she filled all regions with the clanging of her bell, which caused the vigour of all the Daitya hosts to die away.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And she filled all regions with the clanging of her bell, which caused the vigour of all the Daitya hosts to die away.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And she filled all regions with the clanging of her bell, which caused the vigour of all the Daitya hosts to die away.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सिंहो महानादैस्त्याजितेभमहामदैः । पूरयामास गगनं गां तथैव दिशो दश
verses.transliteration: tataH siMho mahAnAdaistyAjitebhamahAmadaiH | pUrayAmAsa gaganaM gAM tathaiva disho dasha
verses.translation: Then her lion filled the heaven, the earth and the ten regions of the sky with loud roars, which checked the copious flow of the exudation from the demons' rutting elephants.
verses.wordMeaning: Then her lion filled the heaven, the earth and the ten regions of the sky with loud roars, which checked the copious flow of the exudation from the demons' rutting elephants.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then her lion filled the heaven, the earth and the ten regions of the sky with loud roars, which checked the copious flow of the exudation from the demons' rutting elephants.
