verses.sanskrit: ततः काली समुत्पत्य गगनं क्ष्मामताडयत् । कराभ्यां तन्निनादेन प्राक्स्वनास्ते तिरोहिताः
verses.transliteration: tataH kAlI samutpatya gaganaM kShmAmatADayat | karAbhyAM tanninAdena prAk.hsvanAste tirohitAH
verses.translation: Kali, springing upward, then struck the heaven and the earth with both her hands; the boom thereof drowned those previous sounds.
verses.wordMeaning: Kali, springing upward, then struck the heaven and the earth with both her hands; the boom thereof drowned those previous sounds.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Kali, springing upward, then struck the heaven and the earth with both her hands; the boom thereof drowned those previous sounds.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Kali, springing upward, then struck the heaven and the earth with both her hands; the boom thereof drowned those previous sounds.

verses.sanskrit: अट्टाट्टहासमशिवं शिवदूती चकार ह । वैः शब्दैरसुरास्त्रेसुः शुम्भः कोपं परं ययौ
verses.transliteration: aTTATTahAsamashivaM shivadUtI chakAra ha | vaiH shabdairasurAstresuH shumbhaH kopaM paraM yayau
verses.translation: Shivaduti uttered a loud inauspicious laugh. At those sounds the Asuras trembled; Shumbha gave way to utmost rage.
verses.wordMeaning: Shivaduti uttered a loud inauspicious laugh. At those sounds the Asuras trembled; Shumbha gave way to utmost rage.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Shivaduti uttered a loud inauspicious laugh. At those sounds the Asuras trembled; Shumbha gave way to utmost rage.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Shivaduti uttered a loud inauspicious laugh. At those sounds the Asuras trembled; Shumbha gave way to utmost rage.

verses.sanskrit: दुरात्मंस्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति व्याजहाराम्बिका यदा । तदा जयेत्यभिहितं देवैराकाशसंस्थितैः
verses.transliteration: durAtmaMstiShTha tiShTheti vyAjahArAmbikA yadA | tadA jayetyabhihitaM devairAkAshasaMsthitaiH
verses.translation: When Ambika cried out 'Stand, O evil-souled! stand!', the gods who had taken their stations in the air then called to her, 'Be thou victorious!'
verses.wordMeaning: When Ambika cried out 'Stand, O evil-souled! stand!', the gods who had taken their stations in the air then called to her, 'Be thou victorious!'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): When Ambika cried out 'Stand, O evil-souled! stand!', the gods who had taken their stations in the air then called to her, 'Be thou victorious!'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): When Ambika cried out 'Stand, O evil-souled! stand!', the gods who had taken their stations in the air then called to her, 'Be thou victorious!'

verses.sanskrit: शुम्भेनागत्य या शक्तिर्मुक्ता ज्वालातिभीषणा । आयान्ती वह्निकूटाभा सा निरस्ता महोल्कया
verses.transliteration: shumbhenAgatya yA shaktirmuktA jvAlAtibhIShaNA | AyAntI vahnikUTAbhA sA nirastA maholkayA
verses.translation: The spear flaming most terribly, which Shumbha approaching hurled—that, gleaming like a mass of fire as it came along, was driven aside by a great fire-brand.
verses.wordMeaning: The spear flaming most terribly, which Shumbha approaching hurled—that, gleaming like a mass of fire as it came along, was driven aside by a great fire-brand.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The spear flaming most terribly, which Shumbha approaching hurled—that, gleaming like a mass of fire as it came along, was driven aside by a great fire-brand.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The spear flaming most terribly, which Shumbha approaching hurled—that, gleaming like a mass of fire as it came along, was driven aside by a great fire-brand.

verses.sanskrit: सिंहनादेन शुम्भस्य व्याप्तं लोकत्रयान्तरम् । निर्घातनिःस्वनो घोरो जितवानवनीपते
verses.transliteration: siMhanAdena shumbhasya vyAptaM lokatrayAntaram | nirghAtaniHsvano ghoro jitavAnavanIpate
verses.translation: The vault between the three worlds reverberated with Shumbha's lion-like roaring, but the dreadful sound of the slaughter among his soldiers surpassed that, O king.
verses.wordMeaning: The vault between the three worlds reverberated with Shumbha's lion-like roaring, but the dreadful sound of the slaughter among his soldiers surpassed that, O king.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The vault between the three worlds reverberated with Shumbha's lion-like roaring, but the dreadful sound of the slaughter among his soldiers surpassed that, O king.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The vault between the three worlds reverberated with Shumbha's lion-like roaring, but the dreadful sound of the slaughter among his soldiers surpassed that, O king.

verses.sanskrit: शुम्भमुक्ताञ्छरान्देवी शुम्भस्तत्प्रहिताञ्छरान् । चिच्छेद स्वशरैरुग्रैः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः
verses.transliteration: shumbhamuktA~nCharAndevI shumbhastatprahitA~nCharAn | chichCheda svasharairugraiH shatasho.atha sahasrashaH
verses.translation: The goddess split the arrows shot by Shumbha, and Shumbha the arrows that she discharged, each with her and his sharp arrows in hundreds and thousands.
verses.wordMeaning: The goddess split the arrows shot by Shumbha, and Shumbha the arrows that she discharged, each with her and his sharp arrows in hundreds and thousands.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The goddess split the arrows shot by Shumbha, and Shumbha the arrows that she discharged, each with her and his sharp arrows in hundreds and thousands.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The goddess split the arrows shot by Shumbha, and Shumbha the arrows that she discharged, each with her and his sharp arrows in hundreds and thousands.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सा चण्डिका क्रुद्धा शूलेनाभिजघान तम् । स तदाभिहतो भूमौ मूर्च्छितो निपपात ह
verses.transliteration: tataH sA chaNDikA kruddhA shUlenAbhijaghAna tam | sa tadAbhihato bhUmau mUrchChito nipapAta ha
verses.translation: Chandika, enraged thereat, smote him with a dart. Wounded therewith, he fell in a faint to the ground.
verses.wordMeaning: Chandika, enraged thereat, smote him with a dart. Wounded therewith, he fell in a faint to the ground.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Chandika, enraged thereat, smote him with a dart. Wounded therewith, he fell in a faint to the ground.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Chandika, enraged thereat, smote him with a dart. Wounded therewith, he fell in a faint to the ground.

verses.sanskrit: ततो निशुम्भः सम्प्राप्य चेतनामात्तकार्मुकः । आजघान शरैर्देवीं कालीं केसरिणं तथा
verses.transliteration: tato nishumbhaH samprApya chetanAmAttakArmukaH | AjaghAna sharairdevIM kAlIM kesariNaM tathA
verses.translation: Thereupon Nishumbha, regaining consciousness, seized his bow again and struck the goddess, and Kali and the lion, with arrows.
verses.wordMeaning: Thereupon Nishumbha, regaining consciousness, seized his bow again and struck the goddess, and Kali and the lion, with arrows.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Thereupon Nishumbha, regaining consciousness, seized his bow again and struck the goddess, and Kali and the lion, with arrows.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Thereupon Nishumbha, regaining consciousness, seized his bow again and struck the goddess, and Kali and the lion, with arrows.

verses.sanskrit: पुनश्च कृत्वा बाहूनामयुतं दनुजेश्वरः । चक्रायुधेन दितिजश्छादयामास चण्डिकाम्
verses.transliteration: punashcha kR^itvA bAhUnAmayutaM danujeshvaraH | chakrAyudhena ditijashChAdayAmAsa chaNDikAm
verses.translation: And the Danava lord, that son of Diti, putting forth a myriad arms, again covered Chandika with a myriad discuses.
verses.wordMeaning: And the Danava lord, that son of Diti, putting forth a myriad arms, again covered Chandika with a myriad discuses.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And the Danava lord, that son of Diti, putting forth a myriad arms, again covered Chandika with a myriad discuses.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And the Danava lord, that son of Diti, putting forth a myriad arms, again covered Chandika with a myriad discuses.

verses.sanskrit: ततो भगवती क्रुद्धा दुर्गा दुर्गार्तिनाशिनी । चिच्छेद देवी चक्राणि स्वशरैः सायकांश्च तान्
verses.transliteration: tato bhagavatI kruddhA durgA durgArtinAshinI | chichCheda devI chakrANi svasharaiH sAyakAMshcha tAn
verses.translation: The goddess then, enraged—she, Durga who destroys the afflictions of adversity—split those discuses and those arrows with her own arrows.
verses.wordMeaning: The goddess then, enraged—she, Durga who destroys the afflictions of adversity—split those discuses and those arrows with her own arrows.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The goddess then, enraged—she, Durga who destroys the afflictions of adversity—split those discuses and those arrows with her own arrows.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The goddess then, enraged—she, Durga who destroys the afflictions of adversity—split those discuses and those arrows with her own arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततो निशुम्भो वेगेन गदामादाय चण्डिकाम् । अभ्यधावत वै हन्तुं दैत्यसैन्यसमावृतः
verses.transliteration: tato nishumbho vegena gadAmAdAya chaNDikAm | abhyadhAvata vai hantuM daityasainyasamAvR^itaH
verses.translation: Then Nishumbha, seizing his club, rushed impetuously at Chandika to slay her outright, with the Daitya host surrounding him.
verses.wordMeaning: Then Nishumbha, seizing his club, rushed impetuously at Chandika to slay her outright, with the Daitya host surrounding him.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then Nishumbha, seizing his club, rushed impetuously at Chandika to slay her outright, with the Daitya host surrounding him.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then Nishumbha, seizing his club, rushed impetuously at Chandika to slay her outright, with the Daitya host surrounding him.

verses.sanskrit: तस्यापतत एवाशु गदां चिच्छेद चण्डिका । खड्गेन शितधारेण स च शूलं समाददे
verses.transliteration: tasyApatata evAshu gadAM chichCheda chaNDikA | khaDgena shitadhAreNa sa cha shUlaM samAdade
verses.translation: As he was just falling upon her, Chandika swiftly clove his club with her sharp-edged scymitar. And he took hold of a dart.
verses.wordMeaning: As he was just falling upon her, Chandika swiftly clove his club with her sharp-edged scymitar. And he took hold of a dart.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): As he was just falling upon her, Chandika swiftly clove his club with her sharp-edged scymitar. And he took hold of a dart.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): As he was just falling upon her, Chandika swiftly clove his club with her sharp-edged scymitar. And he took hold of a dart.

verses.sanskrit: शूलहस्तं समायान्तं निशुम्भममरार्दनम् । हृदि विव्याध शूलेन वेगाविद्धेन चण्डिका
verses.transliteration: shUlahastaM samAyAntaM nishumbhamamarArdanam | hR^idi vivyAdha shUlena vegAviddhena chaNDikA
verses.translation: Chandika, with a dart hurled swiftly, pierced Nishumbha, the afflicter of the Immortals, in the heart, as he approached with dart in hand.
verses.wordMeaning: Chandika, with a dart hurled swiftly, pierced Nishumbha, the afflicter of the Immortals, in the heart, as he approached with dart in hand.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Chandika, with a dart hurled swiftly, pierced Nishumbha, the afflicter of the Immortals, in the heart, as he approached with dart in hand.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Chandika, with a dart hurled swiftly, pierced Nishumbha, the afflicter of the Immortals, in the heart, as he approached with dart in hand.

verses.sanskrit: भिन्नस्य तस्य शूलेन हृदयान्निःसृतोऽपरः । महाबलो महावीर्यस्तिष्ठेति पुरुषो वदन्
verses.transliteration: bhinnasya tasya shUlena hR^idayAnniHsR^ito.aparaH | mahAbalo mahAvIryastiShTheti puruSho vadan
verses.translation: When he was pierced by the dart, out of his heart issued another man of great strength and great valour, exclaiming 'Stand!'
verses.wordMeaning: When he was pierced by the dart, out of his heart issued another man of great strength and great valour, exclaiming 'Stand!'
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): When he was pierced by the dart, out of his heart issued another man of great strength and great valour, exclaiming 'Stand!'
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): When he was pierced by the dart, out of his heart issued another man of great strength and great valour, exclaiming 'Stand!'

verses.sanskrit: तस्य निष्क्रामतो देवी प्रहस्य स्वनवत्ततः । शिरश्चिच्छेद खड्गेन ततोऽसावपतद्भुवि
verses.transliteration: tasya niShkrAmato devI prahasya svanavattataH | shirashchichCheda khaDgena tato.asAvapatadbhuvi
verses.translation: When he stepped forth, the goddess, laughing aloud, then struck off his head with her scymitar; thereupon he fell to the ground.
verses.wordMeaning: When he stepped forth, the goddess, laughing aloud, then struck off his head with her scymitar; thereupon he fell to the ground.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): When he stepped forth, the goddess, laughing aloud, then struck off his head with her scymitar; thereupon he fell to the ground.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): When he stepped forth, the goddess, laughing aloud, then struck off his head with her scymitar; thereupon he fell to the ground.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सिंहश्चखादोग्रदंष्ट्राक्षुण्णशिरोधरान् । असुरांस्तांस्तथा काली शिवदूती तथापरान्
verses.transliteration: tataH siMhashchakhAdogradaMShTrAkShuNNashirodharAn | asurAMstAMstathA kAlI shivadUtI tathAparAn
verses.translation: The lion then devoured those Asuras whose necks he had crushed with his savage teeth, and Kali and Shivaduti devoured the others.
verses.wordMeaning: The lion then devoured those Asuras whose necks he had crushed with his savage teeth, and Kali and Shivaduti devoured the others.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The lion then devoured those Asuras whose necks he had crushed with his savage teeth, and Kali and Shivaduti devoured the others.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The lion then devoured those Asuras whose necks he had crushed with his savage teeth, and Kali and Shivaduti devoured the others.

verses.sanskrit: कौमारीशक्तिनिर्भिन्नाः केचिन्नेशुर्महासुराः । ब्रह्माणीमन्त्रपूतेन तोयेनान्ये निराकृताः
verses.transliteration: kaumArIshaktinirbhinnAH kechinneshurmahAsurAH | brahmANImantrapUtena toyenAnye nirAkR^itAH
verses.translation: Some great Asuras perished, being pierced through by the spear held by Kumara's Energy; others were driven back by the water purified by the spell uttered by Brahma's Energy;
verses.wordMeaning: Some great Asuras perished, being pierced through by the spear held by Kumara's Energy; others were driven back by the water purified by the spell uttered by Brahma's Energy;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Some great Asuras perished, being pierced through by the spear held by Kumara's Energy; others were driven back by the water purified by the spell uttered by Brahma's Energy;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Some great Asuras perished, being pierced through by the spear held by Kumara's Energy; others were driven back by the water purified by the spell uttered by Brahma's Energy;

verses.sanskrit: माहेश्वरीत्रिशूलेन भिन्नाः पेतुस्तथापरे । वाराहीतुण्डघातेन केचिच्चूर्णीकृता भुवि
verses.transliteration: mAheshvarItrishUlena bhinnAH petustathApare | vArAhItuNDaghAtena kechichchUrNIkR^itA bhuvi
verses.translation: and others fell, pierced by the trident wielded by Shiva's Energy; some were pounded to dust on the ground by blows from the snout of Varaha's Energy;
verses.wordMeaning: and others fell, pierced by the trident wielded by Shiva's Energy; some were pounded to dust on the ground by blows from the snout of Varaha's Energy;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and others fell, pierced by the trident wielded by Shiva's Energy; some were pounded to dust on the ground by blows from the snout of Varaha's Energy;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and others fell, pierced by the trident wielded by Shiva's Energy; some were pounded to dust on the ground by blows from the snout of Varaha's Energy;

verses.sanskrit: खण्डं खण्डं च चक्रेण वैष्णव्या दानवाः कृताः । वज्रेण चैन्द्रीहस्ताग्रविमुक्तेन तथापरे
verses.transliteration: khaNDaM khaNDaM cha chakreNa vaiShNavyA dAnavAH kR^itAH | vajreNa chaindrIhastAgravimuktena tathApare
verses.translation: some Danavas were cut to pieces by the discus hurled by Vishnu's Energy; and others again by the thunderbolt discharged from the fingers of Indra's Energy.
verses.wordMeaning: some Danavas were cut to pieces by the discus hurled by Vishnu's Energy; and others again by the thunderbolt discharged from the fingers of Indra's Energy.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): some Danavas were cut to pieces by the discus hurled by Vishnu's Energy; and others again by the thunderbolt discharged from the fingers of Indra's Energy.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): some Danavas were cut to pieces by the discus hurled by Vishnu's Energy; and others again by the thunderbolt discharged from the fingers of Indra's Energy.

verses.sanskrit: केचिद्विनेशुरसुराः केचिन्नष्टा महाहवात् । भक्षिताश्चापरे कालीशिवदूतीमृगाधिपैः
verses.transliteration: kechidvineshurasurAH kechinnaShTA mahAhavAt | bhakShitAshchApare kAlIshivadUtImR^igAdhipaiH
verses.translation: Some Asuras perished outright, some fled from the great battle, and others were devoured by Kali, Shivaduti and the lion.
verses.wordMeaning: Some Asuras perished outright, some fled from the great battle, and others were devoured by Kali, Shivaduti and the lion.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Some Asuras perished outright, some fled from the great battle, and others were devoured by Kali, Shivaduti and the lion.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Some Asuras perished outright, some fled from the great battle, and others were devoured by Kali, Shivaduti and the lion.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ ऋषिरुवाच
verses.transliteration: OM R^iShiruvAcha
verses.translation: Om. The rishi spoke:
verses.wordMeaning: Om. The rishi spoke:
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Om. The rishi spoke:
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Om. The rishi spoke:

verses.sanskrit: निशुम्भं निहतं दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरं प्राणसम्मितम् । हन्यमानं बलं चैव शुम्भः क्रुद्धोऽब्रवीद्वचः
verses.transliteration: nishumbhaM nihataM dR^iShTvA bhrAtaraM prANasammitam | hanyamAnaM balaM chaiva shumbhaH kruddho.abravIdvachaH
verses.translation: Seeing his brother Nishumbha slain, who was dear to him as his life, and his army being slaughtered, Shumbha in wrath spoke thus:
verses.wordMeaning: Seeing his brother Nishumbha slain, who was dear to him as his life, and his army being slaughtered, Shumbha in wrath spoke thus:

verses.sanskrit: बलावलेपदुष्टे त्वं मा दुर्गे गर्वमावह । अन्यासां बलमाश्रित्य युद्ध्यसे चातिमानिनी
verses.transliteration: balAvalepaduShTe tvaM mA durge garvamAvaha | anyAsAM balamAshritya yuddhyase chAtimAninI
verses.translation: 'O Durga, who art tainted with the arrogance of strength, bring not thy pride here, thou who, trusting in the strength of the other goddesses, dost fight in exceeding haughtiness!'
verses.wordMeaning: 'O Durga, who art tainted with the arrogance of strength, bring not thy pride here, thou who, trusting in the strength of the other goddesses, dost fight in exceeding haughtiness!'

verses.transliteration: devyuvAcha

verses.sanskrit: एकैवाहं जगत्यत्र द्वितीया का ममापरा । पश्यैता दुष्ट मय्येव विशन्त्यो मद्विभूतयः
verses.transliteration: ekaivAhaM jagatyatra dvitIyA kA mamAparA | pashyaitA duShTa mayyeva vishantyo madvibhUtayaH
verses.translation: Alone verily am I in the world here; what other goddess is there besides me? See, vile one! that these goddesses, who have their divine power from me, are entering into me indeed.
verses.wordMeaning: Alone verily am I in the world here; what other goddess is there besides me? See, vile one! that these goddesses, who have their divine power from me, are entering into me indeed.

verses.sanskrit: ततः समस्तास्ता देव्यो ब्रह्माणीप्रमुखा लयम् । तस्या देव्यास्तनौ जग्मुरेकैवासीत्तदाम्बिका
verses.transliteration: tataH samastAstA devyo brahmANIpramukhA layam | tasyA devyAstanau jagmurekaivAsIttadAmbikA
verses.translation: Then all those goddesses, Brahmani and the others, became absorbed into the body of the goddess; Ambika then remained alone indeed.
verses.wordMeaning: Then all those goddesses, Brahmani and the others, became absorbed into the body of the goddess; Ambika then remained alone indeed.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then all those goddesses, Brahmani and the others, became absorbed into the body of the goddess; Ambika then remained alone indeed.

verses.sanskrit: देव्युवाच
verses.transliteration: devyuvAcha
verses.translation: The goddess spoke:
verses.wordMeaning: The goddess spoke:

verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The goddess spoke:

verses.sanskrit: अहं विभूत्या बहुभिरिह रूपैर्यदास्थिता । तत्संहृतं मयैकैव तिष्ठाम्याजौ स्थिरो भव
verses.transliteration: ahaM vibhUtyA bahubhiriha rUpairyadAsthitA | tatsaMhR^itaM mayaikaiva tiShThAmyAjau sthiro bhava
verses.translation: Whereas I existed with my divine power in many forms here—that has been drawn in by me; truly alone I stand now. Be thou steadfast in combat!
verses.wordMeaning: Whereas I existed with my divine power in many forms here—that has been drawn in by me; truly alone I stand now. Be thou steadfast in combat!
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Whereas I existed with my divine power in many forms here—that has been drawn in by me; truly alone I stand now. Be thou steadfast in combat!

verses.sanskrit: ऋषिरुवाच
verses.transliteration: R^iShiruvAcha
verses.translation: The rishi spoke:

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं देव्याः शुम्भस्य चोभयोः । पश्यतां सर्वदेवानामसुराणां च दारुणम्
verses.transliteration: tataH pravavR^ite yuddhaM devyAH shumbhasya chobhayoH | pashyatAM sarvadevAnAmasurANAM cha dAruNam
verses.translation: Thereupon commenced a battle between them both, the goddess and Shumbha, while all the gods and the Asuras looked on—a battle without quarter.
verses.wordMeaning: Thereupon commenced a battle between them both, the goddess and Shumbha, while all the gods and the Asuras looked on—a battle without quarter.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Thereupon commenced a battle between them both, the goddess and Shumbha, while all the gods and the Asuras looked on—a battle without quarter.

verses.sanskrit: शरवर्षैः शितैः शस्त्रैस्तथा चास्त्रैः सुदारुणैः । तयोर्युद्धमभूद्भूयः सर्वलोकभयङ्करम्
verses.transliteration: sharavarShaiH shitaiH shastraistathA chAstraiH sudAruNaiH | tayoryuddhamabhUdbhUyaH sarvalokabhaya~Nkaram
verses.translation: With showers of arrows, with sharp weapons and also with pitiless missiles, both engaged anew in a combat which set all the world in fear.
verses.wordMeaning: With showers of arrows, with sharp weapons and also with pitiless missiles, both engaged anew in a combat which set all the world in fear.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): With showers of arrows, with sharp weapons and also with pitiless missiles, both engaged anew in a combat which set all the world in fear.

verses.sanskrit: दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि शतशो मुमुचे यान्यथाम्बिका । बभञ्ज तानि दैत्येन्द्रस्तत्प्रतीघातकर्तृभिः
verses.transliteration: divyAnyastrANi shatasho mumuche yAnyathAmbikA | babha~nja tAni daityendrastatpratIghAtakartR^ibhiH
verses.translation: And the lord of the Daityas broke the heavenly missiles, which Ambika discharged in hundreds, with weapons that parried them.
verses.wordMeaning: And the lord of the Daityas broke the heavenly missiles, which Ambika discharged in hundreds, with weapons that parried them.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And the lord of the Daityas broke the heavenly missiles, which Ambika discharged in hundreds, with weapons that parried them.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And the lord of the Daityas broke the heavenly missiles, which Ambika discharged in hundreds, with weapons that parried them.

verses.sanskrit: मुक्तानि तेन चास्त्राणि दिव्यानि परमेश्वरी । बभञ्ज लीलयैवोग्रहुङ्कारोच्चारणादिभिः
verses.transliteration: muktAni tena chAstrANi divyAni parameshvarI | babha~nja lIlayaivograhu~NkArochchAraNAdibhiH
verses.translation: And the supreme goddess in merest play broke the heavenly missiles that he discharged, with fierce shouts, ejaculations and other sounds.
verses.wordMeaning: And the supreme goddess in merest play broke the heavenly missiles that he discharged, with fierce shouts, ejaculations and other sounds.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And the supreme goddess in merest play broke the heavenly missiles that he discharged, with fierce shouts, ejaculations and other sounds.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And the supreme goddess in merest play broke the heavenly missiles that he discharged, with fierce shouts, ejaculations and other sounds.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शरशतैर्देवीमाच्छादयत सोऽसुरः । सापि तत्कुपिता देवी धनुश्चिच्छेद चेषुभिः
verses.transliteration: tataH sharashatairdevImAchChAdayata so.asuraH | sApi tatkupitA devI dhanushchichCheda cheShubhiH
verses.translation: Then the Asura covered the goddess with hundreds of arrows, and the goddess, enraged thereat, split his bow also with her arrows.
verses.wordMeaning: Then the Asura covered the goddess with hundreds of arrows, and the goddess, enraged thereat, split his bow also with her arrows.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then the Asura covered the goddess with hundreds of arrows, and the goddess, enraged thereat, split his bow also with her arrows.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Then the Asura covered the goddess with hundreds of arrows, and the goddess, enraged thereat, split his bow also with her arrows.

verses.sanskrit: छिन्ने धनुषि दैत्येन्द्रस्तथा शक्तिमथाददे । चिच्छेद देवी चक्रेण तामप्यस्य करे स्थिताम्
verses.transliteration: Chinne dhanuShi daityendrastathA shaktimathAdade | chichCheda devI chakreNa tAmapyasya kare sthitAm
verses.translation: And when his bow was split, the lord of the Daityas took up his spear. The goddess split it, as he held it in his hand, with a discus.
verses.wordMeaning: And when his bow was split, the lord of the Daityas took up his spear. The goddess split it, as he held it in his hand, with a discus.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): And when his bow was split, the lord of the Daityas took up his spear. The goddess split it, as he held it in his hand, with a discus.

verses.sanskrit: ततः खड्गमुपादाय शतचन्द्रं च भानुमत् । अभ्यधा वत तां देवीं दैत्यानामधिपेश्वरः
verses.transliteration: tataH khaDgamupAdAya shatachandraM cha bhAnumat | abhyadhA vata tAM devIM daityAnAmadhipeshvaraH
verses.translation: Next the supreme monarch of the Daityas, seizing his scymitar and sunlike shield, on which a hundred moons were pourtrayed, rushed at the goddess at that moment.
verses.wordMeaning: Next the supreme monarch of the Daityas, seizing his scymitar and sunlike shield, on which a hundred moons were pourtrayed, rushed at the goddess at that moment.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Next the supreme monarch of the Daityas, seizing his scymitar and sunlike shield, on which a hundred moons were pourtrayed, rushed at the goddess at that moment.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Next the supreme monarch of the Daityas, seizing his scymitar and sunlike shield, on which a hundred moons were pourtrayed, rushed at the goddess at that moment.

verses.sanskrit: तस्यापतत एवाशु खड्गं चिच्छेद चण्डिका । धनुर्मुक्तैः शितैर्बाणैश्चर्म चार्ककरामलम् । अश्वांश्च पातयामास रथं सारथिना सह
verses.transliteration: tasyApatata evAshu khaDgaM chichCheda chaNDikA | dhanurmuktaiH shitairbANaishcharma chArkakarAmalam | ashvAMshcha pAtayAmAsa rathaM sArathinA saha
verses.translation: Just as he was falling upon her, Chandika hastily split his scymitar with sharp arrows shot from her bow, and his shield also which was spotless as the sun's rays; and she felled his steeds, and his chariot together with its charioteer.
verses.wordMeaning: Just as he was falling upon her, Chandika hastily split his scymitar with sharp arrows shot from her bow, and his shield also which was spotless as the sun's rays; and she felled his steeds, and his chariot together with its charioteer.

verses.sanskrit: हताश्वः स तदा दैत्यश्छिन्नधन्वा विसारथिः । जग्राह मुद्गरं घोरमम्बिकानिधनोद्यतः
verses.transliteration: hatAshvaH sa tadA daityashChinnadhanvA visArathiH | jagrAha mudgaraM ghoramambikAnidhanodyataH
verses.translation: With his steeds slain, with his bow split, without a charioteer, the Daitya then grasped his terrible mace, being ready to slay Ambika.
verses.wordMeaning: With his steeds slain, with his bow split, without a charioteer, the Daitya then grasped his terrible mace, being ready to slay Ambika.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): With his steeds slain, with his bow split, without a charioteer, the Daitya then grasped his terrible mace, being ready to slay Ambika.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): With his steeds slain, with his bow split, without a charioteer, the Daitya then grasped his terrible mace, being ready to slay Ambika.

verses.sanskrit: चिच्छेदापततस्तस्य मुद्गरं निशितैः शरैः । तथापि सोऽभ्यधावत्तां मुष्टिमुद्यम्य वेगवान्
verses.transliteration: chichChedApatatastasya mudgaraM nishitaiH sharaiH | tathApi so.abhyadhAvattAM muShTimudyamya vegavAn
verses.translation: As he was falling upon her, she clove his mace with sharp arrows; nevertheless, raising his fist, he rushed swiftly at her.
verses.wordMeaning: As he was falling upon her, she clove his mace with sharp arrows; nevertheless, raising his fist, he rushed swiftly at her.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): As he was falling upon her, she clove his mace with sharp arrows; nevertheless, raising his fist, he rushed swiftly at her.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): As he was falling upon her, she clove his mace with sharp arrows; nevertheless, raising his fist, he rushed swiftly at her.

verses.sanskrit: स मुष्टिं पातयामास हृदये दैत्यपुङ्गवः । देव्यास्तं चापि सा देवी तलेनोरस्यताडयत्
verses.transliteration: sa muShTiM pAtayAmAsa hR^idaye daityapu~NgavaH | devyAstaM chApi sA devI talenorasyatADayat
verses.translation: The lordly Daitya brought his fist down on the goddess' heart, and the goddess also smote him on his breast with her palm.
verses.wordMeaning: The lordly Daitya brought his fist down on the goddess' heart, and the goddess also smote him on his breast with her palm.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The lordly Daitya brought his fist down on the goddess' heart, and the goddess also smote him on his breast with her palm.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The lordly Daitya brought his fist down on the goddess' heart, and the goddess also smote him on his breast with her palm.

verses.sanskrit: तलप्रहाराभिहतो निपपात महीतले । स दैत्यराजः सहसा पुनरेव तथोत्थितः
verses.transliteration: talaprahArAbhihato nipapAta mahItale | sa daityarAjaH sahasA punareva tathotthitaH
verses.translation: Wounded by the blow of her palm, the Daitya king fell suddenly on the earth; and again indeed he rose up,
verses.wordMeaning: Wounded by the blow of her palm, the Daitya king fell suddenly on the earth; and again indeed he rose up,
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Wounded by the blow of her palm, the Daitya king fell suddenly on the earth; and again indeed he rose up,
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Wounded by the blow of her palm, the Daitya king fell suddenly on the earth; and again indeed he rose up,

verses.sanskrit: उत्पत्य च प्रगृह्योच्चैर्देवीं गगनमास्थितः । तत्रापि सा निराधारा युयुधे तेन चण्डिका
verses.transliteration: utpatya cha pragR^ihyochchairdevIM gaganamAsthitaH | tatrApi sA nirAdhArA yuyudhe tena chaNDikA
verses.translation: and springing upward he seized the goddess and mounted on high into the sky. There also Chandika, being without any support, fought with him.
verses.wordMeaning: and springing upward he seized the goddess and mounted on high into the sky. There also Chandika, being without any support, fought with him.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and springing upward he seized the goddess and mounted on high into the sky. There also Chandika, being without any support, fought with him.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): and springing upward he seized the goddess and mounted on high into the sky. There also Chandika, being without any support, fought with him.

verses.sanskrit: नियुद्धं खे तदा दैत्यश्चण्डिका च परस्परम् । चक्रतुः प्रथमं सिद्धमुनिविस्मयकारकम्
verses.transliteration: niyuddhaM khe tadA daityashchaNDikA cha parasparam | chakratuH prathamaM siddhamunivismayakArakam
verses.translation: The Daitya and Chandika then fought at first with each other in the sky in a close combat, which wrought dismay among the Siddhas and munis;
verses.wordMeaning: The Daitya and Chandika then fought at first with each other in the sky in a close combat, which wrought dismay among the Siddhas and munis;
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The Daitya and Chandika then fought at first with each other in the sky in a close combat, which wrought dismay among the Siddhas and munis;
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): The Daitya and Chandika then fought at first with each other in the sky in a close combat, which wrought dismay among the Siddhas and munis;

verses.sanskrit: ततो नियुद्धं सुचिरं कृत्वा तेनाम्बिका सह । उत्पाट्य भ्रामयामास चिक्षेप धरणीतले
verses.transliteration: tato niyuddhaM suchiraM kR^itvA tenAmbikA saha | utpATya bhrAmayAmAsa chikShepa dharaNItale
verses.translation: after carrying on the close combat for a very long time with him, Ambika lifted him up then and whirled him around and flung him on the earth.
verses.wordMeaning: after carrying on the close combat for a very long time with him, Ambika lifted him up then and whirled him around and flung him on the earth.
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): after carrying on the close combat for a very long time with him, Ambika lifted him up then and whirled him around and flung him on the earth.
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): after carrying on the close combat for a very long time with him, Ambika lifted him up then and whirled him around and flung him on the earth.

verses.sanskrit: स क्षिप्तो धरणीं प्राप्य मुष्टिमुद्यम्य वेगवान् । अभ्यधावत दुष्टात्मा चण्डिकानिधनेच्छया
verses.transliteration: sa kShipto dharaNIM prApya muShTimudyamya vegavAn | abhyadhAvata duShTAtmA chaNDikAnidhanechChayA
verses.translation: When flung thus he touched the earth, he raised his fist hastily and rushed, evil of soul as he was, with the wish to kill Chandika.
verses.wordMeaning: When flung thus he touched the earth, he raised his fist hastily and rushed, evil of soul as he was, with the wish to kill Chandika.

verses.translation: Seeing him, the lord of all the Daitya folk, approaching, the goddess then pierced him in the breast with a dart and felled him down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit: ततो देवगणाः सर्वे हर्षनिर्भरमानसाः । बभूवुर्निहते तस्मिन् गन्धर्वा ललितं जगुः
verses.transliteration: tato devagaNAH sarve harShanirbharamAnasAH | babhUvurnihate tasmin gandharvA lalitaM jaguH
verses.translation: All the bands of gods then grew exceedingly joyful in mind, when he was slain; the Gandharvas sang out sweetly,
verses.hindi: इस जगत में केवल मैं ही हूँ — मेरे अतिरिक्त दूसरा कौन है? हे दुष्ट! देख, ये मेरी सभी शक्तियाँ मुझमें ही समा रही हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: The Devi's final, definitive statement before slaying Shumbha: "I alone exist." This is not arrogance — it is the highest metaphysics. All the forms that emerged to fight — Kali, the Matrikas, all the manifestations — now dissolve back into the one Devi. Multiplicity returns to unity. The many faces were always one face. Shumbha, who believed in his own separate sovereignty, is about to meet the one reality from which nothing is ultimately separate.
verses.explanation: The Devi's final, definitive statement before slaying Shumbha: "I alone exist." This is not arrogance — it is the highest metaphysics. All the forms that emerged to fight — Kali, the Matrikas, all the manifestations — now dissolve back into the one Devi. Multiplicity returns to unity. The many faces were always one face. verses.science: Physics of field unification: all the apparently distinct forces of nature — the strong and weak nuclear forces, electromagnetism, gravity — are theorised to be manifestations of a single underlying field that differentiated as the universe cooled. The Devi's "I alone exist" and the re-absorption of all her powers is the mythological image of field unification: the many resolving into the one ground from which they arose.
verses.lifeLesson: The final teaching of Chapter 10: everything that appears separate — your many selves, your conflicting desires, your different roles, the parts of you that fight each other — is ultimately one awareness. When you are most fragmented, remember: the same Devi who sent forth all these forms can call them home. You are not your fragments; you are the one who sent them forth. Rest in that.

verses.sanskrit: देवि प्रपन्नार्तिहरे प्रसीद प्रसीद मातर्जगतोऽखिलस्य । प्रसीद विश्वेश्वरि पाहि विश्वं त्वमीश्वरी देवि चराचरस्य
verses.transliteration: devi prapannArtihare prasIda prasIda mAtarjagato.akhilasya | prasIda vishveshvari pAhi vishvaM tvamIshvarI devi charAcharasya
verses.translation: O goddess, who removest the sufferings of thy suppliants, be gracious! Be gracious, O mother of the whole world! Be gracious, O queen of the universe; safeguard the universe! Thou, O goddess, art queen of all that is moveable and immoveable!
verses.hindi: इस प्रकार जब-जब भी दैत्यों से उत्पन्न बाधा होगी, तब-तब मैं अवतरित होकर शत्रुओं का संहार करूँगी।
verses.wordMeaning: The Devi makes the same promise as Krishna in the Bhagavad Gita (Chapter 4) — repeated manifestation to restore balance when evil overwhelms good. The feminine version of this promise is distinctive: it is not the warrior-king archetype but the protective mother who descends when her children are threatened. The Shakta tradition understands the divine not as distant justice but as immediate, maternal protection.
verses.explanation: The Devi makes the same promise as Krishna in the Bhagavad Gita (Chapter 4) — repeated manifestation to restore balance when evil overwhelms good. The feminine version of this promise is distinctive: it is not the warrior-king archetype but the protective mother who descends when her children are threatened. verses.science: Systems theory and homeostasis: all living systems have built-in self-correcting mechanisms. When a system is overwhelmed by disorder (the "asura" principle), corrective forces (the "devi" principle) naturally emerge to restore balance. This is not metaphysics — it is the fundamental operating principle of biological systems from cells to ecosystems. The Goddess's promise is a mythological description of the universe's self-healing capacity.
verses.lifeLesson: Whenever the "demons" in your life — fear, addiction, destructive patterns, toxic relationships — seem overwhelming, remember the Devi's promise: the power to restore balance is inherent in existence itself. You are not alone in the fight. Something within you and within life itself is on the side of your healing and wholeness.

verses.translation: Thou alone hast become the support of the world, because thou dost subsist in the form of the earth! By thee, who existest in the form of water, all this universe is filled, O thou inviolable in thy valour!

verses.sanskrit: विद्याः समस्तास्तव देवि भेदाः स्त्रियः समस्ताः सकला जगत्सु । त्वयैकया पूरितमम्बयैतत् का ते स्तुतिः स्तव्यपरापरोक्तिः
verses.transliteration: vidyAH samastAstava devi bhedAH striyaH samastAH sakalA jagatsu | tvayaikayA pUritamambayaitat kA te stutiH stavyaparAparoktiH
verses.translation: All sciences are portions of thee, O goddess; so are all females without exception in the worlds! By thee alone, as mother, this world has been filled! What praise can there be for thee? Thou art beyond praise, the sublimest expression!
verses.hindi: जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में शक्ति-रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें बार-बार नमस्कार है। नमस्तस्यै, नमस्तस्यै, नमस्तस्यै, नमो नमः।
verses.wordMeaning: This is the most famous verse of the Durga Saptashati — repeated as a refrain nine times with different attributes: as consciousness, as sleep, as hunger, as memory, as mercy, as matter, as power, as peace, as faith. Each verse declares that the same divine feminine power dwells in all beings in a different form. Nothing in existence is excluded from the presence of the Goddess.
verses.explanation: This is the most famous verse of the Durga Saptashati — repeated as a refrain nine times with different attributes: as consciousness, as sleep, as hunger, as memory, as mercy, as matter, as power, as peace, as faith. verses.science: Physics recognizes that all forces in nature — gravity, electromagnetism, the nuclear forces — are expressions of underlying field symmetries. These forces manifest differently in different contexts but share one mathematical structure. The "Ya Devi" refrain — the same power appearing as consciousness, sleep, hunger, memory — is a mythological description of a universe where one fundamental force (Shakti) expresses itself as all apparent multiplicity.
verses.lifeLesson: The next time you feel hungry, tired, curious, loving, or afraid — pause. The same shakti that moves the stars is moving through you right now in this form. Recognizing the divine in the most ordinary experiences — appetite, sleep, longing, fear — is the highest and most accessible form of worship.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वभूता यदा देवी भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायिनी । त्वं स्तुता स्तुतये का वा भवन्तु परमोक्तयः

verses.translation: When as being the goddess who constitutes every created thing, and who bestows enjoyment and final emancipation, thou art praised—for thy praise again what sublime words can be sufficient?

verses.sanskrit: सृष्टिस्थितिविनाशानां शक्तिभूते सनातनि । गुणाश्रये गुणमये नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: sR^iShTisthitivinAshAnAM shaktibhUte sanAtani | guNAshraye guNamaye nArAyaNi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O eternal goddess, who constitutest the energy of creation, permanence and destruction, O thou abode of good qualities, who consistest of good qualities, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O eternal goddess, who constitutest the energy of creation, permanence and destruction, O thou abode of good qualities, who consistest of good qualities, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: शरणागतदीनार्तपरित्राणपरायणे । सर्वस्यार्तिहरे देवि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: sharaNAgatadInArtaparitrANaparAyaNe | sarvasyArtihare devi nArAyaNi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O thou who art devoted to the deliverance of the distressed and afflicted that seek refuge in thee, O goddess who takest away the affliction of all, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O thou who art devoted to the deliverance of the distressed and afflicted that seek refuge in thee, O goddess who takest away the affliction of all, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: हंसयुक्तविमानस्थे ब्रह्माणीरूपधारिणि । कौशाम्भःक्षरिके देवि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: haMsayuktavimAnasthe brahmANIrUpadhAriNi | kaushAmbhaHkSharike devi nArAyaNi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O thou who ridest in a heavenly car yoked with swans, who assumest the form of Brahmani, O goddess who sprinklest kusha-grass-steeped water, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O thou who ridest in a heavenly car yoked with swans, who assumest the form of Brahmani, O goddess who sprinklest kusha-grass-steeped water, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: त्रिशूलचन्द्राहिधरे महावृषभवाहिनि । माहेश्वरीस्वरूपेण नारायणि नमोऽस्तुते
verses.transliteration: trishUlachandrAhidhare mahAvR^iShabhavAhini | mAheshvarIsvarUpeNa nArAyaNi namo.astute
verses.translation: O thou who holdest a trident, the moon and a serpent, who art borne on a huge bull, with the natural character of Maheshvari, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O thou who holdest a trident, the moon and a serpent, who art borne on a huge bull, with the natural character of Maheshvari, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: मयूरकुक्कुटवृते महाशक्तिधरेऽनघे । कौमारीरूपसंस्थाने नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: mayUrakukkuTavR^ite mahAshaktidhare.anaghe | kaumArIrUpasaMsthAne nArAyaNi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O thou who art attended by the peacock and cock, who bearest a great spear, O sinless one; O thou who takest thy station in Kaumari's form, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O thou who art attended by the peacock and cock, who bearest a great spear, O sinless one; O thou who takest thy station in Kaumari's form, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गगृहीतपरमायुधे । प्रसीद वैष्णवीरूपे नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: sha~NkhachakragadAshAr~NgagR^ihItaparamAyudhe | prasIda vaiShNavIrUpe nArAyaNi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O thou who holdest as thy finest weapons a conch, discus, club, and the bow Sharnga, be gracious, O thou who hast Vaishnavi's form; O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O thou who holdest as thy finest weapons a conch, discus, club, and the bow Sharnga, be gracious, O thou who hast Vaishnavi's form; O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: गृहीतोग्रमहाचक्रे दंष्ट्रोद्धृतवसुन्धरे । वराहरूपिणि शिवे नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: gR^ihItogramahAchakre daMShTroddhR^itavasundhare | varAharUpiNi shive nArAyaNi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O thou who graspest a huge formidable discus, who hast uplifted the earth with thy tushes, O auspicious one, who hast a boar-like form, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O thou who graspest a huge formidable discus, who hast uplifted the earth with thy tushes, O auspicious one, who hast a boar-like form, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: नृसिंहरूपेणोग्रेण हन्तुं दैत्यान् कृतोद्यमे । त्रैलोक्यत्राणसहिते नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: nR^isiMharUpeNogreNa hantuM daityAn kR^itodyame | trailokyatrANasahite nArAyaNi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O thou who in the fierce man-lion form didst put forth thy efforts to slay the Daityas, O thou who art connected with the deliverance of the three worlds, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O thou who in the fierce man-lion form didst put forth thy efforts to slay the Daityas, O thou who art connected with the deliverance of the three worlds, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: किरीटिनि महावज्रे सहस्रनयनोज्ज्वले । वृत्रप्राणहरे चैन्द्रि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: kirITini mahAvajre sahasranayanojjvale | vR^itraprANahare chaindri nArAyaNi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O thou who hast a diadem and a great thunderbolt, who art dazzling with a thousand eyes, and who tookest away Vritra's life-breath, O Aindri, Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O thou who hast a diadem and a great thunderbolt, who art dazzling with a thousand eyes, and who tookest away Vritra's life-breath, O Aindri, Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: शिवदूतीस्वरूपेण हतदैत्यमहाबले । घोररूपे महारावे नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: shivadUtIsvarUpeNa hatadaityamahAbale | ghorarUpe mahArAve nArAyaNi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O thou who with the nature of Shivaduti slewest the mighty hosts of the Daityas, O thou of terrible form, of loud shrieks, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O thou who with the nature of Shivaduti slewest the mighty hosts of the Daityas, O thou of terrible form, of loud shrieks, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: दंष्ट्राकरालवदने शिरोमालाविभूषणे । चामुण्डे मुण्डमथने नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: daMShTrAkarAlavadane shiromAlAvibhUShaNe | chAmuNDe muNDamathane nArAyaNi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O thou who hast a face formidable with tushes, who art decorated with a garland of heads, O Chamunda, who grindest shaven heads, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O thou who hast a face formidable with tushes, who art decorated with a garland of heads, O Chamunda, who grindest shaven heads, O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: लक्ष्मि लज्जे महाविद्ये श्रद्धे पुष्टि स्वधे ध्रुवे । महारात्रि महामाये नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: lakShmi lajje mahAvidye shraddhe puShTi svadhe dhruve | mahArAtri mahAmAye nArAyaNi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O Lakshmi, Modesty, Great Knowledge! O Faith, Nourishment, Svadha, Immoveable! O Great Night, Great Illusion! O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O Lakshmi, Modesty, Great Knowledge! O Faith, Nourishment, Svadha, Immoveable! O Great Night, Great Illusion! O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): O Lakshmi, Modesty, Great Knowledge! O Faith, Nourishment, Svadha, Immoveable! O Great Night, Great Illusion! O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): O Lakshmi, Modesty, Great Knowledge! O Faith, Nourishment, Svadha, Immoveable! O Great Night, Great Illusion! O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: मेधे सरस्वति वरे भूति बाभ्रवि तामसि । नियते त्वं प्रसीदेशे नारायणि नमोऽस्तुते
verses.transliteration: medhe sarasvati vare bhUti bAbhravi tAmasi | niyate tvaM prasIdeshe nArAyaNi namo.astute
verses.translation: O Mental Vigour, Sarasvati, Choice One! O Welfare, Wife of Babhru, Dark One! O Self-controlled Queen, be thou gracious! O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O Mental Vigour, Sarasvati, Choice One! O Welfare, Wife of Babhru, Dark One! O Self-controlled Queen, be thou gracious! O Narayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): O Mental Vigour, Sarasvati, Choice One! O Welfare, Wife of Babhru, Dark One! O Self-controlled Queen, be thou gracious! O Narayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: सर्वस्वरूपे सर्वेशे सर्वशक्तिसमन्विते । भयेभ्यस्त्राहि नो देवि दुर्गे देवि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: sarvasvarUpe sarveshe sarvashaktisamanvite | bhayebhyastrAhi no devi durge devi namo.astu te
verses.translation: O thou who hast the nature of all, Queen of all! O thou who possessest the might of all! From terrors save us, O goddess! O goddess Durga, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: O thou who hast the nature of all, Queen of all! O thou who possessest the might of all! From terrors save us, O goddess! O goddess Durga, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: एतत्ते वदनं सौम्यं लोचनत्रयभूषितम् । पातु नः सर्वभूतेभ्यः कात्यायनि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: etatte vadanaM saumyaM lochanatrayabhUShitam | pAtu naH sarvabhUtebhyaH kAtyAyani namo.astu te
verses.translation: Kindly is this thy countenance, which is adorned with three eyes; may it guard us from all created things! O Katyayani, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: Kindly is this thy countenance, which is adorned with three eyes; may it guard us from all created things! O Katyayani, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: ज्वालाकरालमत्युग्रमशेषासुरसूदनम् । त्रिशूलं पातु नो भीतेर्भद्रकालि नमोऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: jvAlAkarAlamatyugramasheShAsurasUdanam | trishUlaM pAtu no bhIterbhadrakAli namo.astu te
verses.translation: Formidable with flames, exceedingly sharp, destroying the Asuras without quarter, may thy trident guard us from fear! O Bhadrakali, reverence be to thee!
verses.wordMeaning: Formidable with flames, exceedingly sharp, destroying the Asuras without quarter, may thy trident guard us from fear! O Bhadrakali, reverence be to thee!
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Formidable with flames, exceedingly sharp, destroying the Asuras without quarter, may thy trident guard us from fear! O Bhadrakali, reverence be to thee!
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Formidable with flames, exceedingly sharp, destroying the Asuras without quarter, may thy trident guard us from fear! O Bhadrakali, reverence be to thee!

verses.sanskrit: हिनस्ति दैत्यतेजांसि स्वनेनापूर्य या जगत् । सा घण्टा पातु नो देवि पापेभ्यो नः सुतानिव
verses.transliteration: hinasti daityatejAMsi svanenApUrya yA jagat | sA ghaNTA pAtu no devi pApebhyo naH sutAniva
verses.translation: Thy bell, that fills the world with its ringing and destroys the glories of the Daityas—may that bell guard us, O goddess, even us like children, from sins!
verses.wordMeaning: Thy bell, that fills the world with its ringing and destroys the glories of the Daityas—may that bell guard us, O goddess, even us like children, from sins!

verses.sanskrit: असुरासृग्वसापङ्कचर्चितस्ते करोज्ज्वलः । शुभाय खड्गो भवतु चण्डिके त्वां नता वयम्
verses.transliteration: asurAsR^igvasApa~Nkacharchitaste karojjvalaH | shubhAya khaDgo bhavatu chaNDike tvAM natA vayam
verses.translation: Besmirched with the blood and fat of the Asuras as with mire, gleaming with rays in thy hand—may thy scymitar be for our welfare! O Chandika, to thee we bow!
verses.wordMeaning: Besmirched with the blood and fat of the Asuras as with mire, gleaming with rays in thy hand—may thy scymitar be for our welfare! O Chandika, to thee we bow!
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Besmirched with the blood and fat of the Asuras as with mire, gleaming with rays in thy hand—may thy scymitar be for our welfare! O Chandika, to thee we bow!

verses.sanskrit: रोगानशेषानपहंसि तुष्टा रुष्टा तु कामान् सकलानभीष्टान् । त्वामाश्रितानां न विपन्नराणां त्वामाश्रिता ह्याश्रयतां प्रयान्ति
verses.transliteration: rogAnasheShAnapahaMsi tuShTA ruShTA tu kAmAn sakalAnabhIShTAn | tvAmAshritAnAM na vipannarANAM tvAmAshritA hyAshrayatAM prayAnti
verses.translation: Thou destroyest all sicknesses, when gratified; but when wrathful, destroyest all longed-for desires. No calamity befalls men who have sought unto thee! They who have sought unto thee become verily a refuge themselves!
verses.wordMeaning: Thou destroyest all sicknesses, when gratified; but when wrathful, destroyest all longed-for desires. No calamity befalls men who have sought unto thee! They who have sought unto thee become verily a refuge themselves!
verses.commentary: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Thou destroyest all sicknesses, when gratified; but when wrathful, destroyest all longed-for desires. No calamity befalls men who have sought unto thee! They who have sought unto thee become verily a refuge themselves!
verses.explanation: Plain sense of this Devi Mahatmyam verse (F.E. Pargiter, public domain): Thou destroyest all sicknesses, when gratified; but when wrathful, destroyest all longed-for desires. No calamity befalls men who have sought unto thee! They who have sought unto thee become verily a refuge themselves!

verses.sanskrit: एतत्कृतं यत्कदनं त्वयाद्य धर्मद्विषां देवि महासुराणाम् । रूपैरनेकैर्बहुधात्ममूर्तिं कृत्वाम्बिके तत्प्रकरोति कान्या
verses.transliteration: etatkR^itaM yatkadanaM tvayAdya dharmadviShAM devi mahAsurANAm | rUpairanekairbahudhAtmamUrtiM kR^itvAmbike tatprakaroti kAnyA
verses.translation: This slaughter that thou hast now wrought on the great Asuras who hate righteousness, O goddess, by multiplying thy body in many forms—O Ambika, what other goddess achieves that?
verses.wordMeaning: This slaughter that thou hast now wrought on the great Asuras who hate righteousness, O goddess, by multiplying thy body in many forms—O Ambika, what other goddess achieves that?

verses.sanskrit: विद्यासु शास्त्रेषु विवेकदीपे- ष्वाद्येषु वाक्येषु च का त्वदन्या । ममत्वगर्तेऽतिमहान्धकारे विभ्रामयत्येतदतीव विश्वम्
verses.transliteration: vidyAsu shAstreShu vivekadIpe\- ShvAdyeShu vAkyeShu cha kA tvadanyA | mamatvagarte.atimahAndhakAre vibhrAmayatyetadatIva vishvam
verses.translation: In the sciences, in the scriptures, which need the lamp of discrimination, and in the ancient sayings, who but thou, within the pit of selfishness, wherein is exceeding great darkness, causes this universe to whirl about most grievously?

verses.sanskrit: रक्षांसि यत्रोग्रविषाश्च नागा यत्रारयो दस्युबलानि यत्र । दावानलो यत्र तथाब्धिमध्ये तत्र स्थिता त्वं परिपासि विश्वम्
verses.transliteration: rakShAMsi yatrograviShAshcha nAgA yatrArayo dasyubalAni yatra | dAvAnalo yatra tathAbdhimadhye tatra sthitA tvaM paripAsi vishvam
verses.translation: Wherever dwell Rakshasas and virulently-poisonous Nagas, wherever foes exist, wherever the powers of the Dasyus, and where flaming fire appears amid the ocean, there abiding thou dost safeguard the universe!
verses.wordMeaning: Wherever dwell Rakshasas and virulently-poisonous Nagas, wherever foes exist, wherever the powers of the Dasyus, and where flaming fire appears amid the ocean, there abiding thou dost safeguard the universe!

verses.sanskrit: विश्वेश्वरि त्वं परिपासि विश्वं विश्वात्मिका धारयसीह विश्वम् । विश्वेशवन्द्या भवती भवन्ति विश्वाश्रया ये त्वयि भक्तिनम्राः
verses.transliteration: vishveshvari tvaM paripAsi vishvaM vishvAtmikA dhArayasIha vishvam | vishveshavandyA bhavatI bhavanti vishvAshrayA ye tvayi bhaktinamrAH
verses.translation: O queen of the universe, thou safeguardest the universe! Thou hast the nature of the universe, for thou upholdest the universe. Thou art the lady worthy to be praised by the lord of the universe. They are the refuge of the universe, who bow in faith before thee!

verses.sanskrit: देवि प्रसीद परिपालय नोऽरिभीते- र्नित्यं यथासुरवधादधुनैव सद्यः । पापानि सर्वजगतां प्रशमं नयाशु उत्पातपाकजनितांश्च महोपसर्गान्
verses.transliteration: devi prasIda paripAlaya no.aribhIte\- rnityaM yathAsuravadhAdadhunaiva sadyaH | pApAni sarvajagatAM prashamaM nayAshu utpAtapAkajanitAMshcha mahopasargAn
verses.translation: O goddess, be gracious! Protect us wholly from fear of our foes perpetually, as thou hast at this very time saved us promptly by the slaughter of the Asuras! And bring thou quickly to rest the sins of all the worlds and the great calamities which have sprung from the maturing of portents!

verses.sanskrit: प्रणतानां प्रसीद त्वं देवि विश्वार्तिहारिणि । त्रैलोक्यवासिनामीड्ये लोकानां वरदा भव
verses.transliteration: praNatAnAM prasIda tvaM devi vishvArtihAriNi | trailokyavAsinAmIDye lokAnAM varadA bhava
verses.translation: To us who are prostrate be thou gracious, O goddess, who takest away affliction from the universe! O thou worthy of praise from the dwellers in the three worlds, bestow thou boons on the worlds!
verses.wordMeaning: To us who are prostrate be thou gracious, O goddess, who takest away affliction from the universe! O thou worthy of praise from the dwellers in the three worlds, bestow thou boons on the worlds!

verses.sanskrit: वरदाहं सुरगणा वरं यन्मनसेच्छथ । तं वृणुध्वं प्रयच्छामि जगतामुपकारकम्
verses.transliteration: varadAhaM suragaNA varaM yanmanasechChatha | taM vR^iNudhvaM prayachChAmi jagatAmupakArakam
verses.translation: I am ready to bestow a boon. O ye hosts of gods, choose whatever boon ye desire in your mind; I grant it as a thing that benefits the worlds.
verses.wordMeaning: I am ready to bestow a boon. O ye hosts of gods, choose whatever boon ye desire in your mind; I grant it as a thing that benefits the worlds.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वाबाधाप्रशमनं त्रैलोक्यस्याखिलेश्वरि । एवमेव त्वया कार्यमस्मद्वैरिविनाशनम्
verses.transliteration: sarvAbAdhAprashamanaM trailokyasyAkhileshvari | evameva tvayA kAryamasmadvairivinAshanam
verses.translation: O queen of all, complete thou thus indeed the pacification of every trouble of the three worlds, and the destruction of our enemies.

verses.sanskrit: वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे प्राप्ते अष्टाविंशतिमे युगे । शुम्भो निशुम्भश्चैवान्यावुत्पत्स्येते महासुरौ
verses.transliteration: vaivasvate.antare prApte aShTAviMshatime yuge | shumbho nishumbhashchaivAnyAvutpatsyete mahAsurau
verses.translation: When the twenty-eighth age has arrived, in the Vaivasvata Manvantara, two other great Asuras shall be born, Shumbha and Nishumbha.
verses.wordMeaning: When the twenty-eighth age has arrived, in the Vaivasvata Manvantara, two other great Asuras shall be born, Shumbha and Nishumbha.

verses.transliteration: nandagopagR^ihe jAtA yashodAgarbhasambhavA | tatastau nAshayiShyAmi vindhyAchalanivAsinI
verses.translation: Then, born as the offspring of Yashoda's womb in the cowherd Nanda's house, and dwelling on the Vindhya mountains, I will destroy them both.

verses.transliteration: punarapyatiraudreNa rUpeNa pR^ithivItale | avatIrya haniShyAmi vaiprachittAMshcha dAnavAn
verses.translation: And again, becoming incarnate in a very terrible form on the face of the earth, I will slay the Vaiprachitta Danavas;

verses.transliteration: bhakShayantyAshcha tAnugrAn vaiprachittAn mahAsurAn | raktA dantA bhaviShyanti dADimIkusumopamAH
verses.translation: and when I devour those fierce and great Vaiprachitta Asuras, my teeth shall become red like the flowers of the pomegranate.
verses.wordMeaning: and when I devour those fierce and great Vaiprachitta Asuras, my teeth shall become red like the flowers of the pomegranate.

verses.sanskrit: ततो मां देवताः स्वर्गे मर्त्यलोके च मानवाः । स्तुवन्तो व्याहरिष्यन्ति सततं रक्तदन्तिकाम्
verses.transliteration: tato mAM devatAH svarge martyaloke cha mAnavAH | stuvanto vyAhariShyanti satataM raktadantikAm
verses.translation: Hence the gods in Svarga and men in the world of mortals, praising me, shall always talk of me as 'Red-toothed' (Raktadantika).
verses.wordMeaning: Hence the gods in Svarga and men in the world of mortals, praising me, shall always talk of me as 'Red-toothed' (Raktadantika).

verses.sanskrit: भूयश्च शतवार्षिक्यामनावृष्ट्यामनम्भसि । मुनिभिः संस्मृता भूमौ सम्भविष्याम्ययोनिजा
verses.transliteration: bhUyashcha shatavArShikyAmanAvR^iShTyAmanambhasi | munibhiH saMsmR^itA bhUmau sambhaviShyAmyayonijA
verses.translation: And again, after a period of a hundred years during which no rain and water shall fall, praised by the munis I shall be born, but not womb-begotten, on the earth.
verses.wordMeaning: And again, after a period of a hundred years during which no rain and water shall fall, praised by the munis I shall be born, but not womb-begotten, on the earth.

verses.transliteration: tataH shatena netrANAM nirIkShiShyAmyahaM munIn | kIrtayiShyanti manujAH shatAkShImiti mAM tataH
verses.translation: Then, because I shall behold the munis with a hundred eyes, mankind shall therefore celebrate me as 'Hundred-eyed' (Shatakshi).

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽहमखिलं लोकमात्मदेहसमुद्भवैः । भरिष्यामि सुराः शाकैरावृष्टेः प्राणधारकैः
verses.transliteration: tato.ahamakhilaM lokamAtmadehasamudbhavaiH | bhariShyAmi surAH shAkairAvR^iShTeH prANadhArakaiH
verses.translation: Next, O ye gods, I shall support the whole world with the life-sustaining vegetables, which shall grow out of my own body, during a period of heavy rain.

verses.transliteration: shAkambharIti vikhyAtiM tadA yAsyAmyahaM bhuvi | tatraiva cha vadhiShyAmi durgamAkhyaM mahAsuram
verses.translation: I shall gain fame on the earth then as Shakambhari; and in that very period I shall slay the great Asura named Durgama.

verses.transliteration: bhImAdevIti vikhyAtaM tanme nAma bhaviShyati | yadAruNAkhyastrailokye mahAbAdhAM kariShyati

verses.sanskrit: शरत्काले महापूजा क्रियते या च वार्षिकी । तस्यां ममैतन्माहात्म्यं श्रुत्वा भक्तिसमन्वितः

verses.translation: And at the great annual worship that is performed in autumn time, the man who listens filled with faith to this poem of my majesty
verses.hindi: दुष्कर्मियों के विनाश के लिए, जनहित की कामना से, और धर्म की स्थापना के लिए — मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होती हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The Devi's own version of the Gita's great promise — with a distinctive feminine emphasis: "hitakāmyayā" — out of the desire for the welfare and good of beings. The Goddess does not descend primarily as judge or warrior; she descends out of love, out of the wish for beings to be well. Every fierce manifestation of the Devi — every battle in the Saptashati — is therefore an act of motherly care, not punishment. The entire scripture is a love story disguised as a war story.
verses.explanation: The Devi's own version of the Gita's great promise — with a distinctive feminine emphasis: "hitakāmyayā" — out of the desire for the welfare and good of beings. The Goddess does not descend primarily as judge or warrior; she descends out of love, out of the wish for beings to be well. Every fierce manifestation of the Devi — every battle in the Saptashati — is therefore an act of motherly care, not punishment. The entire scripture is a love story disguised as a war story.
verses.science: Self-determination theory (Deci & Ryan): actions motivated by genuine care for others ("benevolence" motivation) produce the most sustained, intrinsically energised, and effective outcomes. The Devi's "hitakāmyayā" is the optimal motivational state — intrinsic, caring, freely given. Research confirms: people who act from genuine care rather than obligation, fear, or ego produce better results and sustain effort far longer.
verses.lifeLesson: Why do you do what you do? Strip away the external reasons — the money, the approval, the obligation. What remains? If genuine care for others' wellbeing is somewhere in the bedrock, you have access to the Devi's inexhaustible energy. If it is absent, all effort will eventually exhaust you. Today, reconnect to the care underneath your actions. That care is the Goddess.
verses.commentary: The Devi's own version of the Gita's great promise — with a distinctive feminine emphasis: "hitakāmyayā" — out of the desire for the welfare and good of beings. Every fierce manifestation of the Devi — every battle in the Saptashati — is therefore an act of motherly care, not punishment. The entire scripture is a love story disguised as a war story.

verses.transliteration: viprANAM bhojanairhomaiH prokShaNIyairaharnisham | anyaishcha vividhairbhogaiH pradAnairvatsareNa yA

verses.transliteration: prItirme kriyate sAsmin sakR^iduchcharite shrute | shrutaM harati pApAni tathArogyaM prayachChati
verses.translation: the favour which comes by such means, such favour is won from me when this story of my noble exploits is once heard. When heard, it takes away sins and confers perfect health.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिञ्छ्रुते वैरिकृतं भयं पुंसां न जायते । युष्माभिः स्तुतयो याश्च याश्च ब्रह्मर्षिभिः कृताः

verses.translation: and those composed by Brahma, bestow a splendid mind. He who is surrounded by a raging fire in a forest or on a lonesome road,

verses.transliteration: dasyubhirvA vR^itaH shUnye gR^ihIto vApi shatrubhiH | siMhavyAghrAnuyAto vA vane vA vanahastibhiH
verses.translation: or who is encompassed by robbers in a desolate spot, or who is captured by enemies, or who is prowled after by a lion or tiger or by wild elephants in a forest,

verses.sanskrit: राज्ञा क्रुद्धेन चाज्ञप्तो वध्यो बन्धगतोऽपि वा । आघूर्णितो वा वातेन स्थितः पोते महार्णवे
verses.transliteration: rAj~nA kruddhena chAj~napto vadhyo bandhagato.api vA | AghUrNito vA vAtena sthitaH pote mahArNave

verses.sanskrit: पतत्सु चापि शस्त्रेषु सङ्ग्रामे भृशदारुणे । सर्वाबाधासु घोरासु वेदनाभ्यर्दितोऽपि वा

verses.sanskrit: स्मरन् ममैतच्चरितं नरो मुच्येत सङ्कटात् । मम प्रभावात्सिंहाद्या दस्यवो वैरिणस्तथा
verses.transliteration: smaran mamaitachcharitaM naro muchyeta sa~NkaTAt | mama prabhAvAtsiMhAdyA dasyavo vairiNastathA
verses.translation: such a man, on calling to mind this story of my exploits, is delivered from his strait. Through my power lions and other dangerous beasts, robbers and enemies,

verses.transliteration: dUrAdeva palAyante smaratashcharitaM mama

verses.transliteration: ityuktvA sA bhagavatI chaNDikA chaNDavikramA

verses.transliteration: pashyatAM sarvadevAnAM tatraivAntaradhIyata | te.api devA nirAta~NkAH svAdhikArAnyathA purA
verses.translation: vanished there, while the gods were gazing indeed on her. The gods also, relieved from fear, their foes being slain, all resumed their own dominions as before,

verses.transliteration: yaj~nabhAgabhujaH sarve chakrurvinihatArayaH | daityAshcha devyA nihate shumbhe devaripau yudhi

verses.sanskrit: जगद्विध्वंसके तस्मिन् महोग्रेऽतुलविक्रमे । निशुम्भे च महावीर्ये शेषाः पातालमाययुः
verses.transliteration: jagadvidhvaMsake tasmin mahogre.atulavikrame | nishumbhe cha mahAvIrye sheShAH pAtAlamAyayuH
verses.translation: he who brought ruin on the world and who was peerless in prowess, and when Nishumbha also, great in valour, was slain—the rest all came to Patala.

verses.sanskrit: एवं भगवती देवी सा नित्यापि पुनः पुनः । सम्भूय कुरुते भूप जगतः परिपालनम्
verses.transliteration: evaM bhagavatI devI sA nityApi punaH punaH | sambhUya kurute bhUpa jagataH paripAlanam
verses.translation: Thus that adorable goddess, although everlasting, yet taking birth again and again, accomplishes the safeguarding of the world, O king.
verses.wordMeaning: Thus that adorable goddess, although everlasting, yet taking birth again and again, accomplishes the safeguarding of the world, O king.

verses.sanskrit: तयैतन्मोह्यते विश्वं सैव विश्वं प्रसूयते । सा याचिता च विज्ञानं तुष्टा ऋद्धिं प्रयच्छति
verses.transliteration: tayaitanmohyate vishvaM saiva vishvaM prasUyate | sA yAchitA cha vij~nAnaM tuShTA R^iddhiM prayachChati
verses.translation: By her this universe is bewitched; she verily gives birth to the universe. And when besought, she bestows knowledge; when gratified, she bestows prosperity.
verses.wordMeaning: By her this universe is bewitched; she verily gives birth to the universe. And when besought, she bestows knowledge; when gratified, she bestows prosperity.

verses.sanskrit: व्याप्तं तयैतत्सकलं ब्रह्माण्डं मनुजेश्वर । महादेव्या महाकाली महामारीस्वरूपया
verses.transliteration: vyAptaM tayaitatsakalaM brahmANDaM manujeshvara | mahAdevyA mahAkAlI mahAmArIsvarUpayA
verses.translation: All this egg of Brahma, O king, is pervaded by her, who is Mahakali at Mahakala, and who has the nature of the great destroying goddess Mahamari.
verses.wordMeaning: All this egg of Brahma, O king, is pervaded by her, who is Mahakali at Mahakala, and who has the nature of the great destroying goddess Mahamari.

verses.sanskrit: सैव काले महामारी सैव सृष्टिर्भवत्यजा । स्थितिं करोति भूतानां सैव काले सनातनी
verses.transliteration: saiva kAle mahAmArI saiva sR^iShTirbhavatyajA | sthitiM karoti bhUtAnAM saiva kAle sanAtanI
verses.translation: She indeed is Mahamari at the fated time; she indeed is creation, the Unborn; she indeed, the Eternal, gives stability to created beings at their fated time.
verses.wordMeaning: She indeed is Mahamari at the fated time; she indeed is creation, the Unborn; she indeed, the Eternal, gives stability to created beings at their fated time.

verses.sanskrit: भवकाले नृणां सैव लक्ष्मीर्वृद्धिप्रदा गृहे । सैवाभावे तथालक्ष्मीर्विनाशायोपजायते
verses.transliteration: bhavakAle nR^iNAM saiva lakShmIrvR^iddhipradA gR^ihe | saivAbhAve tathAlakShmIrvinAshAyopajAyate
verses.translation: She indeed is Lakshmi, bestowing prosperity on the houses of men while she abides with them; and she indeed, when she is absent, becomes the goddess of Ill Fortune unto their destruction.

verses.sanskrit: स्तुता सम्पूजिता पुष्पैर्गन्धधूपादिभिस्तथा । ददाति वित्तं पुत्रांश्च मतिं धर्मे गतिं शुभाम्

verses.hindi: हे राजन्! यह सर्वोत्तम देवीमाहात्म्य तुम्हें सुनाया गया। यही शक्ति उस देवी की है, जिसके द्वारा यह जगत धारण किया जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Sage Medhas concludes the entire Saptashati with this verse: the power by which the world is sustained (dharana) is the Devi's power. Not merely the power by which demons are slain — but the continuous sustaining power that holds the universe together from moment to moment. This is the Saptashati's final and deepest teaching: the Goddess is not an episode in cosmic history but the ongoing ground of existence itself.
verses.explanation: Sage Medhas concludes the entire Saptashati with this verse: the power by which the world is sustained (dharana) is the Devi's power. Not merely the power by which demons are slain — but the continuous sustaining power that holds the universe together from moment to moment. This is the Saptashati's final and deepest teaching: the Goddess is not an episode in cosmic history but the ongoing ground of existence itself.
verses.science: Cosmological fine-tuning: the physical constants — the gravitational constant, the mass of the electron, the cosmological constant — are tuned to extraordinary precision to allow complex structures to exist and persist. A change of even fractional amounts in several of these constants would produce a universe where nothing coheres for more than an instant. This "sustaining power" — the fine-tuned coherence of existence — is what the Devi Mahatmyam calls the Goddess. Whatever underlies the continuous coherence of reality is Devi.
verses.lifeLesson: The final verse asks: what holds your life together? Not your willpower or planning — what sustains the ground beneath all of that? The heartbeat continuing without effort, the immune system running silently, the love persisting even when not consciously generated — this sustaining power is the Goddess. You have just heard 13 chapters about her. Now rest. She is carrying this.
